# LISQM: List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics

> A list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics, also called sound quality (SQ) metrics: loudness, sharpness, roughness, fluctuation strength, tonality, impulsiveness and psychoacoustic annoyance. Each implementation is listed under the standard edition or model it follows. All programming languages.

Data as of 2026-10-09. 22 metrics, 39 projects, languages: C, C#, C++, Julia, MATLAB, Octave, Pure Data, Python, Rust. Each implementation is tied to the standard edition or model paper it follows, with its validation evidence as stated by the project. Repository and package metadata are refreshed monthly. Implementations are listed with established projects first, SQAT and MoSQITo (widely used), and sottek-hearing-model (a very good implementation) at the top and in bold. Projects marked (newly released) were first released less than about a year ago and are not yet seen to be widely used in the community; projects marked (legacy) are archived or have had no commit for three years or more.

Developed by Zhenxian LI with assistance from Claude Code.

## Loudness

- [Zwicker loudness (ISO 532-1, DIN 45631)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-zwicker.md): current edition ISO 532-1:2017; implementations: SQAT, MoSQITo, AARAE, MetaSona (newly released), iso532-1-rs (newly released), Kirin Hypha (newly released), Mosqito.NET (newly released), phonometry (newly released), SoundPalette (newly released), ZwickerLoudness.jl (newly released), pySQAT (developing), PsychoacousticParametersMeasurer (legacy)
- [Moore–Glasberg loudness of stationary sounds (ISO 532-2, ANSI S3.4)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg.md): current edition ISO 532-2:2017; implementations: phonometry (newly released)
- [Time-varying loudness, Moore–Glasberg–Schlittenlacher (ISO 532-3)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg-time-varying.md): current edition ISO 532-3:2023; implementations: iso532-3 (tv2018.m), phonometry (newly released)
- [Loudness from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-ecma-418-2.md): current edition ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.); implementations: SQAT (unreleased), sottek-hearing-model, refmap-psychoacoustics, MetaSona (newly released), phonometry (newly released)

## Sharpness

- [Sharpness (DIN 45692, Aures, von Bismarck)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/sharpness.md): current edition DIN 45692:2009; implementations: SQAT, MoSQITo, refmap-psychoacoustics, MetaSona (newly released), Kirin Hypha (newly released), Mosqito.NET (newly released), phonometry (newly released), PsychoacousticMetrics.jl (newly released), SoundPalette (newly released), pySQAT (developing), PsychoacousticParametersMeasurer (legacy)

## Roughness

- [Roughness, Daniel & Weber model](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/roughness-daniel-weber.md): current edition Daniel & Weber (1997); implementations: SQAT, MoSQITo, AARAE, ITA-Toolbox, MetaSona (newly released), Mosqito.NET (newly released), PsychoacousticMetrics.jl (newly released), SoundPalette (newly released), pySQAT (developing), PsySound3 (legacy)
- [Roughness from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/roughness-ecma-418-2.md): current edition ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.); implementations: SQAT (unreleased), sottek-hearing-model, refmap-psychoacoustics, MetaSona (newly released), phonometry (newly released)
- [Roughness, DIN 38455](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/roughness-din-38455.md): current edition DIN 38455:2024; implementations: none found

## Fluctuation strength

- [Fluctuation strength, Osses et al. model and Fastl & Zwicker formula](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/fluctuation-strength-osses.md): current edition Osses et al. (2016); implementations: SQAT, phonometry (newly released), PsychoacousticMetrics.jl (newly released), pySQAT (developing), fluctuation-strength-TUe (legacy)
- [Fluctuation strength from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/fluctuation-strength-ecma-418-2.md): current edition ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.); implementations: SQAT (PR), sottek-hearing-model (unreleased), phonometry (newly released)

## Tonality

- [Tonality, Aures/Terhardt model](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tonality-aures.md): current edition Aures (1985b); implementations: SQAT, MoSQITo (PR), MetaSona (newly released), pySQAT (developing)
- [Tonality from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tonality-ecma-418-2.md): current edition ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.); implementations: SQAT (unreleased), sottek-hearing-model, refmap-psychoacoustics, MetaSona (newly released), phonometry (newly released)
- [Tone-to-noise ratio and prominence ratio (ECMA-418-1)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tone-to-noise-prominence-ratio.md): current edition ECMA-418-1:2024 (3rd ed.); implementations: phonometry (newly released)
- [Tonal components and tone adjustment (DIN 45681)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tonality-din-45681.md): current edition DIN 45681:2005; implementations: none found
- [Audibility of tones in noise (ISO/TS 20065)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tonal-audibility-iso-20065.md): current edition ISO/TS 20065:2022; implementations: none found
- [Tonal audibility in environmental noise (ISO 1996-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tonal-audibility-iso-1996-2.md): current edition ISO 1996-2:2017; implementations: MoSQITo (PR), phonometry (newly released)
- [Tonal audibility of wind turbine noise (IEC 61400-11)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tonal-audibility-iec-61400-11.md): current edition IEC 61400-11:2012+AMD1:2018; implementations: phonometry (newly released)

## Impulsiveness

- [Prominence of impulsive sounds (ISO/PAS 1996-3, NT ACOU 112)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/impulsiveness.md): current edition ISO/PAS 1996-3:2022; implementations: phonometry (newly released)

## Psychoacoustic annoyance

- [Psychoacoustic annoyance (Widmann, Zwicker & Fastl, More, Di et al.)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/psychoacoustic-annoyance.md): current edition Widmann (1992), Zwicker & Fastl (1999), More (2010), and Di et al. (2016); implementations: SQAT, refmap-psychoacoustics, phonometry (newly released), PsychoacousticMetrics.jl (newly released), pySQAT (developing), PsychoacousticParametersMeasurer (legacy)

## Related quantities

- [Equal-loudness-level contours (ISO 226)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/equal-loudness-contours.md): current edition ISO 226:2023; implementations: phonometry (newly released)
- [Perceived noise level, PNLT and EPNL (ICAO Annex 16, 14 CFR Part 36)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/epnl.md): current edition ICAO Annex 16, Vol. I and 14 CFR Part 36; implementations: SQAT, phonometry (newly released), pySQAT (developing), SUAVE (legacy)
- [Aural detectability of sounds in background noise](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/aural-detectability.md): current edition Fidell et al. (1974); implementations: refmap-psychoacoustics

## Projects

- **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.md)**: MATLAB; established, widely used; MATLAB toolbox for sound quality analysis that bundles most psychoacoustic metrics in one place: ISO 532-1 and ECMA-418-2 loudness, DIN 45692 sharpness, Daniel & Weber and ECMA-418-2 roughness, Osses fluctuation strength, Aures and ECMA-418-2 tonality, three psychoacoustic annoyance models (Zwicker & Fastl, which main also provides under its original attribution to Widmann; More; Di et al.) and EPNL.
- **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.md)**: Python; established, widely used; Python library for sound quality metrics: ISO 532-1 loudness, DIN 45692 sharpness, Daniel & Weber roughness, ECMA-418-2 hearing-model loudness (Clause 5) and roughness (2nd edition), tone-to-noise and prominence ratios, and the speech intelligibility index.
- **[sottek-hearing-model](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sottek-hearing-model.md)**: Python; established, a very good implementation; Python implementation of the ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th edition) Sottek Hearing Model metrics: loudness and roughness (with binaural combination), tonality (per channel), and fluctuation strength on the main branch.
- [acoustic-toolbox](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/acoustic-toolbox.md): Python; established; Python acoustics library under the Université Gustave Eiffel GitHub organisation, continuing python-acoustics.
- [AMT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/amt.md): MATLAB, Octave; established; MATLAB/Octave toolbox of auditory models for reproducible research.
- [PSYCHO](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/pd-psycho.md): Pure Data, C; established; Pure Data library of psychoacoustic objects (C externals and abstractions) from the author's research on dissonance models.
- [refmap-psychoacoustics](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/refmap-psychoacoustics.md): MATLAB, Python; established; Research code of the REFMAP project at the University of Salford, in MATLAB with Python ports.
- [AARAE](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/aarae.md): MATLAB; established; Audio and Acoustical Response Analysis Environment: a MATLAB environment with a graphical interface, made to support teaching and research in acoustics.
- [iso532-3 (tv2018.m)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/js2251-iso532-3.md): MATLAB; established; MATLAB code by Brian C. J. Moore, Brian R. Glasberg and Josef Schlittenlacher (Cambridge Hearing Group) for the loudness of time-varying sounds: the model of Moore et al. (2016) with the revised time constants of Moore et al. (2018).
- [ITA-Toolbox](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/ita-toolbox.md): MATLAB; established; MATLAB toolbox for acoustic measurements and signal processing from the Institute of Technical Acoustics, RWTH Aachen University, open source since 2010.
- [PyDSM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/pydsm.md): Python; established; Python toolbox for the design and simulation of delta-sigma modulators.
- [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/metasona.md): C, Python; newly released (not yet seen to be widely used); C library with a typed Python interface and prebuilt wheels, written to make repeated psychoacoustic analysis fast.
- [iso532-1-rs](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/iso532-1-rs.md): Rust, C, Python; newly released (not yet seen to be widely used); Rust engine (README title "ISO532") for ISO 532-1:2017 Zwicker loudness: stationary, time-varying and a streaming interface, with a C ABI and a Python binding (PyO3/maturin).
- [Kirin Hypha](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/kirin-hypha.md): Rust; newly released (not yet seen to be widely used); Free PRE/POST measurement plug-in for mixing and mastering.
- [Mosqito.NET](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito-net.md): C#; newly released (not yet seen to be widely used); C# (.NET 8) port of MoSQITo 1.2.1 with the same metrics: ISO 532-1 loudness, ECMA-418-2 (2nd edition) loudness and roughness, DIN 45692 sharpness, Daniel & Weber roughness, and ECMA-74 tone-to-noise and prominence ratios.
- [NumpyLibforPsychoAcoustic](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/numpylib-psychoacoustic.md): Python; newly released (not yet seen to be widely used); Python (NumPy) adaptation of loudness models from the Auditory Modeling Toolbox (AMT), written as a second-year student project at Mines School of Nancy: the stationary model of Moore, Glasberg & Baer (1997) and the time-varying model of Glasberg & Moore (2002).
- [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.md): Python; newly released (not yet seen to be widely used); Python acoustics library (formerly PyOctaveBand) that added a large psychoacoustics module in July 2026: ISO 532-1, -2 and -3 loudness, ECMA-418-2:2025 loudness, tonality, roughness and fluctuation strength (monaural), DIN 45692 sharpness, Osses fluctuation strength, ECMA-418-1:2024 TNR/PR, tonal audibility, impulsiveness, EPNL and ISO 226:2023.
- [PsychoacousticMetrics.jl](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psychoacousticmetrics-jl.md): Julia; newly released (not yet seen to be widely used); Julia package for the Zwicker family of sound-quality metrics on top of ZwickerLoudness.jl: DIN 45692:2009 sharpness (with Aures, von Bismarck and Fastl weightings), Daniel & Weber roughness, Osses et al. (2016) fluctuation strength and Widmann (1992) psychoacoustic annoyance.
- [SoundPalette](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/soundpalette.md): C++; newly released (not yet seen to be widely used); C++ tool for game audio that analyses a folder of sound effects and draws each file as a glyph in a palette, built as a static library, a command-line tool (including a lint mode for CI) and a desktop app.
- [torch_amt](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/torch-amt.md): Python; newly released (not yet seen to be widely used); PyTorch implementations of models from the MATLAB Auditory Modeling Toolbox (AMT), differentiable and able to run on GPU.
- [ZwickerLoudness.jl](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/zwickerloudness-jl.md): Julia; newly released (not yet seen to be widely used); Julia package that computes ISO 532-1:2017 Zwicker loudness from one-third-octave band levels: the stationary method (clause 5) from 28 band levels and, since v0.3.0, the time-varying method (clause 6) with N5 and N10 from a band-level time series.
- [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/pysqat.md): Python; developing; Python port of the MATLAB toolbox SQAT (README title "SQAT4PY") with a PySide6 graphical interface.
- [LoudnessModel](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/loudnessmodel.md): Python; developing; Python translation of the Cambridge MATLAB code for the TVL2018 loudness model: Moore et al. (2016) with the revised time constants of Moore et al. (2018).
- [deeuu/loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/deeuu-loudness.md): C++, Python; legacy, no commit since 2019-08; C++ library with SWIG Python bindings for building loudness models from cascaded processing modules.
- [fluctuation-strength-TUe](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/fluctuation-strength-tue.md): MATLAB; legacy, no commit since 2020-01; MATLAB code of the fluctuation strength model of Osses, García & Kohlrausch (2016) (FluctuationStrength_TUe.m), with the stimuli of the paper and a demo that reproduces its figures.
- [HAW loudness tool](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/haw-specific-loudness.md): MATLAB; legacy, no commit since 2022-12; MATLAB tool with a graphical interface, from HAW Hamburg, that shows the specific loudness of time-varying sounds: a Moore–Glasberg front end on ERB bands with temporal processing after Glasberg & Moore (2002), Chalupper & Fastl (2002) or Baumgarte (2000).
- [IoSR Matlab Toolbox](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/iosr-matlab-toolbox.md): MATLAB; legacy, no commit since 2017-08; General-purpose MATLAB toolbox from the Institute of Sound Recording (University of Surrey) for auditory modelling, signal processing, source separation, statistics and plotting.
- [MoSQITo-FDP](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito-fdp.md): Python; legacy, archived; Archived Python snapshot of a MoSQITo fork made for a final-degree project.
- [PsychoacousticParametersMeasurer](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psychoacoustic-parameters-measurer.md): Python; legacy, no commit since 2021-06; Python scripts, commented in Spanish, that translate psychoacoustic parameters described in Zwicker and Fastl's book: Zwicker loudness (stationary and time-varying, from third-octave levels), sharpness, roughness, fluctuation strength and psychoacoustic annoyance.
- [PsySound3](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psysound3.md): MATLAB; legacy, no commit since 2015-03; MATLAB program with a graphical interface for analysing sound recordings.
- [python-acoustics](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/python-acoustics.md): Python; legacy, archived; General Python library for acousticians, published on PyPI as acoustics.
- [SUAVE](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/suave.md): Python; legacy, no commit since 2022-12; Python environment for the multi-fidelity conceptual design of aircraft ("An Aerospace Vehicle Environment").
- [Swift & Gee codes](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/rapid-loudness-sharpness.md): MATLAB; legacy, no commit since 2020-01; MATLAB code by S. Hales Swift (Brigham Young University) on MATLAB File Exchange for fast Moore–Glasberg loudness: ANSI S3.4-2007 stationary loudness and Glasberg & Moore (2002) time-varying loudness, each with the sharpness of Swift & Gee (2017), which is computed from Moore–Glasberg specific loudness.
- [Zhen-Ni/epnl](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/zhen-ni-epnl.md): Rust; legacy, no commit since 2023-07; Small Rust crate that computes perceived noisiness (noy), perceived noise level (PNL) and tone-corrected perceived noise level (PNLT) from 24 one-third-octave band levels, citing ICAO Annex 16, Volume I, Appendix 2 in its code comments.
- [zwickerloudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/zwickerloudness-sourceforge.md): C; legacy, no commit since 2018-06; Console program in C, for BSD, Linux and Windows, that calculates the loudness of stationary sounds with Zwicker's method (ISO 532B / DIN 45631) from one-third-octave band levels.

## Others

Tools that do not compute the metrics themselves: interfaces, front ends and wrappers that call one of the listed projects. They are not listed under the metrics.

- [PsychoBox](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psychobox.md): Python; calls MoSQITo; Desktop application (PySide6 GUI) for playing, editing, filtering and analysing audio.
- [Soundscapy](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/soundscapy.md): Python; calls MoSQITo; Python library for soundscape assessment.
- [ZwickerLoudnessAudio.jl](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/zwickerloudnessaudio-jl.md): Julia; calls ZwickerLoudness.jl; newly released (not yet seen to be widely used); Julia front end to ZwickerLoudness.jl that computes ISO 532-1:2017 Zwicker loudness from waveforms or WAV files: stationary loudness, and since v0.3.0 time-varying loudness with N5 and N10.

## Status unknown

Projects whose code could not be opened, for example because the repository needs a login. What they implement is unverified, so they are listed with what they claim and not under the metrics.

- [PsyTools](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psytools.md): Python; the repository cannot be opened without a login; claims: A conference paper describes an open-source Python toolbox for standardised psychoacoustic analysis: loudness, sharpness, fluctuation strength, roughness, tonality, psychoacoustic annoyance, LAeq and LAmax, following ISO 532-1, DIN 45692 and ECMA-418, with the Zwicker model and the Sottek Hearing Model.

---

# About LISQM

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/about.html

Are you looking for an open-source way to calculate psychoacoustic metrics such as loudness, sharpness, roughness and tonality? One you can trust, and that fits your coding environment, whether Python, MATLAB, C/C++, Rust, Julia or another language? LISQM lists the open-source implementations of each metric under the standard it follows, together with the validation each one reports.

LISQM stands for List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics. LISQM does not compute anything itself; it lists the implementations and compares what they state. The listed implementations publish their source code, most under an open-source licence; a few have no licence file, or a source-available or non-commercial licence: they are tagged on the metric pages and the Languages page, and each project's page gives the details. The data of LISQM is open, but many of the standards the implementations follow are not free.

## Why I built LISQM

I built LISQM out of my own frustration. I work in Python and used **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)**.
Unfortunately, it hasn't been updated since 2024, and some metrics I needed, like Aures tonality, were missing. I
ended up calling the **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** toolbox from Python through the
[MATLAB Engine API](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/languages.html#across). Only much later did I come across [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/pysqat.html), a
newer Python port of SQAT.

So I started a living list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic and sound quality metrics, hoping to
save others with the same need some time.

LISQM is built from each project's own documentation and the related publications, and is renewed monthly. The
judgements on the site currently rest mainly on my own experience as a user, so I would really value the
community's input. Whether you use these tools, contribute to them, maintain a project, or want to share a new
one you've built, I'd love to [hear from you](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/faq.html#message). Corrections, missing projects and suggestions are
all welcome. I hope LISQM becomes a useful place for all of us.

— Zhenxian LI

## What is included

The list includes open-source code that computes a psychoacoustic metric and says which model or standard edition it follows. Quantities: loudness, sharpness, roughness, fluctuation strength, tonality, impulsiveness, psychoacoustic annoyance, and related quantities. Not included: LUFS / ITU-R BS.1770, speech intelligibility, codec quality metrics (PEAQ, PESQ, ViSQOL), psychophysics experiment software, music sensory-dissonance models, feature extractors whose loudness or sharpness follow no named psychoacoustic model, and closed-source tools. The ISO 532 reference programs (free to download, not modifiable) are described on the standards' entries. Reviewed exclusions are listed with reasons in https://github.com/ZhenxianLi/LISQM/blob/main/data/ignored.yaml.

## How entries are checked

Each entry is written from the project's own README, documentation, release notes, licence file and package metadata, with links to those sources. The list records what a project claims. It does not run the code. Repository dates, releases and package versions are refreshed monthly by a GitHub Action, which also searches for new candidate projects and watches the standards bodies for new editions. A person reviews the findings before anything is added.

## Status of an implementation

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| available | In the latest release, or on the default branch of a project without releases. |
| unreleased | Merged on the default branch but newer than the latest release. |
| PR | Open pull request or separate branch, not merged. |

## Validation evidence

Validation is recorded as each project states it. When a project says what it compared its results with (MoSQITo, SQAT, the model authors' code or commercial software), the list names it, and the project page gives the details under *How it was validated*. Two implementations that agree compute the same values, but an error they share goes unnoticed.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| standard or paper data | Compared with test signals or values published in the standard or the model paper. |
| reference code | Compared with the reference program or the model authors' own code. |
| compared with another implementation | Compared with another implementation, named when the project says which. Agreement means that both compute the same values; they may still share an error. |
| own tests only | Tests exist, but without external reference data. |
| not stated | The project does not say how it was validated. |

## Standing of a project

Each project is in one group. A project whose code could not be opened is under status unknown, one that computes nothing itself and calls another listed project is under others, and one that is archived or has had no commit for three years is legacy. Every other project keeps the standing recorded for it: established, newly released or developing. All lists follow the order established, newly released, developing, legacy, others, status unknown, so a project that is new, little used, no longer maintained or unverified is never suggested first. A few projects come before all others in every list, in bold: SQAT and MoSQITo (widely used), and sottek-hearing-model (a very good implementation). They are never listed as legacy, and neither are reference programs published with a standard.

| Group | Meaning |
|---|---|
| established | Described in a publication, used by others, or written by the authors of the model, with more than a year of history. |
| newly released | First released less than about a year ago, and not yet seen to be widely used in the community. |
| developing | Public for more than a year, but without a publication or documented use by others: research, teaching or personal code. |
| legacy | Archived, or no commit for three years or more. Kept for reference. The code may follow an older edition and may not run with current software. |
| other | Tools that do not compute the metrics themselves: interfaces, front ends and wrappers that call one of the listed projects. |
| status unknown | Projects whose code could not be opened, for example because the repository needs a login. What they implement is unverified, so they are listed with what they claim and not under the metrics. |

## Kinds of project

The kind says what a project is for someone who wants to use it. Each project page names it.

| Kind | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Library/Toolbox | Functions to call from your own code: a Python package, a MATLAB toolbox, or a C, C++, C#, Rust or Julia library. |
| Research code | Code published with a study, a thesis or a student project, to run or adapt; not packaged as a library. |
| Application | A program to run, with a graphical or command-line interface; no programming needed. |
| Plug-in | Runs inside other software: a plug-in for an audio workstation, or a Pure Data external. |
| Reference program | Code published with a standard or by the authors of the model, as the reference for it. |

## Leads not yet verified

Candidates that may belong in the list but could not be checked yet. Nothing here has been confirmed.

- [Genesis Loudness Toolbox](http://www.genesis-acoustics.com/index.php?page=32) (MATLAB): Free MATLAB toolbox (2010) said to cover ISO 532B / DIN 45631, ANSI S3.4-2007, Zwicker's time-varying model, Glasberg & Moore (2002) and Boullet's (2006) loudness model for impulsive sounds. An [archived copy](https://web.archive.org/web/20150306205824/http://genesis-acoustics.com/index.php?page=32) of the page (2015) says the ZIP file contains MATLAB source files, validation WAV files and a Readme with the terms of use, but the download page was not archived and the website could not be reached, so the code and its licence could not be checked.
- [Salford sound quality MATLAB codes](https://acoustics.salford.ac.uk/psychoacoustics/sound-quality-making-products-sound-better/an-introduction-to-sound-quality-testing/matlab-codes/) (MATLAB): Functions named `loudness_1991` (Zwicker loudness, free or diffuse field), `sharpness_Fastl` and `roughness4`. The page describes the functions, but its "Download the MATLAB codes" item has no link, also in an [archived copy](https://web.archive.org/web/20250709072252/https://acoustics.salford.ac.uk/psychoacoustics/sound-quality-making-products-sound-better/an-introduction-to-sound-quality-testing/matlab-codes/) of July 2025, so the code could not be obtained.

Not listed because they are closed source: MATLAB Audio Toolbox, HEAD acoustics ArtemiS SUITE, Simcenter Testlab, HBK BK Connect and Ansys Sound.

## Machine-readable data

- [index.json](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/index.json): the whole index as JSON
- [llms.txt](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/llms.txt) and [llms-full.txt](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/llms-full.txt): summaries for language models
- [feed.xml](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/feed.xml): Atom feed of updates
- [references.bib](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/references.bib): every standard, model paper and software paper, as BibTeX
- Source data and schema: https://github.com/ZhenxianLi/LISQM/tree/main/data

Visits to the website are counted with Cloudflare Web Analytics, which sets no cookies.

To cite the list, use the CITATION.cff file in the repository, and cite the implementations you used as each project page says under *How to cite*. The standards and papers are in https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/references.bib.

# Frequently asked questions

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/faq.html

Questions, corrections and suggestions are welcome as GitHub issues: https://github.com/ZhenxianLi/LISQM/issues/new

## Which code should I use for a psychoacoustic metric?

Choose by your own environment first: the language you work in and how the results will be used. The [Languages](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/languages.html) page shows which metrics can be computed from each language and how each project can be called, also from another language. The [Metrics](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/) page names the current edition of each of the 22 metrics, and each metric page lists every implementation of it, with the validation it states, the code it was ported from and the choices that change its numbers. Those widely used projects, **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** (MATLAB) and **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)** (Python), come first in the lists, together with **[sottek-hearing-model](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sottek-hearing-model.html)** (Python), a very good implementation, but they are not the only choice. Newer projects, not yet seen to be widely used, often check their results against MoSQITo or SQAT (8 of the 10 newly released ones do), and some are built for a particular use: [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/metasona.html) is a C library written for fast, real-time analysis, with a rolling analyser for audio that arrives in chunks; [iso532-1-rs](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/iso532-1-rs.html) is a Rust engine with a streaming interface and a C interface; [torch_amt](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/torch-amt.html) brings the AMT loudness models to PyTorch, differentiable and able to run on GPU. [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/pysqat.html) ports SQAT to Python, adds a graphical interface and checks each metric against SQAT v1.3. Before relying on any of them, check the validation each project states and whether the fix you need is in a release or only on its main branch.

## Which metrics can I compute in Python, MATLAB or C?

Metrics whose current edition has a released open-source implementation, by language: Python: 19 of 22 (8 only from newly released projects); MATLAB/Octave: 12 of 22; C/C++: 7 of 22 (7 only from newly released projects); Rust: 2 of 22 (2 only from newly released projects); Julia: 5 of 22 (5 only from newly released projects). The [Languages](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/languages.html) page lists them, and explains how each project can be used from another language, for example a MATLAB toolbox from Python through the MATLAB Engine API.

## Why does it matter which edition a tool implements?

Psychoacoustic standards change between editions. ECMA-418-2, for example, has had four editions since 2020 that changed the hearing model, roughness and loudness, and all three parts of ISO 532 are being revised. Two tools that both claim to implement a standard can therefore give different values for the same sound. Liu et al. (2026, Acoustics Australia, doi:10.1007/s40857-026-00393-3) compared four tools and found differences large enough to change the predictions of sound-quality models. Each metric page lists the editions and which tool follows which.

## Which metrics have no open-source implementation yet?

No available open-source implementation of the current edition was found for [Roughness, DIN 38455](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/roughness-din-38455.html), [Tonal components and tone adjustment (DIN 45681)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tonality-din-45681.html), and [Audibility of tones in noise (ISO/TS 20065)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tonal-audibility-iso-20065.html). The current editions of [Moore–Glasberg loudness of stationary sounds (ISO 532-2, ANSI S3.4)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg.html), [Fluctuation strength from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/fluctuation-strength-ecma-418-2.html), [Tone-to-noise ratio and prominence ratio (ECMA-418-1)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tone-to-noise-prominence-ratio.html), [Tonal audibility in environmental noise (ISO 1996-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tonal-audibility-iso-1996-2.html), [Tonal audibility of wind turbine noise (IEC 61400-11)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tonal-audibility-iec-61400-11.html), [Prominence of impulsive sounds (ISO/PAS 1996-3, NT ACOU 112)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/impulsiveness.html), and [Equal-loudness-level contours (ISO 226)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/equal-loudness-contours.html) have released implementations only from newly released projects, not yet seen to be widely used.

## What do established, newly released, developing and legacy mean?

Every project is in one group. Established: Described in a publication, used by others, or written by the authors of the model, with more than a year of history. Newly released: First released less than about a year ago, and not yet seen to be widely used in the community. Developing: Public for more than a year, but without a publication or documented use by others: research, teaching or personal code. Legacy: Archived, or no commit for three years or more. Kept for reference. The code may follow an older edition and may not run with current software. Others: Tools that do not compute the metrics themselves: interfaces, front ends and wrappers that call one of the listed projects. Status unknown: Projects whose code could not be opened, for example because the repository needs a login. What they implement is unverified, so they are listed with what they claim and not under the metrics. Lists follow this order, so a project that is new, little used, no longer maintained or unverified is never suggested first. SQAT and MoSQITo (widely used), and sottek-hearing-model (a very good implementation) come first in every list, in bold, and they and the reference programs published with a standard are never listed as legacy. Newly released projects: [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/metasona.html) (First released in September 2026), [iso532-1-rs](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/iso532-1-rs.html) (First version tagged in July 2026), [Kirin Hypha](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/kirin-hypha.html) (First public commit in April 2026; v1.0.0 was released in May 2026), [Mosqito.NET](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito-net.html) (First published on GitHub in April 2026), [NumpyLibforPsychoAcoustic](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/numpylib-psychoacoustic.html) (First published on GitHub in November 2025), [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html) (Its psychoacoustics module was first released in July 2026 (version 3.1.0)), [PsychoacousticMetrics.jl](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psychoacousticmetrics-jl.html) (First registered in July 2026), [SoundPalette](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/soundpalette.html) (Its psychoacoustic metrics were added in July 2026 (v0.5.0)), [torch_amt](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/torch-amt.html) (First released in February 2026), and [ZwickerLoudness.jl](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/zwickerloudness-jl.html) (First registered in February 2026). Legacy projects: [deeuu/loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/deeuu-loudness.html) (last commit 2019-08), [fluctuation-strength-TUe](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/fluctuation-strength-tue.html) (last commit 2020-01), [HAW loudness tool](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/haw-specific-loudness.html) (last commit 2022-12), [IoSR Matlab Toolbox](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/iosr-matlab-toolbox.html) (last commit 2017-08), [MoSQITo-FDP](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito-fdp.html) (archived), [PsychoacousticParametersMeasurer](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psychoacoustic-parameters-measurer.html) (last commit 2021-06), [PsySound3](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psysound3.html) (last commit 2015-03), [python-acoustics](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/python-acoustics.html) (archived), [SUAVE](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/suave.html) (last commit 2022-12), [Swift & Gee codes](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/rapid-loudness-sharpness.html) (last commit 2020-01), [Zhen-Ni/epnl](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/zhen-ni-epnl.html) (last commit 2023-07), and [zwickerloudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/zwickerloudness-sourceforge.html) (last commit 2018-06). All groups are on the [Projects](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/) page.

## How are the entries checked?

From each project's own README, documentation, release notes, licence file and package metadata, with links to those sources. The list records what a project claims and does not run the code. Repository and package metadata are refreshed monthly, and a person reviews new findings.

## Can I rely on a listed implementation in a report that an authority will check?

Being listed here is not a certification or an approval: LISQM records what each project states and has not run the code. For a report that an authority, a certification body or a client will check, use the edition and method that the regulation or contract names, check the implementation yourself with the test signals or reference data of that edition where it gives them, and state the version or commit you used. Each metric page lists the editions and what each project says about its validation.


---

# Zwicker loudness (ISO 532-1, DIN 45631)

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html

**Quantity:** Loudness · **Unit:** sone, phon · **Also known as:** ISO 532-1, ISO 532B, ISO 532 method B, DIN 45631, DIN 45631/A1, Zwicker method

Loudness from Zwicker's model: third-octave band levels are turned into specific loudness on the critical-band (Bark) scale and integrated. ISO 532-1:2017 specifies one procedure for stationary sounds and one for time-varying sounds (from which percentile values are taken, such as N5, the loudness exceeded 5 % of the time), and replaced method B of ISO 532:1975. The German standards DIN 45631 (stationary) and DIN 45631/A1 (time-varying) specify Zwicker's method; ISO 532-1:2017 states that its stationary method is based on DIN 45631:1991.

The current edition is ISO 532-1:2017. In development: ISO/CD 532-1. Open-source implementations of it: **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** (MATLAB; stationary and time-varying), **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)** (Python; stationary (also per segment and from a spectrum) and time-varying), [AARAE](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/aarae.html) (MATLAB; stationary and time-varying), [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/metasona.html) (C, Python; newly released, not yet seen to be widely used; stationary and time-varying; also from 28 third-octave levels), [iso532-1-rs](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/iso532-1-rs.html) (Rust, C, Python; newly released, not yet seen to be widely used; stationary, time-varying and streaming), [Kirin Hypha](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/kirin-hypha.html) (Rust; newly released, not yet seen to be widely used; time-varying, per channel at 48 kHz; stored in the recorded data), [Mosqito.NET](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito-net.html) (C#; newly released, not yet seen to be widely used; stationary (also per segment and from a spectrum) and time-varying), [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html) (Python; newly released, not yet seen to be widely used; stationary and time-varying), [SoundPalette](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/soundpalette.html) (C++; newly released, not yet seen to be widely used; time-varying, reported as N5; monaural), [ZwickerLoudness.jl](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/zwickerloudness-jl.html) (Julia; newly released, not yet seen to be widely used; stationary, from 28 one-third-octave band levels), [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/pysqat.html) (Python; developing), and [PsychoacousticParametersMeasurer](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psychoacoustic-parameters-measurer.html) (Python; legacy, no commit since 2021-06; stationary and time-varying, from third-octave levels). Implementations of earlier editions or related models: [ITA-Toolbox](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/ita-toolbox.html) (MATLAB; DIN 45631/A1:2010; time-varying, with N5), [AARAE](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/aarae.html) (MATLAB; Chalupper & Fastl (2002); time-varying), [ITA-Toolbox](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/ita-toolbox.html) (MATLAB; DIN 45631:1991; stationary; free or diffuse field), [PsySound3](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psysound3.html) (MATLAB; legacy, no commit since 2015-03; Chalupper & Fastl (2002); time-varying), [deeuu/loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/deeuu-loudness.html) (C++, Python; legacy, no commit since 2019-08; DIN 45631:1991; stationary only), and [zwickerloudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/zwickerloudness-sourceforge.html) (C; legacy, no commit since 2018-06; DIN 45631:1991; stationary, from one-third-octave band levels).

In China, GB/T 25982-2024 (interior noise of buses, in force since July 2025) sets loudness and sharpness limits and gives Zwicker's calculation in an informative annex.

## Editions and who implements them

| Date | Edition | Status | What changed | Implemented by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2024-11 | [ISO/CD 532-1](https://www.iso.org/standard/90809.html) | in development | Second edition at committee-draft stage since November 2024. | — |
| 2017-06 | [ISO 532-1:2017](https://www.iso.org/standard/63077.html) | current; Under revision; the 2nd edition has been at committee-draft stage since 2024-11-01. | Stationary and time-varying procedures; Annex A reference program, Annex B test signals. | **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)**, **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)**, [AARAE](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/aarae.html), [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/metasona.html), [iso532-1-rs](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/iso532-1-rs.html), [Kirin Hypha](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/kirin-hypha.html), [Mosqito.NET](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito-net.html), [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html), [SoundPalette](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/soundpalette.html), [ZwickerLoudness.jl](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/zwickerloudness-jl.html), [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/pysqat.html), [PsychoacousticParametersMeasurer](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psychoacoustic-parameters-measurer.html) |
| 2010-03 | [DIN 45631/A1:2010](https://www.dinmedia.de/en/standard/din-45631-a1/122476084) | current | Adds the procedure for time-varying sounds. | [ITA-Toolbox](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/ita-toolbox.html) |
| 2002 | [Chalupper & Fastl (2002)](https://www.ingentaconnect.com/contentone/dav/aaua/2002/00000088/00000003/art00009) | published | Dynamic loudness model built on Zwicker's model, also for hearing impairment (not standardised). | [AARAE](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/aarae.html), [PsySound3](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psysound3.html) |
| 1991-03 | [DIN 45631:1991](https://www.dinmedia.de/en/standard/din-45631/1666531) | current | Stationary sounds. | [ITA-Toolbox](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/ita-toolbox.html), [deeuu/loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/deeuu-loudness.html), [zwickerloudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/zwickerloudness-sourceforge.html) |
| 1975-07 | [ISO 532:1975](https://www.iso.org/standard/4603.html) | withdrawn | Method B (Zwicker) for stationary sounds, from third-octave levels. | — |

## Implementations

| Project | Language | Edition | Functions | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** | MATLAB | [ISO 532-1:2017](https://www.iso.org/standard/63077.html) (stationary and time-varying; since v1.0) | `Loudness_ISO532_1`, `Loudness_ISO532_1_from_wavfile` | standard or paper data (in v1.3, test signal 10 is off by 18.14 %) | The releases do not allow commercial use; the default branch has another licence. Fixes to the time-varying procedure are on `main` only (PR #48). |
| **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)** | Python | [ISO 532-1:2017](https://www.iso.org/standard/63077.html) (stationary (also per segment and from a spectrum) and time-varying; since 1.0.0) | `loudness_zwst`, `loudness_zwst_perseg`, `loudness_zwst_freq`, `loudness_zwtv` | standard or paper data (outcome not stated) | — |
| [AARAE](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/aarae.html) | MATLAB | [ISO 532-1:2017](https://www.iso.org/standard/63077.html) (stationary and time-varying) | `Loudness_ISO532_1` | standard or paper data (time-varying signals only) | The header cites a 2014 draft of ISO 532-1 and describes the code as Ella Manor's 2015 MATLAB port, with adjustments, of the Annex A C code. |
| [ITA-Toolbox](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/ita-toolbox.html) | MATLAB | [DIN 45631/A1:2010](https://www.dinmedia.de/en/standard/din-45631-a1/122476084) (time-varying, with N5) | `ita_loudness_timevariant` | standard or paper data (results plotted, not checked) | The header says "DIN 45631/A1" without a year; the function was written in August 2010, after the amendment was published. A code comment says the C code of the nonlinearity block was copied from the DIN document, "without its errors". |
| [AARAE](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/aarae.html) | MATLAB | [Chalupper & Fastl (2002)](https://www.ingentaconnect.com/contentone/dav/aaua/2002/00000088/00000003/art00009) (time-varying) | `LoudnessCF` | not stated | Also outputs loudness fluctuation and time-varying sharpness. Josef Chalupper's code (2000) in its PsySound3 version (2007), adjusted for AARAE by Ella Manor in 2015. |
| [ITA-Toolbox](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/ita-toolbox.html) | MATLAB | [DIN 45631:1991](https://www.dinmedia.de/en/standard/din-45631/1666531) (stationary; free or diffuse field) | `ita_loudness` | standard or paper data | The header says "DIN 45631 / ISO 532 B". The C core (`private/DIN45631.c`) is Aaron Hastings' version (2000) of the BASIC program published by Zwicker, Fastl, Widmann, Kurakata, Kuwano and Namba in J. Acoust. Soc. Jpn (E) 12(1), 1991. |
| [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/metasona.html) | C, Python | [ISO 532-1:2017](https://www.iso.org/standard/63077.html) (stationary and time-varying; also from 28 third-octave levels; since 0.1.0) | `stationary_loudness`, `time_varying_loudness`, `loudness_from_levels` | compared with MoSQITo (its source) | Newly released project, not yet seen to be widely used. |
| [iso532-1-rs](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/iso532-1-rs.html) | Rust, C, Python | [ISO 532-1:2017](https://www.iso.org/standard/63077.html) (stationary, time-varying and streaming; since 0.1.0) | `loudness_zwst`, `loudness_zwtv`, `ZwtvStream` | standard or paper data; also compared with MoSQITo | Newly released project, not yet seen to be widely used. Python uses the same names (`iso532.loudness_zwst` …); the C API has `iso532_loudness_zwst`, `iso532_loudness_zwtv` and `iso532_stream_*`. |
| [Kirin Hypha](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/kirin-hypha.html) | Rust | [ISO 532-1:2017](https://www.iso.org/standard/63077.html) (time-varying, per channel at 48 kHz; stored in the recorded data; since 1.0.0) | `kirin_measure::phase_d` | compared with MoSQITo (its source) | Newly released project, not yet seen to be widely used. Ported from MoSQITo v1.2.1. |
| [Mosqito.NET](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito-net.html) | C# | [ISO 532-1:2017](https://www.iso.org/standard/63077.html) (stationary (also per segment and from a spectrum) and time-varying) | `Sq.LoudnessZwst`, `Sq.LoudnessZwstFreq`, `Sq.LoudnessZwstPerSeg`, `Sq.LoudnessZwtv` | standard or paper data; also compared with MoSQITo (its source) | Newly released project, not yet seen to be widely used. |
| [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html) | Python | [ISO 532-1:2017](https://www.iso.org/standard/63077.html) (stationary and time-varying; since 3.1.0) | `loudness_zwicker`, `loudness_zwicker_from_spectrum` | standard or paper data | Newly released project, not yet seen to be widely used. |
| [SoundPalette](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/soundpalette.html) | C++ | [ISO 532-1:2017](https://www.iso.org/standard/63077.html) (time-varying, reported as N5; monaural; since v0.5.0) | `sp::compute_psycho` | compared with MoSQITo | Newly released project, not yet seen to be widely used. A source-available licence, not an open-source one: some uses are not allowed. No MoSQITo code is ported. |
| [ZwickerLoudness.jl](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/zwickerloudness-jl.html) | Julia | [ISO 532-1:2017](https://www.iso.org/standard/63077.html) (stationary, from 28 one-third-octave band levels; since 0.2.0) | `zwicker_loudness` | standard or paper data (one Annex B signal); also compared with MoSQITo | Newly released project, not yet seen to be widely used. |
| [ZwickerLoudness.jl](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/zwickerloudness-jl.html) | Julia | [ISO 532-1:2017](https://www.iso.org/standard/63077.html) (time-varying, from band levels at 2000 Hz; N5 and N10; since 0.3.0) | `zwicker_loudness_time_varying` | standard or paper data (one Annex B signal); also compared with MoSQITo (its source) | Newly released project, not yet seen to be widely used. |
| [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/pysqat.html) | Python | [ISO 532-1:2017](https://www.iso.org/standard/63077.html) | `Loudness_ISO532_1` | compared with SQAT (its source) | Developing project: no publication or documented use by others. No licence file: by default, copying, changing or sharing the code needs the author's permission. |
| [PsychoacousticParametersMeasurer](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psychoacoustic-parameters-measurer.html) | Python | [ISO 532-1:2017](https://www.iso.org/standard/63077.html) (stationary and time-varying, from third-octave levels) | `loudness_ISO532`, `loudness_ISO532_time` | not stated | Legacy project, no longer maintained. No licence file: by default, copying, changing or sharing the code needs the author's permission. The file header says "Loudness ISO 532-1:2014" and the filter coefficients are labelled "ISO 532-1:2014"; the published edition is ISO 532-1:2017. |
| [PsySound3](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psysound3.html) | MATLAB | [Chalupper & Fastl (2002)](https://www.ingentaconnect.com/contentone/dav/aaua/2002/00000088/00000003/art00009) (time-varying) | `@LoudnessCF` | not stated | Legacy project, no longer maintained. No licence file: by default, copying, changing or sharing the code needs the author's permission. The analyser names J. Chalupper and H. Fastl as authors. |
| [deeuu/loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/deeuu-loudness.html) | C++, Python | [DIN 45631:1991](https://www.dinmedia.de/en/standard/din-45631/1666531) (stationary only) | `StationaryLoudnessDIN456311991` | compared with GENESIS ACOUSTICS code (Python port) | Legacy project, no longer maintained. Uses 28 third-octave filters with third-order Butterworth responses after ANSI S1.11:1986; there is no time-varying (DIN 45631/A1) model. |
| [zwickerloudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/zwickerloudness-sourceforge.html) | C | [DIN 45631:1991](https://www.dinmedia.de/en/standard/din-45631/1666531) (stationary, from one-third-octave band levels) | — | own tests only | Legacy project, no longer maintained. Port of the 1991 BASIC program "according to DIN 45631 (ISO 532B)", the program that accompanies DIN 45631:1991; the same program is the basis of deeuu/loudness. |

Also available through tools that call one of these implementations: [PsychoBox](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psychobox.html) (via MoSQITo, ISO 532-1:2017), [Soundscapy](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/soundscapy.html) (via MoSQITo, ISO 532-1:2017), and [ZwickerLoudnessAudio.jl](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/zwickerloudnessaudio-jl.html) (via ZwickerLoudness.jl, ISO 532-1:2017).

**See also:** [Sharpness (DIN 45692, Aures, von Bismarck)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/sharpness.html), [Loudness from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-ecma-418-2.html)

## How they were validated

As reported by each project; LISQM has not run the code. Two implementations that agree can still share the same error.

- **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)**, ISO 532-1:2017: standard or paper data (in v1.3, test signal 10 is off by 18.14 %)
  - Ported or adapted from [AARAE](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/aarae.html).
  - Checked with the 25 test signals of Annex B.2–B.5 against the standard's tolerances.
- **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)**, ISO 532-1:2017: standard or paper data (outcome not stated)
  - Ported or adapted from BASIC program of DIN 45631 (Zwicker et al., 1991).
  - Validation scripts use the ISO 532-1 Annex B test signals; the documentation marks it as validated.
- [AARAE](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/aarae.html), ISO 532-1:2017: standard or paper data (time-varying signals only)
  - Ported or adapted from ISO 532-1 Annex A reference program.
  - A commit of 2017-12-11 says the code was verified with the time-varying test signals of Annex B.5; no check of the stationary method is stated.
- [ITA-Toolbox](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/ita-toolbox.html), DIN 45631/A1:2010: standard or paper data (results plotted, not checked)
  - A test script plots the results for the amendment's test signals A to D (1 kHz tone pulses of 10 ms to 500 ms) against its tolerance bands; it does not check them automatically.
- [AARAE](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/aarae.html), Chalupper & Fastl (2002): not stated
  - Ported or adapted from [PsySound3](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psysound3.html) (the author's own code).
- [ITA-Toolbox](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/ita-toolbox.html), DIN 45631:1991: standard or paper data
  - Ported or adapted from BASIC program of DIN 45631 (Zwicker et al., 1991).
  - A test compares the loudness of a generated pink noise with 95.09 sone (GF), a value the test attributes to DIN 45631, within 5 %, with third-octave levels computed both by FFT and by filter bank.
- [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/metasona.html), ISO 532-1:2017: compared with **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)** (its source)
  - Ported or adapted from **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)** and **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)**. It was compared with the code it was ported from, which checks the port only.
  - Model tables taken from MoSQITo were checked element by element; one upper-slope value (0.22) follows the ISO 532-1 reference C table where MoSQITo uses 0.24.
  - The project says that detailed validation and reference comparisons are kept outside the repository; the results are not published. The README says standards conformance has not been established.
- [iso532-1-rs](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/iso532-1-rs.html), ISO 532-1:2017: standard or paper data; also compared with **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)**
  - Parity tests with MoSQITo 1.2.1 on nine synthetic and Annex B signals (worst reported difference 1.3e-9).
  - Checked separately against ISO 532-1 Annex B: the README reports stationary offsets of about +0.82 % and −0.76 % for signals 3 and 5, inside the standard's tolerance, and details signals 3, 5 and 10 in docs/ISO-ANNEXB-NUMERICAL-ERROR-2026-07-04.md.
- [Kirin Hypha](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/kirin-hypha.html), ISO 532-1:2017: compared with **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)** (its source)
  - Ported or adapted from **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)**. It was compared with the code it was ported from, which checks the port only.
  - Tests assert specific loudness within a relative 1e-3 of MoSQITo.
- [Mosqito.NET](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito-net.html), ISO 532-1:2017: standard or paper data; also compared with **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)** (its source)
  - Ported or adapted from **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)**. It was compared with the code it was ported from, which checks the port only.
  - Unit tests ported from MoSQITo compare stationary loudness with ISO 532-1 Annex B values.
  - Every public function is compared with the output of Python MoSQITo for seven WAV files (three of them ISO 532-1 test signals), within 1 % (0.5 dB for levels).
- [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html), ISO 532-1:2017: standard or paper data
  - Ported or adapted from ISO 532-1 Annex A reference program.
  - Annex B test signals are used in the tests.
- [SoundPalette](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/soundpalette.html), ISO 532-1:2017: compared with **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)**
  - Compared with MoSQITo 1.2.1 on calibrated test signals, used as a development-time reference (`NOTES.md`, `tools/psycho_oracle`).
- [ZwickerLoudness.jl](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/zwickerloudness-jl.html), ISO 532-1:2017 (stationary, from 28 one-third-octave band levels): standard or paper data (one Annex B signal); also compared with **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)**
  - Checked against ISO 532-1 Annex B signal 1, the only 28-band reference in Annex B (83.296 sone, tolerance ±5 %).
  - Checked per Bark bin against MoSQITo output (maximum difference below 0.001 sone/Bark).
- [ZwickerLoudness.jl](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/zwickerloudness-jl.html), ISO 532-1:2017 (time-varying, from band levels at 2000 Hz; N5 and N10): standard or paper data (one Annex B signal); also compared with **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)** (its source)
  - Ported or adapted from **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)**. It was compared with the code it was ported from, which checks the port only.
  - Stages are tested against MoSQITo `loudness_zwtv` intermediates (agreement about 1e-9 to 1e-15).
  - An Annex B.4 "Test signal 6" test regenerates band levels from a local MoSQITo checkout and is skipped when none is present; CI clones MoSQITo for it.
  - The ISO WAV files are not included.
- [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/pysqat.html), ISO 532-1:2017: compared with **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** (its source)
  - Ported or adapted from **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)**. It was compared with the code it was ported from, which checks the port only.
  - Compared with SQAT v1.3, run in MATLAB, by `validation/FINAL_VAL.py`; the generated reports are not committed.
- [deeuu/loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/deeuu-loudness.html), DIN 45631:1991: compared with GENESIS ACOUSTICS code (Python port)
  - Ported or adapted from BASIC program of DIN 45631 (Zwicker et al., 1991).
  - Tested against "a quick and dirty Python port of the Matlab code private by GENESIS ACOUSTICS".
- [zwickerloudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/zwickerloudness-sourceforge.html), DIN 45631:1991: own tests only
  - Ported or adapted from BASIC program of DIN 45631 (Zwicker et al., 1991).
  - The documentation in the release archive says that tests with "classical cases", such as the included test WAV files, "seems to give correct results", and invites users to compare the output with that of the original BASIC program.
- [ZwickerLoudnessAudio.jl](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/zwickerloudnessaudio-jl.html) (via ZwickerLoudness.jl), ISO 532-1:2017 (stationary, from a waveform or WAV file): standard or paper data
  - ISO 532-1 Annex B signals 2–5, synthesised in-process, are within the standard's ±5 % (+2.9 %, +3.6 %, +0.5 % and +2.6 % per the README).
- [ZwickerLoudnessAudio.jl](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/zwickerloudnessaudio-jl.html) (via ZwickerLoudness.jl), ISO 532-1:2017 (time-varying, from a waveform or WAV file at 48 kHz): standard or paper data; also compared with **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)** (its source)
  - Ported or adapted from **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)**. It was compared with the code it was ported from, which checks the port only.
  - Cross-checked end to end with MoSQITo `loudness_zwtv` (N(t) about 3e-16 relative, N5/N10 about 2e-15 absolute).
  - An Annex B.4 test is skipped when the ISO recording is not available locally.

Not stated by PsychoacousticParametersMeasurer, PsySound3, PsychoBox, and Soundscapy.

On the map without a line, as no relation is recorded for them: [PsychoacousticParametersMeasurer](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psychoacoustic-parameters-measurer.html).

## Before you compare numbers

Implementations of the same metric can give different numbers without either being wrong. Check these choices first.

- **Sound field.** ISO 532-1 has a free-field and a diffuse-field version, which give different values for the same signal. Most implementations use free field unless told otherwise.
- **Calibration.** The input is sound pressure in pascals. Audio read from a file has to be scaled first, and tools ask for this in different ways: a calibration factor, a reference level or a full-scale level.
- **Sample rate.** The time-varying method is specified at 48 kHz. Some implementations reject other rates, others resample them, and the resampler changes the result slightly.
- **Percentiles.** N5, the loudness exceeded 5 % of the time, depends on how the percentile is taken: SQAT picks the nearest rank, while MATLAB's `prctile` and the NumPy and Julia quantile functions interpolate, each in its own way.
- **Start of the signal.** Time-varying loudness starts from silence and needs time to settle. Whether the start is left out of N5 and other statistics (`time_skip` in SQAT, `time_skip_s` in MetaSona) matters for short signals.

What the projects state:

- **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)**: Statistics such as N5 take the nearest rank of the sorted time series, without interpolation (`get_exceeded_value`), and leave out the first `time_skip` seconds of the signal.
- **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)**: Signals sampled below 48 kHz are resampled to 48 kHz (FFT method) with a warning; time-varying loudness rejects rates above 48 kHz.
- [ITA-Toolbox](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/ita-toolbox.html): N5 is MATLAB's `prctile(N, 95)`. Blocks are 2 ms long without overlap by default, and the signal is processed at its own sample rate. Third-octave levels come from an FFT by default, or from a filter bank (`'mode', 'filter'`).
- [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/metasona.html): Expects calibrated sound pressure in pascals. The C functions require 48 kHz input; the Python interface resamples other rates to 48 kHz (SciPy `resample_poly`). `time_skip_s` (default 0 s) leaves out the start of the signal from the reported frames; the computation still runs over the whole signal. Time-varying results include every complete frame, labelled at frame centres, which differs from SQAT's handling of the last frame and of time stamps.
- [Mosqito.NET](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito-net.html): Time-varying loudness and ECMA-418-2 roughness resample input at any other rate to 48 kHz, and stationary loudness resamples rates below 48 kHz; MoSQITo rejects rates above 48 kHz for time-varying loudness.
- [ZwickerLoudnessAudio.jl](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/zwickerloudnessaudio-jl.html): Stationary loudness resamples input below 48 kHz to 48 kHz (polyphase), with a warning. Time-varying loudness accepts 48 kHz input only (an error otherwise).

## References

1. ISO 532:1975. Acoustics — Method for calculating loudness level. https://www.iso.org/standard/4603.html
2. DIN 45631:1991. Berechnung des Lautstärkepegels und der Lautheit aus dem Geräuschspektrum; Verfahren nach E. Zwicker. https://www.dinmedia.de/en/standard/din-45631/1666531
3. Chalupper, J., & Fastl, H. (2002). Dynamic loudness model (DLM) for normal and hearing-impaired listeners. *Acta Acustica united with Acustica*, 88(3), 378–386. https://www.ingentaconnect.com/contentone/dav/aaua/2002/00000088/00000003/art00009
4. DIN 45631/A1:2010. Calculation of loudness level and loudness from the sound spectrum — Zwicker method — Amendment 1: Calculation of the loudness of time-variant sound. https://www.dinmedia.de/en/standard/din-45631-a1/122476084
5. ISO 532-1:2017. Acoustics — Methods for calculating loudness — Part 1: Zwicker method. https://www.iso.org/standard/63077.html
6. ISO/CD 532-1. Acoustics — Methods for calculating loudness — Part 1: Zwicker method (2nd edition). https://www.iso.org/standard/90809.html

# Moore–Glasberg loudness of stationary sounds (ISO 532-2, ANSI S3.4)

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg.html

**Quantity:** Loudness · **Unit:** sone, phon · **Also known as:** ISO 532-2, ANSI S3.4, ANSI/ASA S3.4-2007, Moore-Glasberg method, Cambridge loudness model

Loudness of stationary sounds from the Moore–Glasberg model: the spectrum is turned into an excitation pattern on the ERB-number scale, then into specific loudness, which is summed. ANSI S3.4-2007 standardised the model of Moore, Glasberg & Baer (1997) with later modifications; ISO 532-2:2017 specifies the method for monaural and binaural listening.

The current edition is ISO 532-2:2017. In development: ISO/CD 532-2. Open-source implementations of it: [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html) (Python; newly released, not yet seen to be widely used; with binaural inhibition). So far, only newly released projects, not yet seen to be widely used in the community, have released an implementation of it. Check their validation before relying on them. Implementations of earlier editions or related models: [AMT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/amt.html) (MATLAB, Octave; Chen et al. (2011)), [AMT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/amt.html) (MATLAB, Octave; Moore, Glasberg & Baer (1997)), [AARAE](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/aarae.html) (MATLAB; Moore, Glasberg & Baer (1997); one channel, or two channels for binaural loudness), [NumpyLibforPsychoAcoustic](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/numpylib-psychoacoustic.html) (Python; newly released, not yet seen to be widely used; Moore, Glasberg & Baer (1997)), [deeuu/loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/deeuu-loudness.html) (C++, Python; legacy, no commit since 2019-08; Chen et al. (2011)), [deeuu/loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/deeuu-loudness.html) (C++, Python; legacy, no commit since 2019-08; ANSI/ASA S3.4-2007; with the binaural inhibition of Moore & Glasberg (2007) for two ears), [Swift & Gee codes](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/rapid-loudness-sharpness.html) (MATLAB; legacy, no commit since 2020-01; ANSI/ASA S3.4-2007), and [PsySound3](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psysound3.html) (MATLAB; legacy, no commit since 2015-03; Moore, Glasberg & Baer (1997)).

## Editions and who implements them

| Date | Edition | Status | What changed | Implemented by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2024-11 | [ISO/CD 532-2](https://www.iso.org/standard/90812.html) | in development | Second edition at committee-draft stage since November 2024. | — |
| 2017-06 | [ISO 532-2:2017](https://www.iso.org/standard/63078.html) | current; Under revision; the 2nd edition has been at committee-draft stage since 2024-11-01. | Monaural and binaural loudness of stationary sounds; source code supplied with the standard. | [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html) |
| 2011 | [Chen et al. (2011)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.heares.2011.08.001) | published | Faster excitation-pattern calculation, also for hearing loss (not standardised). | [AMT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/amt.html), [deeuu/loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/deeuu-loudness.html) |
| 2007 | [ANSI/ASA S3.4-2007](https://webstore.ansi.org/standards/asa/ANSIASAS32007R2020) | current | American standard based on the 1997 model with later modifications. | [deeuu/loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/deeuu-loudness.html), [Swift & Gee codes](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/rapid-loudness-sharpness.html) |
| 1997 | [Moore, Glasberg & Baer (1997)](https://aes2.org/publications/elibrary-page/?id=10272) | published | Model paper (thresholds, loudness and partial loudness). | [AMT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/amt.html), [AARAE](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/aarae.html), [NumpyLibforPsychoAcoustic](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/numpylib-psychoacoustic.html), [PsySound3](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psysound3.html) |

## Implementations

| Project | Language | Edition | Functions | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [AMT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/amt.html) | MATLAB, Octave | [Chen et al. (2011)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.heares.2011.08.001) | `chen2011` | standard or paper data | Listed as "CHEN2011 - Fast excitation pattern estimation". |
| [AMT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/amt.html) | MATLAB, Octave | [Moore, Glasberg & Baer (1997)](https://aes2.org/publications/elibrary-page/?id=10272) | `moore1997` | standard or paper data | Listed as "MOORE1997 - Loudness model for stationary signals" in models/Contents.m. |
| [AARAE](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/aarae.html) | MATLAB | [Moore, Glasberg & Baer (1997)](https://aes2.org/publications/elibrary-page/?id=10272) (one channel, or two channels for binaural loudness) | `Loudness_MGB2b` | not stated | A port and extension of PsySound3's code by Densil Cabrera and Doheon Lee, version 1.02 (27 October 2015). Two-channel input gives binaural loudness after Moore & Glasberg (2007). The audio is resampled to 32 kHz. |
| [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html) | Python | [ISO 532-2:2017](https://www.iso.org/standard/63078.html) (with binaural inhibition; since 3.1.0) | `loudness_moore_glasberg`, `loudness_moore_glasberg_from_spectrum`, `loudness_moore_glasberg_from_third_octave` | standard or paper data | Newly released project, not yet seen to be widely used. |
| [NumpyLibforPsychoAcoustic](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/numpylib-psychoacoustic.html) | Python | [Moore, Glasberg & Baer (1997)](https://aes2.org/publications/elibrary-page/?id=10272) | `model.moore1997`, `equalSones.getEqualSones` | standard or paper data; also compared with AMT (its source) | Newly released project, not yet seen to be widely used. No licence file: by default, copying, changing or sharing the code needs the author's permission. |
| [deeuu/loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/deeuu-loudness.html) | C++, Python | [Chen et al. (2011)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.heares.2011.08.001) | `StationaryLoudnessCHGM2011` | own tests only | Legacy project, no longer maintained. |

| [Swift & Gee codes](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/rapid-loudness-sharpness.html) | MATLAB | [ANSI/ASA S3.4-2007](https://webstore.ansi.org/standards/asa/ANSIASAS32007R2020) | `stationaryLoudness` | not stated | Legacy project, no longer maintained. |
