No licence file: by default, copying, changing or sharing the code needs the author's permission. Also cites Glasberg & Moore (1990) for the auditory filters. The analyser description says it covers time-varying and binaural loudness, and it also cites Glasberg & Moore (2002) and Moore & Glasberg (2007). |

**See also:** [Time-varying loudness, Moore–Glasberg–Schlittenlacher (ISO 532-3)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg-time-varying.html)

## How they were validated

As reported by each project; LISQM has not run the code. Two implementations that agree can still share the same error.

- [AMT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/amt.html), Chen et al. (2011): standard or paper data
  - Has the experiment script `exp_chen2011`; AMT's experiment scripts reproduce the results of the publication they are named after.
- [AMT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/amt.html), Moore, Glasberg & Baer (1997): standard or paper data
  - AMT's experiment scripts (`exp_…`) reproduce published results; this model has `exp_moore1997`.
- [AARAE](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/aarae.html), Moore, Glasberg & Baer (1997): not stated
  - Ported or adapted from [PsySound3](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psysound3.html) (the author's own code).
- [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html), ISO 532-2:2017: standard or paper data
  - The documentation says it reproduces the Annex B tone and broadband cases to within a percent or two.
- [NumpyLibforPsychoAcoustic](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/numpylib-psychoacoustic.html), Moore, Glasberg & Baer (1997): standard or paper data; also compared with [AMT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/amt.html) (its source)
  - Ported or adapted from [AMT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/amt.html). It was compared with the code it was ported from, which checks the port only.
  - The implementation document says the model is compared with the results shown in the original article (plots of its Fig. 8 and Fig. 12).
  - Numerical error reports (PDF) compare intermediate arrays, such as the outer- and middle-ear filter, with AMT's MATLAB output.
- [deeuu/loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/deeuu-loudness.html), Chen et al. (2011): own tests only
- [deeuu/loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/deeuu-loudness.html), ANSI/ASA S3.4-2007: own tests only
  - Unit tests cover each module and model.
  - A validation script writes computed and expected loudness of pure tones to CSV; the expected values are labelled "Table 7" and "Example 2" without naming their source.

Not stated by Swift & Gee codes and PsySound3.

## Project map

The lines of the project map for Moore–Glasberg loudness only (the whole map: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/map.md). Agreement between a project and the code it was ported or adapted from only checks the port.

### Ported or adapted from another project

- From [AMT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/amt.html): [NumpyLibforPsychoAcoustic](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/numpylib-psychoacoustic.html) (Moore, Glasberg & Baer (1997))

### The author's own code

- From [PsySound3](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psysound3.html) (Densil Cabrera): [AARAE](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/aarae.html) (Moore, Glasberg & Baer (1997))

On the map without a line, as no relation is recorded for them: [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html), [deeuu/loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/deeuu-loudness.html), and [Swift & Gee codes](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/rapid-loudness-sharpness.html).

## Before you compare numbers

Implementations of the same metric can give different numbers without either being wrong. Check these choices first.

What the projects state:

- [Swift & Gee codes](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/rapid-loudness-sharpness.html): The code works at 32 kHz; other rates are resampled with the Signal Processing Toolbox's `resample`.

## References

1. Moore, B. C. J., Glasberg, B. R., & Baer, T. (1997). A model for the prediction of thresholds, loudness, and partial loudness. *Journal of the Audio Engineering Society*, 45(4), 224–240. https://aes2.org/publications/elibrary-page/?id=10272
2. ANSI/ASA S3.4-2007. Procedure for the Computation of Loudness of Steady Sounds. https://webstore.ansi.org/standards/asa/ANSIASAS32007R2020
3. Chen, Z., Hu, G., Glasberg, B. R., & Moore, B. C. J. (2011). A new method of calculating auditory excitation patterns and loudness for steady sounds. *Hearing Research*, 282(1–2), 204–215. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.heares.2011.08.001
4. ISO 532-2:2017. Acoustics — Methods for calculating loudness — Part 2: Moore-Glasberg method. https://www.iso.org/standard/63078.html
5. ISO/CD 532-2. Acoustics — Methods for calculating loudness — Part 2: Moore-Glasberg method (2nd edition). https://www.iso.org/standard/90812.html

# Time-varying loudness, Moore–Glasberg–Schlittenlacher (ISO 532-3)

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg-time-varying.html

**Quantity:** Loudness · **Unit:** sone, phon · **Also known as:** ISO 532-3, TVL, time-varying loudness, Glasberg and Moore 2002, Moore-Glasberg-Schlittenlacher method, short-term loudness, long-term loudness

Loudness of time-varying sounds as instantaneous, short-term and long-term loudness. It starts from the Glasberg & Moore (2002) model; Moore et al. (2016) added binaural inhibition and Moore et al. (2018) revised the time constants. ISO 532-3:2023 standardises the resulting Moore–Glasberg–Schlittenlacher method for stationary and time-varying sounds.

The current edition is ISO 532-3:2023. In development: ISO/CD 532-3. Open-source implementations of it: [iso532-3 (tv2018.m)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/js2251-iso532-3.html) (MATLAB; reference MATLAB code referred to in ISO 532-3, per its readme) and [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html) (Python; newly released, not yet seen to be widely used). Implementations of earlier editions or related models: [AMT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/amt.html) (MATLAB, Octave; Moore et al. (2016); binaural), [AMT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/amt.html) (MATLAB, Octave; Glasberg & Moore (2002)), [AARAE](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/aarae.html) (MATLAB; Glasberg & Moore (2002); time-varying; one channel, or two channels for binaural loudness), [torch_amt](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/torch-amt.html) (Python; newly released, not yet seen to be widely used; Moore et al. (2016); binaural), [NumpyLibforPsychoAcoustic](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/numpylib-psychoacoustic.html) (Python; newly released, not yet seen to be widely used; Glasberg & Moore (2002)), [torch_amt](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/torch-amt.html) (Python; newly released, not yet seen to be widely used; Glasberg & Moore (2002); short-term and long-term loudness), [LoudnessModel](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/loudnessmodel.html) (Python; developing; Moore et al. (2018); instantaneous, short-term and long-term loudness; binaural), [deeuu/loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/deeuu-loudness.html) (C++, Python; legacy, no commit since 2019-08; Glasberg & Moore (2002)), [HAW loudness tool](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/haw-specific-loudness.html) (MATLAB; legacy, no commit since 2022-12; Glasberg & Moore (2002); specific loudness over time on ERB bands; three temporal models), [PsySound3](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psysound3.html) (MATLAB; legacy, no commit since 2015-03; Glasberg & Moore (2002); time-varying and binaural), and [Swift & Gee codes](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/rapid-loudness-sharpness.html) (MATLAB; legacy, no commit since 2020-01; Glasberg & Moore (2002)).

## Editions and who implements them

| Date | Edition | Status | What changed | Implemented by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2024-11 | [ISO/CD 532-3](https://www.iso.org/standard/90816.html) | in development | Second edition at committee-draft stage since November 2024. | — |
| 2023-07 | [ISO 532-3:2023](https://www.iso.org/standard/69856.html) | current; Under revision; the 2nd edition has been at committee-draft stage since 2024-11-01. | Standardised method; source code supplied with the standard. | [iso532-3 (tv2018.m)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/js2251-iso532-3.html), [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html) |
| 2018 | [Moore et al. (2018)](https://doi.org/10.1121/1.5027246) | published | Revised time constants. | [LoudnessModel](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/loudnessmodel.html) |
| 2016 | [Moore et al. (2016)](https://doi.org/10.1177/2331216516682698) | published | Adds binaural inhibition. | [AMT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/amt.html), [torch_amt](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/torch-amt.html) |
| 2002 | [Glasberg & Moore (2002)](https://aes2.org/publications/elibrary-page/?id=11081) | published | Time-varying loudness model (short-term and long-term loudness). | [AMT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/amt.html), [AARAE](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/aarae.html), [NumpyLibforPsychoAcoustic](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/numpylib-psychoacoustic.html), [torch_amt](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/torch-amt.html), [deeuu/loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/deeuu-loudness.html), [HAW loudness tool](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/haw-specific-loudness.html), [PsySound3](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psysound3.html), [Swift & Gee codes](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/rapid-loudness-sharpness.html) |

## Implementations

| Project | Language | Edition | Functions | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [iso532-3 (tv2018.m)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/js2251-iso532-3.html) | MATLAB | [ISO 532-3:2023](https://www.iso.org/standard/69856.html) (reference MATLAB code referred to in ISO 532-3, per its readme) | `tv2018` | not stated | No licence file: by default, copying, changing or sharing the code needs the author's permission. Written by the model's authors (per the readme PDF). |
| [AMT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/amt.html) | MATLAB, Octave | [Moore et al. (2016)](https://doi.org/10.1177/2331216516682698) (binaural) | `moore2016` | not stated | Listed as "MOORE2016 - Binaural loudness model". The header says Josef Schlittenlacher provided the original implementation for the AMT in 2018, from code written for ANSI S3.4-2007 and ISO 532-2:2017. |
| [AMT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/amt.html) | MATLAB, Octave | [Glasberg & Moore (2002)](https://aes2.org/publications/elibrary-page/?id=11081) | `glasberg2002` | standard or paper data | Listed as "GLASBERG2002 - Loudness model for time-variant signals". |
| [AARAE](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/aarae.html) | MATLAB | [Glasberg & Moore (2002)](https://aes2.org/publications/elibrary-page/?id=11081) (time-varying; one channel, or two channels for binaural loudness) | `Loudness_MGB2b` | not stated | Same function as the stationary model; the binaural extension follows Moore & Glasberg (2007). |
| [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html) | Python | [ISO 532-3:2023](https://www.iso.org/standard/69856.html) (since 3.1.0) | `loudness_moore_glasberg_time` | standard or paper data | Newly released project, not yet seen to be widely used. |
| [torch_amt](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/torch-amt.html) | Python | [Moore et al. (2016)](https://doi.org/10.1177/2331216516682698) (binaural) | `torch_amt.models.Moore2016` | compared with AMT (its source) | Newly released project, not yet seen to be widely used. Described as a "1:1 port" of AMT `moore2016`, with outer and middle ear per ANSI S3.4-2007 (docstring). |
| [NumpyLibforPsychoAcoustic](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/numpylib-psychoacoustic.html) | Python | [Glasberg & Moore (2002)](https://aes2.org/publications/elibrary-page/?id=11081) | `model.glasberg2002` | not stated | Newly released project, not yet seen to be widely used. No licence file: by default, copying, changing or sharing the code needs the author's permission. Present in the code but not described in the implementation document. |
| [torch_amt](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/torch-amt.html) | Python | [Glasberg & Moore (2002)](https://aes2.org/publications/elibrary-page/?id=11081) (short-term and long-term loudness) | `torch_amt.models.Glasberg2002` | compared with AMT (its source) | Newly released project, not yet seen to be widely used. Ported from AMT `glasberg2002`. |
| [LoudnessModel](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/loudnessmodel.html) | Python | [Moore et al. (2018)](https://doi.org/10.1121/1.5027246) (instantaneous, short-term and long-term loudness; binaural) | `tvl2018.compute_loudness`, `tvl2018_jax.compute_loudness` | own tests only | Developing project: no publication or documented use by others. |
| [deeuu/loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/deeuu-loudness.html) | C++, Python | [Glasberg & Moore (2002)](https://aes2.org/publications/elibrary-page/?id=11081) | `DynamicLoudnessGM2002` | own tests only | Legacy project, no longer maintained. Per the header, excitation patterns follow ANSI S3.4-2007, and parameter sets use the modified long-term time constants of Moore et al. (2003) and the ANSI S3.4-2007 equation for specific loudness at high levels. |
| [HAW loudness tool](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/haw-specific-loudness.html) | MATLAB | [Glasberg & Moore (2002)](https://aes2.org/publications/elibrary-page/?id=11081) (specific loudness over time on ERB bands; three temporal models) | `loud_gui`, `matlab_loud` | reference code: LOUDAES and TVL (Glasberg & Moore's programs) | Legacy project, no longer maintained. |
| [PsySound3](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psysound3.html) | MATLAB | [Glasberg & Moore (2002)](https://aes2.org/publications/elibrary-page/?id=11081) (time-varying and binaural) | `@LoudnessMGB` | not stated | Legacy project, no longer maintained. No licence file: by default, copying, changing or sharing the code needs the author's permission. The same analyser as the stationary entry; its description cites Glasberg & Moore (2002). |
| [Swift & Gee codes](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/rapid-loudness-sharpness.html) | MATLAB | [Glasberg & Moore (2002)](https://aes2.org/publications/elibrary-page/?id=11081) | `Glasberg_loudness` | not stated | Legacy project, no longer maintained. |

**See also:** [Moore–Glasberg loudness of stationary sounds (ISO 532-2, ANSI S3.4)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg.html)

## How they were validated

As reported by each project; LISQM has not run the code. Two implementations that agree can still share the same error.

- [iso532-3 (tv2018.m)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/js2251-iso532-3.html), ISO 532-3:2023: not stated
  - The folder "code for tables" has scripts that compute Table 5 (sone to phon) and the values of Annexes B and C (AnnexC.m is headed "Signals numbered as in ISO 532-2 Annex B"); the scripts do not name ISO 532-3.
- [AMT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/amt.html), Moore et al. (2016): not stated
  - There is no `exp_moore2016` experiment script on the develop branch.
- [AMT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/amt.html), Glasberg & Moore (2002): standard or paper data
  - Has the experiment script `exp_glasberg2002`; AMT's experiment scripts reproduce the results of the publication they are named after.
- [AARAE](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/aarae.html), Glasberg & Moore (2002): not stated
  - Ported or adapted from [PsySound3](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psysound3.html) (the author's own code).
- [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html), ISO 532-3:2023: standard or paper data
  - A documented deviation: the Annex B WAV-file cases are not reproduced, and Annex C values are used instead.
- [torch_amt](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/torch-amt.html), Moore et al. (2016); Glasberg & Moore (2002): compared with [AMT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/amt.html) (its source)
  - Ported or adapted from [AMT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/amt.html). It was compared with the code it was ported from, which checks the port only.
  - Agreement with AMT is claimed in the documentation, without stored reference data.
- [LoudnessModel](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/loudnessmodel.html), Moore et al. (2018): own tests only
  - Ported or adapted from [iso532-3 (tv2018.m)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/js2251-iso532-3.html).
  - Tests run in GitHub Actions compare overall loudness, the first five short-term and long-term values and selected intermediate stages for one input (1 kHz tone, 100 ms, 32 kHz) with hard-coded expected values.
  - The README calls this "a known accurate output", but neither it nor the tests say where the values come from.
- [deeuu/loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/deeuu-loudness.html), Glasberg & Moore (2002): own tests only
- [HAW loudness tool](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/haw-specific-loudness.html), Glasberg & Moore (2002): reference code: LOUDAES and TVL (Glasberg & Moore's programs)
  - The thesis compares the total loudness of pure tones (30–100 dB) with LOUDAES, Glasberg & Moore's program for stationary sounds: mostly within 5 %, with larger deviations at low levels near 50 Hz and above 5 kHz (−9.3 % for 5 kHz at 30 dB).
  - For two equal-level tones at 1 and 2 kHz, the deviation from LOUDAES ranges from −4.4 % to +3.8 % with the Hann-window FFT and reaches +6.7 % with the Fourier-time transform.
  - For the stationary part of signals the thesis reports good agreement with TVL, Glasberg & Moore's program for time-varying sounds, without figures.

Not stated by NumpyLibforPsychoAcoustic, PsySound3, and Swift & Gee codes.

## Project map

The lines of the project map for time-varying loudness (Moore–Glasberg–Schlittenlacher) only (the whole map: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/map.md). Agreement between a project and the code it was ported or adapted from only checks the port.

### Ported or adapted from another project

- From [AMT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/amt.html): [NumpyLibforPsychoAcoustic](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/numpylib-psychoacoustic.html) (Glasberg & Moore (2002)); [torch_amt](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/torch-amt.html) (Moore et al. (2016) and Glasberg & Moore (2002))
- From [iso532-3 (tv2018.m)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/js2251-iso532-3.html): [LoudnessModel](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/loudnessmodel.html) (Moore et al. (2018))

### The author's own code

- From [PsySound3](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psysound3.html) (Densil Cabrera): [AARAE](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/aarae.html) (Glasberg & Moore (2002))

On the map without a line, as no relation is recorded for them: [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html), [deeuu/loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/deeuu-loudness.html), [HAW loudness tool](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/haw-specific-loudness.html), and [Swift & Gee codes](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/rapid-loudness-sharpness.html).

## Before you compare numbers

Implementations of the same metric can give different numbers without either being wrong. Check these choices first.

- **Sample rate.** The Cambridge programs and ISO 532-3 work at 32 kHz. Most implementations resample to it; phonometry runs at the native rate (a documented deviation), and the Swift & Gee code and the HAW tool expect 32 kHz input.
- **Which output.** The models give instantaneous, short-term and long-term loudness; compare like with like.

What the projects state:

- [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html): Documented deviation: it runs at the native sample rate instead of resampling to 32 kHz.
- [HAW loudness tool](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/haw-specific-loudness.html): Input must be sampled at 32 kHz; the reference level is entered as the sound pressure level of a full-scale sine.
- [Swift & Gee codes](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/rapid-loudness-sharpness.html): The code works at 32 kHz; other rates are resampled with the Signal Processing Toolbox's `resample`.

## References

1. Glasberg, B. R., & Moore, B. C. J. (2002). A model of loudness applicable to time-varying sounds. *Journal of the Audio Engineering Society*, 50(5), 331–342. https://aes2.org/publications/elibrary-page/?id=11081
2. Moore, B. C. J., Glasberg, B. R., Varathanathan, A., & Schlittenlacher, J. (2016). A loudness model for time-varying sounds incorporating binaural inhibition. *Trends in Hearing*, 20, 2331216516682698. https://doi.org/10.1177/2331216516682698
3. Moore, B. C. J., Jervis, M., Harries, L., & Schlittenlacher, J. (2018). Testing and refining a loudness model for time-varying sounds incorporating binaural inhibition. *The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America*, 143(3), 1504–1513. https://doi.org/10.1121/1.5027246
4. ISO 532-3:2023. Acoustics — Methods for calculating loudness — Part 3: Moore-Glasberg-Schlittenlacher method. https://www.iso.org/standard/69856.html
5. ISO/CD 532-3. Acoustics — Methods for calculating loudness — Part 3: Moore-Glasberg-Schlittenlacher method (2nd edition). https://www.iso.org/standard/90816.html

# Loudness from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-ecma-418-2.html

**Quantity:** Loudness · **Unit:** sone_HMS · **Also known as:** ECMA-418-2 loudness, Sottek Hearing Model, SHM loudness, sone_HMS, hearing model loudness

Loudness from the Sottek Hearing Model defined in ECMA-418-2. The hearing model (Clause 5) produces specific loudness; the 2nd edition (2022) added a loudness calculation for sounds with tonal and noise components (Clause 8). ECMA-418-2 has had four editions in five years, so implementations of different editions can disagree.

The current edition is ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.). Open-source implementations of it: **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** (MATLAB; unreleased), **[sottek-hearing-model](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sottek-hearing-model.html)** (Python; mono or stereo, with combined binaural output), [refmap-psychoacoustics](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/refmap-psychoacoustics.html) (MATLAB, Python; binaural and specific loudness), [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/metasona.html) (C, Python; newly released, not yet seen to be widely used; Clause 8 loudness with tonal/noise separation; mono or stereo), and [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html) (Python; newly released, not yet seen to be widely used; mono only). Implementations of earlier editions or related models: **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** (MATLAB; ECMA-418-2:2024 (3rd ed.); mono or two channels with binaural combination), **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)** (Python; ECMA-418-2:2022 (2nd ed.); Clause 5 hearing-model specific and total loudness only; the Clause 8 loudness added in the 2nd edition is not implemented), [Mosqito.NET](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito-net.html) (C#; newly released, not yet seen to be widely used; ECMA-418-2:2022 (2nd ed.); Clause 5 hearing-model loudness only, as in MoSQITo), and [MoSQITo-FDP](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito-fdp.html) (Python; legacy, archived; ECMA-418-2:2020 (1st ed.); hearing model with specific and total loudness).

| 2024-12 | [ECMA-418-2:2024 (3rd ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_3rd_edition_december_2024.pdf) | superseded | Adds a diffuse-field outer and middle ear filter. | **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** |
| 2022-12 | [ECMA-418-2:2022 (2nd ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_2nd_edition_december_2022.pdf) | superseded | New Clause 8, loudness of sounds with subcritical or wider bandwidth. | **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)**, [Mosqito.NET](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito-net.html) |
| 2020-12 | [ECMA-418-2:2020 (1st ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_1st_edition_december_2020.pdf) | superseded | Hearing model (Clause 5) with specific loudness. | [MoSQITo-FDP](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito-fdp.html) |

## How they were validated

As reported by each project; LISQM has not run the code. Two implementations that agree can still share the same error.

- **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)**, ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.): compared with ArtemiS SUITE (HEAD acoustics)
  - Ported or adapted from [refmap-psychoacoustics](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/refmap-psychoacoustics.html) (the author's own code).
  - On `main`, checked for the 4th edition against the ISO 226:2003 equal-loudness contours and against reference results from HEAD acoustics ArtemiS SUITE 17.1 (named in the source of SQAT's validation page) for a binaural recording of a train station (last checked in November 2025).
- **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)**, ECMA-418-2:2024 (3rd ed.): compared with ArtemiS SUITE (HEAD acoustics)
  - Ported or adapted from [refmap-psychoacoustics](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/refmap-psychoacoustics.html) (the author's own code).
  - Checked against the ISO 226:2003 equal-loudness contours and against reference results from HEAD acoustics ArtemiS SUITE 15.7 (named in the source of SQAT's validation page) for a binaural recording of a train station.
- **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)**, ECMA-418-2:2022 (2nd ed.): standard or paper data (outcome not stated)
  - Validation scripts compare with figures of the standard.
- **[sottek-hearing-model](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sottek-hearing-model.html)**, ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.): standard or paper data (calibration signals and one recording); also compared with ArtemiS SUITE (HEAD acoustics)
  - Ported or adapted from [refmap-psychoacoustics](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/refmap-psychoacoustics.html) (the author's own code).
  - Unit tests check the standard's calibration signals (1 kHz, 40 dB gives 1 sone_HMS).
  - RefMap's verification compared the Python code, before it became this package, and the MATLAB original with HEAD acoustics ArtemiS v17.1 for the two calibration signals and a 30 s binaural street recording.
  - **Checked by the maintainer of LISQM:** In personal use, Zhenxian LI found its results in very good agreement with those of HEAD acoustics ArtemiS SUITE. This is a personal check, not a published comparison.
- [refmap-psychoacoustics](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/refmap-psychoacoustics.html), ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.): compared with ArtemiS SUITE (HEAD acoustics)
  - MATLAB and Python verified against HEAD acoustics ArtemiS v17.1 for a 1 kHz tone at 40 dB SPL, a 1 kHz tone amplitude-modulated at 70 Hz at 60 dB SPL and a 30 s binaural street recording.
  - The audio and reference results are on Zenodo (doi:10.5281/zenodo.18849587).
- [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/metasona.html), ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.): compared with **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** (its source)
  - Ported or adapted from **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)**. It was compared with the code it was ported from, which checks the port only.
  - The project says that detailed validation and reference comparisons are kept outside the repository; the results are not published.
- [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html), ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.): standard or paper data (calibration signal only; outside the allowed adjustment)
  - Checked at the calibration signal only, where it gives 0.9843 sone_HMS (−1.55 %).
- [Mosqito.NET](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito-net.html), ECMA-418-2:2022 (2nd ed.): compared with **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)** (its source)
  - Ported or adapted from **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)**. It was compared with the code it was ported from, which checks the port only.
  - Every public function is compared with the output of Python MoSQITo for seven WAV files (three of them ISO 532-1 test signals), within 1 % (0.5 dB for levels); MoSQITo's unit tests are ported too.
- [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/pysqat.html) (via sottek-hearing-model), ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.): compared with **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** (also ported from [refmap-psychoacoustics](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/refmap-psychoacoustics.html))
  - Code ported from the same source is expected to agree, so that comparison is not an independent check.
  - Compared by `validation/FINAL_VAL.py` with the bundled SQAT v1.3 MATLAB code, which follows ECMA-418-2:2024 (3rd edition), so the comparison crosses editions.
- [MoSQITo-FDP](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito-fdp.html), ECMA-418-2:2020 (1st ed.): standard or paper data
  - Ported or adapted from **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)** (the author's own code).
  - Validation scripts compare the ear filter and model output with figures and values from ECMA-418-2 and ECMA-74 Annex F.

Not stated by PsychoBox.

## Before you compare numbers

Implementations of the same metric can give different numbers without either being wrong. Check these choices first.

- **Edition.** The four editions give different results; compare implementations of the same edition (see the table of editions).
- **Which loudness.** Clause 5 gives the hearing model's basic loudness; from the 2nd edition on, Clause 8 defines the loudness to report. MoSQITo and Mosqito.NET compute only the Clause 5 value, while the RefMap code and its ports (SQAT, sottek-hearing-model, MetaSona) compute the Clause 8 loudness.
- **Start of the signal.** The filters need time to settle, so overall values leave out the first 304 ms (Section 8.1.4 of the 2025 edition, as cited by SQAT, which enforces it).
- **Sample rate.** The model is defined at 48 kHz; other rates are resampled, and resamplers differ slightly.
- **Sound field and channels.** The outer- and middle-ear filter can be free frontal or, from the 3rd edition, diffuse, and two channels can be combined into one binaural value. Check both settings.

What the projects state:

- **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)**: Statistics take the nearest rank of the sorted time series, without interpolation (`get_exceeded_value`), and leave out the first `time_skip` seconds; the code enforces at least 304 ms (it cites ECMA-418-2:2025, Section 8.1.4).
- **[sottek-hearing-model](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sottek-hearing-model.html)**: Input at other sample rates is resampled to 48 kHz.
- [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/metasona.html): Expects calibrated sound pressure in pascals. The C functions require 48 kHz input; the Python interface resamples other rates to 48 kHz (SciPy `resample_poly`). `time_skip_s` (default 0 s) leaves out the start of the signal from the reported frames; the computation still runs over the whole signal. Time-varying results include every complete frame, labelled at frame centres, which differs from SQAT's handling of the last frame and of time stamps.

## References

1. ECMA-418-2:2020 (1st ed.). Psychoacoustic metrics for ITT equipment — Part 2 (models based on human perception). https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_1st_edition_december_2020.pdf
2. ECMA-418-2:2022 (2nd ed.). Psychoacoustic metrics for ITT equipment — Part 2 (models based on human perception). https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_2nd_edition_december_2022.pdf
3. ECMA-418-2:2024 (3rd ed.). Psychoacoustic metrics for ITT equipment — Part 2 (methods for describing human perception based on the Sottek Hearing Model). https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_3rd_edition_december_2024.pdf
4. ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.). Psychoacoustic metrics for ITT equipment — Part 2 (methods for describing human perception based on the Sottek Hearing Model). https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_4th_edition_june_2025.pdf

# Sharpness (DIN 45692, Aures, von Bismarck)

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/sharpness.html

**Quantity:** Sharpness · **Unit:** acum · **Also known as:** DIN 45692, acum, Zwicker sharpness, Aures sharpness, von Bismarck sharpness

Sharpness is the weighted first moment of specific loudness along the critical-band rate, with a weighting that emphasises high frequencies. DIN 45692:2009 standardises the weighting and a test procedure, using Zwicker specific loudness (ISO 532-1 / DIN 45631). Most implementations also offer the weightings of von Bismarck (1974) and Aures (1985).

The current edition is DIN 45692:2009. Open-source implementations of it: **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** (MATLAB; DIN 45692 weighting, plus von Bismarck and Aures options), **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)** (Python; weightings: DIN 45692, Aures, von Bismarck, Fastl), [refmap-psychoacoustics](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/refmap-psychoacoustics.html) (MATLAB, Python; DIN 45692 weighting applied to ECMA-418-2 loudness), [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/metasona.html) (C, Python; newly released, not yet seen to be widely used; from specific loudness), [Kirin Hypha](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/kirin-hypha.html) (Rust; newly released, not yet seen to be widely used; from the time-varying specific loudness; shown in the plug-in), [Mosqito.NET](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito-net.html) (C#; newly released, not yet seen to be widely used; weightings: DIN 45692, Aures, von Bismarck, Fastl), [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html) (Python; newly released, not yet seen to be widely used; also the informative Aures and von Bismarck variants), [PsychoacousticMetrics.jl](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psychoacousticmetrics-jl.html) (Julia; newly released, not yet seen to be widely used; weightings: DIN 45692 (default), Aures, von Bismarck, Fastl; from a ZwickerLoudness.jl result), [SoundPalette](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/soundpalette.html) (C++; newly released, not yet seen to be widely used; from time-averaged specific loudness), [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/pysqat.html) (Python; developing), and [PsychoacousticParametersMeasurer](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psychoacoustic-parameters-measurer.html) (Python; legacy, no commit since 2021-06). Implementations of earlier editions or related models: [AARAE](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/aarae.html) (MATLAB; Fastl & Zwicker (2007); from the specific loudness of `LoudnessCF`) and [Swift & Gee codes](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/rapid-loudness-sharpness.html) (MATLAB; legacy, no commit since 2020-01; Swift & Gee (2017); from Moore–Glasberg specific loudness, stationary and time-varying).

## How they were validated

As reported by each project; LISQM has not run the code. Two implementations that agree can still share the same error.

- **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)**, DIN 45692:2009: standard or paper data
  - Checked with the narrowband and broadband test signals of DIN 45692.
- **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)**, DIN 45692:2009: standard or paper data (outcome not stated)
  - Validation scripts use the DIN 45692 test signals; the documentation marks it as validated.
- [Kirin Hypha](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/kirin-hypha.html), DIN 45692:2009: compared with **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)** (its source)
  - Ported or adapted from **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)**. It was compared with the code it was ported from, which checks the port only.
  - Tests assert agreement with MoSQITo within 0.05 acum.
- [Mosqito.NET](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito-net.html), DIN 45692:2009: compared with **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)** (its source)
  - Ported or adapted from **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)**. It was compared with the code it was ported from, which checks the port only.
  - Every public function is compared with the output of Python MoSQITo for seven WAV files (three of them ISO 532-1 test signals), within 1 % (0.5 dB for levels); MoSQITo's unit tests are ported too.
- [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html), DIN 45692:2009: standard or paper data
  - Checked with the DIN 45692 reference signal and Tables A.2 and A.3.
- [PsychoacousticMetrics.jl](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psychoacousticmetrics-jl.html), DIN 45692:2009: standard or paper data; also compared with **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)**
  - Tested against all 41 reference signals of DIN 45692:2009 chapter 6 (21 narrowband, 20 broadband) within the standard's tolerance of ±max(5 %, 0.05 acum).
  - Cross-checked against MoSQITo for all four weightings.
  - Total loudness N is computed as the Riemann sum over the 240-bin specific loudness (`0.1 * sum`), not taken from `ZwickerResult.loudness` (see the `sharpness` docstring).
- [SoundPalette](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/soundpalette.html), DIN 45692:2009: compared with **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)**
  - Compared with MoSQITo 1.2.1 (tolerance ±5 %).
- [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/pysqat.html), DIN 45692:2009: compared with **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** (its source)
  - Ported or adapted from **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)**. It was compared with the code it was ported from, which checks the port only.
  - Compared with SQAT v1.3, run in MATLAB, by `validation/FINAL_VAL.py`; the generated reports are not committed.

Not stated by refmap-psychoacoustics, AARAE, MetaSona, Swift & Gee codes, PsychoacousticParametersMeasurer, PsychoBox, and Soundscapy.

## Project map

The lines of the project map for sharpness only (the whole map: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/map.md). Agreement between a project and the code it was ported or adapted from only checks the port.

### Ported or adapted from another project

- From **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)**: [Kirin Hypha](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/kirin-hypha.html) (DIN 45692:2009); [Mosqito.NET](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito-net.html) (DIN 45692:2009)
- From **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)**: [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/pysqat.html) (DIN 45692:2009)

### Used at run time

- [PsychoacousticMetrics.jl](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psychoacousticmetrics-jl.html) needs [ZwickerLoudness.jl](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/zwickerloudness-jl.html) (DIN 45692:2009)
- [PsychoBox](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psychobox.html) calls **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)** (DIN 45692:2009)
- [Soundscapy](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/soundscapy.html) calls **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)** (DIN 45692:2009)

### Results checked against another project

- [PsychoacousticMetrics.jl](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psychoacousticmetrics-jl.html) against **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)** (DIN 45692:2009)
- [SoundPalette](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/soundpalette.html) against **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)** (DIN 45692:2009)

### Same contributor

- **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** and [refmap-psychoacoustics](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/refmap-psychoacoustics.html) (Mike Lotinga)

On the map without a line, as no relation is recorded for them: [AARAE](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/aarae.html), [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/metasona.html), [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html), [PsychoacousticParametersMeasurer](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psychoacoustic-parameters-measurer.html), and [Swift & Gee codes](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/rapid-loudness-sharpness.html).

## Before you compare numbers

Implementations of the same metric can give different numbers without either being wrong. Check these choices first.

- **Weighting.** The DIN 45692, Aures and von Bismarck weightings give different values for the same sound, and Aures' weighting depends on loudness. Many tools offer several; check which one is used (RefMap's default is Aures).
- **Loudness input.** Sharpness is computed from Zwicker specific loudness, so the loudness choices (sound field, calibration, sample rate) carry over. Sharpness from another loudness model, such as ECMA-418-2 (RefMap) or Moore–Glasberg (Swift & Gee), is a different quantity.

What the projects state:

- **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)**: Statistics such as N5 take the nearest rank of the sorted time series, without interpolation (`get_exceeded_value`), and leave out the first `time_skip` seconds of the signal.
- [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/metasona.html): Expects calibrated sound pressure in pascals. The C functions require 48 kHz input; the Python interface resamples other rates to 48 kHz (SciPy `resample_poly`). `time_skip_s` (default 0 s) leaves out the start of the signal from the reported frames; the computation still runs over the whole signal. Time-varying results include every complete frame, labelled at frame centres, which differs from SQAT's handling of the last frame and of time stamps.
- [Swift & Gee codes](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/rapid-loudness-sharpness.html): The code works at 32 kHz; other rates are resampled with the Signal Processing Toolbox's `resample`.

## References

1. von Bismarck, G. (1974). Sharpness as an attribute of the timbre of steady sounds. *Acustica*, 30(3), 159–172. https://www.ingentaconnect.com/contentone/dav/aaua/1974/00000030/00000003/art00006
2. Aures, W. (1985). Berechnungsverfahren für den sensorischen Wohlklang beliebiger Schallsignale [A model for calculating the sensory euphony of various sounds]. *Acustica*, 59, 130–141.
3. Fastl, H., & Zwicker, E. (2007). *Psychoacoustics: Facts and models* (3rd ed.). Springer. https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-540-68888-4
4. DIN 45692:2009. Messtechnische Simulation der Hörempfindung Schärfe (Measurement technique for the simulation of the auditory sensation of sharpness). https://www.dinmedia.de/en/standard/din-45692/117635111
5. Swift, S. H., & Gee, K. L. (2017). Extending sharpness calculation for an alternative loudness metric input. *The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America*, 142(6), EL549. https://doi.org/10.1121/1.5016193

# Roughness, Daniel & Weber model

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/roughness-daniel-weber.html

**Quantity:** Roughness · **Unit:** asper · **Also known as:** Daniel and Weber roughness, Daniel & Weber 1997, Aures roughness, asper

Roughness from the model of Daniel & Weber (1997), an optimised version of Aures's (1985) model. It is not standardised, and the paper leaves details open (filter bank, calibration, framing), so implementations can give different values for the same signal.

There is no standard; the reference model is Daniel & Weber (1997). Open-source implementations of it: **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** (MATLAB), **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)** (Python), [AARAE](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/aarae.html) (MATLAB), [ITA-Toolbox](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/ita-toolbox.html) (MATLAB), [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/metasona.html) (C, Python; newly released, not yet seen to be widely used), [Mosqito.NET](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito-net.html) (C#; newly released, not yet seen to be widely used), [PsychoacousticMetrics.jl](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psychoacousticmetrics-jl.html) (Julia; newly released, not yet seen to be widely used), [SoundPalette](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/soundpalette.html) (C++; newly released, not yet seen to be widely used), [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/pysqat.html) (Python; developing), and [PsySound3](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psysound3.html) (MATLAB; legacy, no commit since 2015-03).

SQAT rewrote its implementation in September 2026 (PR #65). It builds on Alejandro Osses's code and was corrected against revised code that Dik Hermes provided in 2025, which changes results compared with SQAT v1.3 and earlier.

## Editions and who implements them

| Date | Edition | Status | What changed | Implemented by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1997 | [Daniel & Weber (1997)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/standards.html#ref-daniel-weber-1997) | published | Reference model. | **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)**, **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)**, [AARAE](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/aarae.html), [ITA-Toolbox](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/ita-toolbox.html), [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/metasona.html), [Mosqito.NET](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito-net.html), [PsychoacousticMetrics.jl](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psychoacousticmetrics-jl.html), [SoundPalette](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/soundpalette.html), [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/pysqat.html), [PsySound3](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psysound3.html) |
| 1985 | [Aures (1985a)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/standards.html#ref-aures-1985-roughness) | published | Earlier model that Daniel & Weber optimised. | — |

## Implementations

| Project | Language | Edition | Functions | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** | MATLAB | [Daniel & Weber (1997)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/standards.html#ref-daniel-weber-1997) (since v1.0) | `Roughness_Daniel1997`, `Roughness_Daniel1997_from_wavfile` | standard or paper data | The releases do not allow commercial use; the default branch has another licence. The v1.x code is AARAE's `roughnessDW.m` (Dik Hermes's code), adapted and verified for SQAT in 2023. Rewritten on `main` (PR #65, 2026-09-08) after revised code from Dik Hermes: 63 of 119 validation values go up and 56 down (largest change 0.155 asper). |
| **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)** | Python | [Daniel & Weber (1997)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/standards.html#ref-daniel-weber-1997) (since 1.0.0) | `roughness_dw`, `roughness_dw_freq` | standard or paper data (outcome not stated) | — |
| [AARAE](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/aarae.html) | MATLAB | [Daniel & Weber (1997)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/standards.html#ref-daniel-weber-1997) | `RoughnessDW` | not stated | Ported from PsySound3's `@RoughnessDW` by Ella Manor and Densil Cabrera (2015). |
| [ITA-Toolbox](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/ita-toolbox.html) | MATLAB | [Daniel & Weber (1997)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/standards.html#ref-daniel-weber-1997) | `ita_roughness_daniel` | standard or paper data (a code comment only) | Uses sub-functions written by Martin Klemenz in 2000 (`external_packages/roughness_daniel`). |
| [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/metasona.html) | C, Python | [Daniel & Weber (1997)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/standards.html#ref-daniel-weber-1997) (since 0.1.0) | `roughness_daniel_weber` | compared with SQAT (its source) | Newly released project, not yet seen to be widely used. Follows SQAT revision `e6228b78`, which includes SQAT's September 2026 rewrite but not its later fix to the Terhardt filter bank (PR #77). |
| [Mosqito.NET](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito-net.html) | C# | [Daniel & Weber (1997)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/standards.html#ref-daniel-weber-1997) | `Sq.RoughnessDw`, `Sq.RoughnessDwFreq` | compared with MoSQITo (its source) | Newly released project, not yet seen to be widely used. |
| [PsychoacousticMetrics.jl](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psychoacousticmetrics-jl.html) | Julia | [Daniel & Weber (1997)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/standards.html#ref-daniel-weber-1997) (since 0.2.0) | `roughness_dw` | standard or paper data; also compared with MoSQITo (its source) | Newly released project, not yet seen to be widely used. |
| [SoundPalette](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/soundpalette.html) | C++ | [Daniel & Weber (1997)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/standards.html#ref-daniel-weber-1997) (since v0.5.0) | `sp::compute_psycho` | compared with MoSQITo | Newly released project, not yet seen to be widely used. A source-available licence, not an open-source one: some uses are not allowed. |
| [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/pysqat.html) | Python | [Daniel & Weber (1997)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/standards.html#ref-daniel-weber-1997) | `Roughness_Daniel1997` | compared with SQAT (its source) | Developing project: no publication or documented use by others. No licence file: by default, copying, changing or sharing the code needs the author's permission. Follows SQAT v1.3, before SQAT's September 2026 rewrite. |
| [PsySound3](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psysound3.html) | MATLAB | [Daniel & Weber (1997)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/standards.html#ref-daniel-weber-1997) | `@RoughnessDW` | not stated | Legacy project, no longer maintained. No licence file: by default, copying, changing or sharing the code needs the author's permission. Adapted for PsySound3 by Matt Flax (2006), with changes by Farhan Rizwi (2007). AARAE's `RoughnessDW.m` is a port of this analyser. |

Also available through tools that call one of these implementations: [PsychoBox](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psychobox.html) (via MoSQITo, Daniel & Weber (1997)) and [Soundscapy](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/soundscapy.html) (via MoSQITo, Daniel & Weber (1997)).

**See also:** [Roughness from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/roughness-ecma-418-2.html)

## How they were validated

As reported by each project; LISQM has not run the code. Two implementations that agree can still share the same error.

- **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)**, Daniel & Weber (1997): standard or paper data
  - Ported or adapted from [AARAE](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/aarae.html).
  - Checked against amplitude- and frequency-modulation dependences from the literature.
- **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)**, Daniel & Weber (1997): standard or paper data (outcome not stated)
  - The documentation marks it as validated against reference data.
- [AARAE](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/aarae.html), Daniel & Weber (1997): not stated
  - Ported or adapted from [PsySound3](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psysound3.html) (the author's own code).
- [ITA-Toolbox](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/ita-toolbox.html), Daniel & Weber (1997): standard or paper data (a code comment only)
  - A code comment says that after major bug fixes the values "more or less match those of the paper by Daniel"; no test or comparison script is included.
- [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/metasona.html), Daniel & Weber (1997): compared with **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** (its source)
  - Ported or adapted from **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** and **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)**. It was compared with the code it was ported from, which checks the port only.
  - The project says that detailed validation and reference comparisons are kept outside the repository; the results are not published.
  - The API documentation calls the function experimental and says normative validation remains open.
- [Mosqito.NET](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito-net.html), Daniel & Weber (1997): compared with **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)** (its source)
  - Ported or adapted from **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)**. It was compared with the code it was ported from, which checks the port only.
  - Every public function is compared with the output of Python MoSQITo for seven WAV files (three of them ISO 532-1 test signals), within 1 % (0.5 dB for levels); MoSQITo's unit tests are ported too.
- [PsychoacousticMetrics.jl](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psychoacousticmetrics-jl.html), Daniel & Weber (1997): standard or paper data; also compared with **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)** (its source)
  - Ported or adapted from **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)**. It was compared with the code it was ported from, which checks the port only.
  - Tested against the Zwicker & Fastl reference curves on MoSQITo's validation grid (7 carrier × 11 modulation frequencies) within ±0.1 asper, and cross-checked against MoSQITo's `roughness_dw` on identical signals.
  - Five points at a 2 kHz carrier miss the ±0.1 asper gate. MoSQITo misses them by the same amount (and overshoots Daniel & Weber's own curve there by 15–31 %), so these five are checked for agreement with MoSQITo to 5e-3 asper instead.
  - Against the Daniel & Weber curves themselves, 63 of the 77 grid points are within 30 % of the reference (reported, not gated).
- [SoundPalette](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/soundpalette.html), Daniel & Weber (1997): compared with **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)**
  - Compared with MoSQITo 1.2.1 with a wider tolerance (±15 %); the README notes that published Daniel & Weber implementations differ by about 10–20 %.
- [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/pysqat.html), Daniel & Weber (1997): compared with **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** (its source)
  - Ported or adapted from **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)**. It was compared with the code it was ported from, which checks the port only.
  - Compared with SQAT v1.3, run in MATLAB, by `validation/FINAL_VAL.py`; the generated reports are not committed.

Not stated by PsySound3, PsychoBox, and Soundscapy.

## Project map

The lines of the project map for roughness (Daniel & Weber) only (the whole map: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/map.md). Agreement between a project and the code it was ported or adapted from only checks the port.

### Ported or adapted from another project

- From [AARAE](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/aarae.html): **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** (Daniel & Weber (1997))
- From **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)**: [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/metasona.html) (Daniel & Weber (1997)); [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/pysqat.html) (Daniel & Weber (1997))
- From **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)**: [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/metasona.html) (Daniel & Weber (1997)); [Mosqito.NET](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito-net.html) (Daniel & Weber (1997)); [PsychoacousticMetrics.jl](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psychoacousticmetrics-jl.html) (Daniel & Weber (1997))

### The author's own code

- From [PsySound3](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psysound3.html) (Densil Cabrera): [AARAE](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/aarae.html) (Daniel & Weber (1997))

### Used at run time

- [PsychoBox](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psychobox.html) calls **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)** (Daniel & Weber (1997))
- [Soundscapy](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/soundscapy.html) calls **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)** (Daniel & Weber (1997))

### Results checked against another project

- [SoundPalette](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/soundpalette.html) against **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)** (Daniel & Weber (1997))

On the map without a line, as no relation is recorded for them: [ITA-Toolbox](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/ita-toolbox.html).

## Before you compare numbers

Implementations of the same metric can give different numbers without either being wrong. Check these choices first.

- **Frames.** The model works on 200 ms frames. Implementations differ in the hop between frames and in whether the last complete frame is reported, which changes time series and their percentiles.
- **Code lineage.** SQAT's code (after Dik Hermes) and MoSQITo's differ in details, and ports follow one or the other; PsychoacousticMetrics.jl, which follows MoSQITo, says the two place the weighting g(z_i) differently.
- **Version.** SQAT rewrote its roughness on `main` in September 2026, so SQAT v1.3, `main` and code ported from either give different values.

What the projects state:

- **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)**: Statistics such as N5 take the nearest rank of the sorted time series, without interpolation (`get_exceeded_value`), and leave out the first `time_skip` seconds of the signal.
- [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/metasona.html): Expects calibrated sound pressure in pascals. The C functions require 48 kHz input; the Python interface resamples other rates to 48 kHz (SciPy `resample_poly`). `time_skip_s` (default 0 s) leaves out the start of the signal from the reported frames; the computation still runs over the whole signal. Time-varying results include every complete frame, labelled at frame centres, which differs from SQAT's handling of the last frame and of time stamps.

## References

1. Aures, W. (1985). Ein Berechnungsverfahren der Rauhigkeit [A procedure for calculating auditory roughness]. *Acustica*, 58, 268–281.
2. Daniel, P., & Weber, R. (1997). Psychoacoustical roughness: Implementation of an optimized model. *Acta Acustica united with Acustica*, 83(1), 113–123.


---

# Roughness from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/roughness-ecma-418-2.html

**Quantity:** Roughness · **Unit:** asper_HMS · **Also known as:** ECMA-418-2 roughness, asper_HMS, Sottek roughness, SHM roughness

Roughness from the Sottek Hearing Model, Clause 7 of ECMA-418-2. The 2nd edition (2022) added an optional entropy weighting for cases where rotational speed is measured; the 3rd edition (2024) adapted zero-padding and segmentation, and its refinements were mainly to roughness.

The current edition is ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.). Open-source implementations of it: **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** (MATLAB; unreleased), **[sottek-hearing-model](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sottek-hearing-model.html)** (Python; with combined binaural output), [refmap-psychoacoustics](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/refmap-psychoacoustics.html) (MATLAB, Python), [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/metasona.html) (C, Python; newly released, not yet seen to be widely used; mono or stereo; optional entropy weighting not applied), and [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html) (Python; newly released, not yet seen to be widely used; mono only; no entropy weighting). Implementations of earlier editions or related models: **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** (MATLAB; ECMA-418-2:2024 (3rd ed.); with binaural combination), **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)** (Python; ECMA-418-2:2022 (2nd ed.)), and [Mosqito.NET](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito-net.html) (C#; newly released, not yet seen to be widely used; ECMA-418-2:2022 (2nd ed.)).

## Editions and who implements them

| Date | Edition | Status | What changed | Implemented by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2025-06 | [ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_4th_edition_june_2025.pdf) | current | Hearing-model and conformance updates (48 kHz sampling). | **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** (unreleased), **[sottek-hearing-model](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sottek-hearing-model.html)**, [refmap-psychoacoustics](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/refmap-psychoacoustics.html), [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/metasona.html), [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html) |
| 2024-12 | [ECMA-418-2:2024 (3rd ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_3rd_edition_december_2024.pdf) | superseded | Zero-padding and segmentation adapted; refinements mainly to roughness. | **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** |
| 2022-12 | [ECMA-418-2:2022 (2nd ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_2nd_edition_december_2022.pdf) | superseded | Refined calculation; optional entropy-weighted roughness. | **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)**, [Mosqito.NET](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito-net.html) |
| 2020-12 | [ECMA-418-2:2020 (1st ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_1st_edition_december_2020.pdf) | superseded | Clause 7 roughness. | — |

| **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** | MATLAB | [ECMA-418-2:2024 (3rd ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_3rd_edition_december_2024.pdf) (with binaural combination; since v1.3) | `Roughness_ECMA418_2` | compared with ArtemiS SUITE (HEAD acoustics) | The releases do not allow commercial use; the default branch has another licence. |

Uses the standard's 20 ms grid and nominal calibration factor, where SQAT uses a slightly adjusted calibration. |
| [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html) | Python | [ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_4th_edition_june_2025.pdf) (mono only; no entropy weighting; since 3.1.0) | `roughness_ecma` | standard or paper data (calibration signal only) | Newly released project, not yet seen to be widely used. |
| [Mosqito.NET](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito-net.html) | C# | [ECMA-418-2:2022 (2nd ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_2nd_edition_december_2022.pdf) | `Sq.RoughnessEcma` | compared with MoSQITo (its source) | Newly released project, not yet seen to be widely used. |

Also available through tools that call one of these implementations: [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/pysqat.html) (via sottek-hearing-model, ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.)) and [PsychoBox](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psychobox.html) (via MoSQITo, ECMA-418-2:2022 (2nd ed.)).

**See also:** [Roughness, Daniel & Weber model](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/roughness-daniel-weber.html), [Loudness from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-ecma-418-2.html)

## How they were validated

As reported by each project; LISQM has not run the code. Two implementations that agree can still share the same error.

- **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)**, ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.): compared with ArtemiS SUITE (HEAD acoustics)
  - Ported or adapted from [refmap-psychoacoustics](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/refmap-psychoacoustics.html) (the author's own code).
  - On `main`, checked for the 4th edition for the dependence of the roughness of AM tones on modulation frequency, and against reference results from HEAD acoustics ArtemiS SUITE 17.1 (named in the source of SQAT's validation page) for a binaural recording of a train station.
- **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)**, ECMA-418-2:2024 (3rd ed.): compared with ArtemiS SUITE (HEAD acoustics)
  - Ported or adapted from [refmap-psychoacoustics](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/refmap-psychoacoustics.html) (the author's own code).
  - Checked for the dependence of the roughness of AM tones on modulation frequency, and against reference results from HEAD acoustics ArtemiS SUITE 15.7 (named in the source of SQAT's validation page) for a binaural recording of a train station.
- **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)**, ECMA-418-2:2022 (2nd ed.): standard or paper data; also compared with ArtemiS SUITE (HEAD acoustics)
  - A unit test checks the standard's reference signal (1 kHz tone, 100 % amplitude-modulated at 70 Hz, 60 dB), which should give 1 asper, within ±0.1 asper.
  - A validation script compares the specific roughness of amplitude-modulated tones (carriers from 125 Hz to 4 kHz, 65 dB) with values computed in HEAD acoustics ArtemiS SUITE, within ±10 %.
- **[sottek-hearing-model](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sottek-hearing-model.html)**, ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.): standard or paper data (reference signal and one recording); also compared with ArtemiS SUITE (HEAD acoustics)
  - Ported or adapted from [refmap-psychoacoustics](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/refmap-psychoacoustics.html) (the author's own code).
  - Unit tests check the standard's reference signal, which should give 1 asper_HMS, at 48 and 44.1 kHz.
  - RefMap's verification against ArtemiS v17.1, as for loudness.
  - **Checked by the maintainer of LISQM:** In personal use, Zhenxian LI found its results in very good agreement with those of HEAD acoustics ArtemiS SUITE. This is a personal check, not a published comparison.
- [refmap-psychoacoustics](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/refmap-psychoacoustics.html), ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.): compared with ArtemiS SUITE (HEAD acoustics)
  - Verified against HEAD acoustics ArtemiS v17.1 with the same three signals as loudness.
- [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/metasona.html), ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.): compared with **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** (its source)
  - Ported or adapted from **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)**. It was compared with the code it was ported from, which checks the port only.
  - The project says that detailed validation and reference comparisons are kept outside the repository; the results are not published.
- [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html), ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.): standard or paper data (calibration signal only)
  - Checked at the calibration signal only.
- [Mosqito.NET](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito-net.html), ECMA-418-2:2022 (2nd ed.): compared with **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)** (its source)
  - Ported or adapted from **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)**. It was compared with the code it was ported from, which checks the port only.
  - Every public function is compared with the output of Python MoSQITo for seven WAV files (three of them ISO 532-1 test signals), within 1 % (0.5 dB for levels); MoSQITo's unit tests are ported too.
- [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/pysqat.html) (via sottek-hearing-model), ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.): compared with **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** (also ported from [refmap-psychoacoustics](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/refmap-psychoacoustics.html))
  - Code ported from the same source is expected to agree, so that comparison is not an independent check.
  - Compared by `validation/FINAL_VAL.py` with the bundled SQAT v1.3 MATLAB code, which follows ECMA-418-2:2024 (3rd edition), so the comparison crosses editions.

Not stated by PsychoBox.

On the map without a line, as no relation is recorded for them: [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html).

## Before you compare numbers

Implementations of the same metric can give different numbers without either being wrong. Check these choices first.

- **Edition.** Compare implementations of the same edition: MoSQITo, Mosqito.NET and tools that call MoSQITo follow the 2nd edition, the others the 3rd or 4th.
- **Overall value.** The single value is the 90th percentile of the time-dependent roughness after the first 320 ms. NumPy's percentile (sottek-hearing-model) and MATLAB's `prctile` (RefMap, SQAT) interpolate differently, so single values can differ slightly.
- **Calibration and time grid.** SQAT uses a slightly adjusted calibration factor and a time grid that ends at the signal duration; MetaSona uses the standard's nominal factor (0.0180685) and its 20 ms grid.
- **Binaural.** Two channels can be combined into one binaural value; per-channel and combined values differ.

What the projects state:

- **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)**: The single value is the 90th percentile from MATLAB's `prctile`, which interpolates; the other statistics take the nearest rank (`get_exceeded_value`). The first `time_skip` seconds are left out; the code enforces at least 320 ms (it cites ECMA-418-2:2025, Section 7.1.8).
- **[sottek-hearing-model](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sottek-hearing-model.html)**: Input at other sample rates is resampled to 48 kHz. Overall roughness and fluctuation strength are 90th percentiles computed with NumPy (linear interpolation, Hyndman–Fan type 7). The MATLAB code it was translated from uses `prctile`, which interpolates differently, so single values can differ slightly from RefMap and SQAT.
- [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/metasona.html): Expects calibrated sound pressure in pascals. The C functions require 48 kHz input; the Python interface resamples other rates to 48 kHz (SciPy `resample_poly`). `time_skip_s` (default 0 s) leaves out the start of the signal from the reported frames; the computation still runs over the whole signal. Time-varying results include every complete frame, labelled at frame centres, which differs from SQAT's handling of the last frame and of time stamps.
- [Mosqito.NET](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito-net.html): Time-varying loudness and ECMA-418-2 roughness resample input at any other rate to 48 kHz, and stationary loudness resamples rates below 48 kHz; MoSQITo rejects rates above 48 kHz for time-varying loudness.

## References

1. ECMA-418-2:2020 (1st ed.). Psychoacoustic metrics for ITT equipment — Part 2 (models based on human perception). https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_1st_edition_december_2020.pdf
2. ECMA-418-2:2022 (2nd ed.). Psychoacoustic metrics for ITT equipment — Part 2 (models based on human perception). https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_2nd_edition_december_2022.pdf
3. ECMA-418-2:2024 (3rd ed.). Psychoacoustic metrics for ITT equipment — Part 2 (methods for describing human perception based on the Sottek Hearing Model). https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_3rd_edition_december_2024.pdf
4. ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.). Psychoacoustic metrics for ITT equipment — Part 2 (methods for describing human perception based on the Sottek Hearing Model). https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_4th_edition_june_2025.pdf

# Roughness, DIN 38455

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/roughness-din-38455.html

**Quantity:** Roughness · **Unit:** asper · **Also known as:** DIN 38455, Rauigkeit, German roughness standard

DIN 38455:2024 is the first German standard for calculating roughness. Its text is not freely available, and the model it specifies could not be confirmed from public sources; a hearing-model roughness was proposed for DIN standardisation by Sottek & Becker (2019).

The current edition is DIN 38455:2024. No open-source implementation of it has been found.

## Editions and who implements them

| Date | Edition | Status | What changed | Implemented by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2024-11 | [DIN 38455:2024](https://www.dinmedia.de/en/standard/din-38455/376186532) | current | First edition. | — |

## Implementations

No open-source implementation has been found yet. If you know one, please [open an issue](https://github.com/ZhenxianLi/LISQM/issues/new/choose).

**See also:** [Roughness from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/roughness-ecma-418-2.html), [Roughness, Daniel & Weber model](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/roughness-daniel-weber.html)

## References

1. DIN 38455:2024. Berechnung der Hörempfindung Rauigkeit (Calculation of the auditory sensation of roughness). https://www.dinmedia.de/en/standard/din-38455/376186532

# Fluctuation strength, Osses et al. model and Fastl & Zwicker formula

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/fluctuation-strength-osses.html

**Quantity:** Fluctuation strength · **Unit:** vacil · **Also known as:** fluctuation strength, vacil, Osses 2016, Fastl and Zwicker fluctuation strength

Fluctuation strength describes slow modulation around 4 Hz. Osses, García & Kohlrausch (2016) proposed a signal-based model; Fastl & Zwicker give a closed-form expression for modulated tones and noises. Neither is standardised. ECMA-418-2:2025 added a hearing-model method, listed on its own page.

There is no standard; the reference model is Osses et al. (2016). Open-source implementations of it: **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** (MATLAB), [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html) (Python; newly released, not yet seen to be widely used), [PsychoacousticMetrics.jl](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psychoacousticmetrics-jl.html) (Julia; newly released, not yet seen to be widely used), [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/pysqat.html) (Python; developing), and [fluctuation-strength-TUe](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/fluctuation-strength-tue.html) (MATLAB; legacy, no commit since 2020-01). Implementations of earlier editions or related models: [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html) (Python; newly released, not yet seen to be widely used; Fastl & Zwicker (2007); closed-form expression for amplitude-modulated noise) and [PsychoacousticParametersMeasurer](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psychoacoustic-parameters-measurer.html) (Python; legacy, no commit since 2021-06; Fastl & Zwicker (2007); Zwicker & Fastl formula).

## Editions and who implements them

| Date | Edition | Status | What changed | Implemented by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2016 | [Osses et al. (2016)](https://doi.org/10.1121/2.0000410) | published | Signal-based model. | **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)**, [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html), [PsychoacousticMetrics.jl](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psychoacousticmetrics-jl.html), [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/pysqat.html), [fluctuation-strength-TUe](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/fluctuation-strength-tue.html) |
| 2007 | [Fastl & Zwicker (2007)](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-540-68888-4) | published | Closed-form expression for amplitude- and frequency-modulated sounds. | [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html), [PsychoacousticParametersMeasurer](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psychoacoustic-parameters-measurer.html) |
