## How they were validated

As reported by each project; LISQM has not run the code. Two implementations that agree can still share the same error.

- **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)**, Osses et al. (2016): standard or paper data
  - Ported or adapted from [fluctuation-strength-TUe](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/fluctuation-strength-tue.html) (the author's own code).
  - Checked against amplitude- and frequency-modulation dependences from the literature.
- [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html), Osses et al. (2016): standard or paper data; also compared with **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)**
  - Compared with the literature values in Table 1 of Osses et al. (2016): for amplitude-modulated 70 dB tones the Pearson correlation is about 0.98, within a factor of about 2.1 at every point. SQAT's `FluctuationStrength_Osses2016` was consulted as a numeric reference for the shape of the sweep.
  - Validated for amplitude modulation only; a steady 1 kHz tone reads about 0.09 vacil.
- [PsychoacousticMetrics.jl](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psychoacousticmetrics-jl.html), Osses et al. (2016): reference code: **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)**
  - Cross-checked against SQAT's `FluctuationStrength_Osses2016`, run under Octave, on identical signals: 26 cases, including all 18 points of Fastl & Zwicker's AM/FM reference grid (Osses 2018 thesis, Table B.1), each reproduced to a relative tolerance of 1e-6 (measured 3e-9).
  - The grid stimuli are synthesised following the Osses et al. (2016) validation files that SQAT's own validation reads; the tests also check that each synthetic stimulus gives the value SQAT gives on the real file (tones to 5e-3, noise to 25 % across random draws).
  - Against the published curves, 11 of the 18 points are within 30 %, and exactly those 11 are gated. The other seven are misses of the reference model itself (FM tones with a modulation frequency above 4 Hz overestimated three- to fourfold, thesis §B.4.1; the shoulder and tail points of AM tones and noise), which SQAT's own validation figures also show.
- [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html), Fastl & Zwicker (2007): standard or paper data
  - A conformance row checks Eq. (10.2) of Fastl & Zwicker for amplitude-modulated broadband noise.
- [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/pysqat.html), Osses et al. (2016): compared with **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** (its source)
  - Ported or adapted from **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)**. It was compared with the code it was ported from, which checks the port only.
  - Compared with SQAT v1.3, run in MATLAB, by `validation/FINAL_VAL.py`; the generated reports are not committed.
- [fluctuation-strength-TUe](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/fluctuation-strength-tue.html), Osses et al. (2016): standard or paper data
  - `demos/demo_osses2016a.m` reproduces the figures of the paper with the included stimuli (AM and FM tones, AM noise and excerpts of real sounds).

Not stated by PsychoacousticParametersMeasurer.

## Project map

The lines of the project map for fluctuation strength (Osses et al.) only (the whole map: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/map.md). Agreement between a project and the code it was ported or adapted from only checks the port.

### Ported or adapted from another project

- From **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)**: [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/pysqat.html) (Osses et al. (2016))

### The author's own code

- From [fluctuation-strength-TUe](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/fluctuation-strength-tue.html) (Alejandro Osses): **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** (Osses et al. (2016))

### Results checked against another project

- [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html) against **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** (Osses et al. (2016))
- [PsychoacousticMetrics.jl](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psychoacousticmetrics-jl.html) against **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** (Osses et al. (2016))

On the map without a line, as no relation is recorded for them: [PsychoacousticParametersMeasurer](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psychoacoustic-parameters-measurer.html).

## Before you compare numbers

Implementations of the same metric can give different numbers without either being wrong. Check these choices first.

- **Sample rate.** The model's envelope filters exist for 44.1 and 48 kHz: SQAT resamples other rates, PsychoacousticMetrics.jl rejects them.
- **Steady sounds.** The model is meant for modulated sounds; a steady tone does not give exactly zero (phonometry reports about 0.09 vacil for a 1 kHz tone).

What the projects state:

- **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)**: Statistics such as N5 take the nearest rank of the sorted time series, without interpolation (`get_exceeded_value`), and leave out the first `time_skip` seconds of the signal.
- [PsychoacousticMetrics.jl](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psychoacousticmetrics-jl.html): Needs audio at 44.1 or 48 kHz (an error otherwise); SQAT resamples other rates itself.

## References

1. Fastl, H., & Zwicker, E. (2007). *Psychoacoustics: Facts and models* (3rd ed.). Springer. https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-540-68888-4
2. Osses Vecchi, A., García León, R., & Kohlrausch, A. (2016). Modelling the sensation of fluctuation strength. *Proceedings of Meetings on Acoustics*, 28, 050005. https://doi.org/10.1121/2.0000410

# Fluctuation strength from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/fluctuation-strength-ecma-418-2.html

**Quantity:** Fluctuation strength · **Unit:** vacil_HMS · **Also known as:** ECMA-418-2 fluctuation strength, vacil_HMS, Sottek fluctuation strength

Fluctuation strength from the Sottek Hearing Model, new in the 4th edition of ECMA-418-2 (June 2025, Clause 9). It uses high-resolution spectral analysis for modulation rates of about 0.25 to 20 Hz.

The current edition is ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.). Open-source implementations of it: **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** (MATLAB; PR, not merged), **[sottek-hearing-model](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sottek-hearing-model.html)** (Python; needs at least 1.37 s of signal; binaural option; unreleased), and [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html) (Python; newly released, not yet seen to be widely used; mono only). So far, only newly released projects, not yet seen to be widely used in the community, have released an implementation of it. Check their validation before relying on them.

## Editions and who implements them

| Date | Edition | Status | What changed | Implemented by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2025-06 | [ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_4th_edition_june_2025.pdf) | current | New Clause 9. | **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** (PR), **[sottek-hearing-model](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sottek-hearing-model.html)** (unreleased), [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html) |

## Implementations

| Project | Language | Edition | Functions | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** | MATLAB | [ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_4th_edition_june_2025.pdf) | `FluctuationStrength_ECMA418_2` | not stated | PR (https://github.com/ggrecow/SQAT/pull/78). Open pull request since 2026-09-17. |
| **[sottek-hearing-model](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sottek-hearing-model.html)** | Python | [ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_4th_edition_june_2025.pdf) (needs at least 1.37 s of signal; binaural option) | `shm_fluctuation_ecma` | compared with refmap-psychoacoustics (its source) and ArtemiS SUITE (HEAD acoustics) | Unreleased. Merged on 2026-09-18. Five departures from the printed text are documented (four equations and one interpretation of Section 9.1.8). |
| [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html) | Python | [ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_4th_edition_june_2025.pdf) (mono only; since 3.3.0) | `fluctuation_strength_ecma` | standard or paper data (calibration signal only) | Newly released project, not yet seen to be widely used. Misprints found in Clause 9 are listed in the project's errata. |

**See also:** [Fluctuation strength, Osses et al. model and Fastl & Zwicker formula](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/fluctuation-strength-osses.html), [Loudness from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-ecma-418-2.html)

## How they were validated

As reported by each project; LISQM has not run the code. Two implementations that agree can still share the same error.

- **[sottek-hearing-model](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sottek-hearing-model.html)**, ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.): compared with [refmap-psychoacoustics](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/refmap-psychoacoustics.html) (its source) and ArtemiS SUITE (HEAD acoustics)
  - Ported or adapted from [refmap-psychoacoustics](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/refmap-psychoacoustics.html) (the author's own code). It was compared with the code it was ported from, which checks the port only.
  - A draft report (18 September 2026) compares it with `acousticSHMFluctuation.m`, the MATLAB code it was translated from: equal to floating-point precision on the synthetic signals and on one channel of each recording, with a small difference in a short time window on the other channel.
  - Against HEAD acoustics ArtemiS SUITE v17: 0.994 against 1.003 vacil_HMS for the calibration signal (the standard's target is 1.0), −8 % to +12 % for the overall values of three binaural recordings, and correlations of 0.91 to 0.998 for the time-dependent values.
  - **Checked by the maintainer of LISQM:** In personal use, Zhenxian LI found its results in very good agreement with those of HEAD acoustics ArtemiS SUITE. This is a personal check, not a published comparison.
- [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html), ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.): standard or paper data (calibration signal only)
  - Checked at the calibration signal only (0.993 vacil_HMS).

Not stated by SQAT.

## Project map

The lines of the project map for Sottek Hearing Model fluctuation strength only (the whole map: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/map.md). Agreement between a project and the code it was ported or adapted from only checks the port.

### The author's own code

- From [refmap-psychoacoustics](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/refmap-psychoacoustics.html) (Mike Lotinga): **[sottek-hearing-model](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sottek-hearing-model.html)** (ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.))

### Same contributor

- **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** and **[sottek-hearing-model](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sottek-hearing-model.html)** (Mike Lotinga)

On the map without a line, as no relation is recorded for them: [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html).

## Before you compare numbers

Implementations of the same metric can give different numbers without either being wrong. Check these choices first.

- **Overall value.** The single value is a 90th percentile of the time-dependent values after the filters have settled. NumPy (sottek-hearing-model) and MATLAB's `prctile` interpolate differently, by at most 0.0005 vacil_HMS on sottek-hearing-model's test signals.
- **Interpretation.** Implementers report misprints and open questions in Clause 9 of the 2025 edition (phonometry's errata, sottek-hearing-model's documented departures), so implementations can differ until they are resolved.

What the projects state:

- **[sottek-hearing-model](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sottek-hearing-model.html)**: Input at other sample rates is resampled to 48 kHz. Overall roughness and fluctuation strength are 90th percentiles computed with NumPy (linear interpolation, Hyndman–Fan type 7). The MATLAB code it was translated from uses `prctile`, which interpolates differently, so single values can differ slightly from RefMap and SQAT.

## References

1. ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.). Psychoacoustic metrics for ITT equipment — Part 2 (methods for describing human perception based on the Sottek Hearing Model). https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_4th_edition_june_2025.pdf

# Tonality, Aures/Terhardt model

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tonality-aures.html

**Quantity:** Tonality · **Unit:** t.u. · **Also known as:** Aures tonality, Terhardt tonality, tonality units, t.u., sensory euphony

Tonality from Aures (1985): tonal components are extracted with the method of Terhardt, Stoll & Seewann (1982), weighted, and related to the loudness of the whole sound. Not standardised.

There is no standard; the reference model is Aures (1985b). Open-source implementations of it: **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** (MATLAB), **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)** (Python; PR, not merged), [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/metasona.html) (C, Python; newly released, not yet seen to be widely used), and [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/pysqat.html) (Python; developing).

SQAT corrected several issues in September 2026 (for example, the level excess of only one tonal component, the last positive one, entered the result, combined with the first component's frequency and bandwidth), which changes results compared with SQAT v1.3 and earlier.

## Editions and who implements them

| Date | Edition | Status | What changed | Implemented by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1985 | [Aures (1985b)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/standards.html#ref-aures-1985-euphony) | published | Tonality model. | **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)**, **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)** (PR), [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/metasona.html), [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/pysqat.html) |
| 1982 | [Terhardt et al. (1982)](https://doi.org/10.1121/1.387544) | published | Extraction of tonal components used by the model. | — |

## Implementations

| Project | Language | Edition | Functions | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** | MATLAB | [Aures (1985b)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/standards.html#ref-aures-1985-euphony) (since v1.0) | `Tonality_Aures1985`, `Tonality_Aures1985_from_wavfile` | standard or paper data (v1.3: one signal-to-noise comparison) | The releases do not allow commercial use; the default branch has another licence. Eight defects were fixed on `main` in September 2026 (for example, only one tonal component's level excess entered the result, and tones were removed from the wrong spectrum). |
| **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)** | Python | [Aures (1985b)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/standards.html#ref-aures-1985-euphony) | — | not stated | PR (https://github.com/Eomys/MoSQITo/pull/97). Pull request from April 2026 following the improved Aures metric of Estreder et al. (2023); no maintainer reply. |
| [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/metasona.html) | C, Python | [Aures (1985b)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/standards.html#ref-aures-1985-euphony) (since 0.1.0) | `tonality_aures` | compared with SQAT (its source) | Newly released project, not yet seen to be widely used. Follows SQAT's September 2026 revision (250 ms Hann windows, 125 ms hop). |
| [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/pysqat.html) | Python | [Aures (1985b)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/standards.html#ref-aures-1985-euphony) | `Tonality_Aures1985` | compared with SQAT (its source) | Developing project: no publication or documented use by others. No licence file: by default, copying, changing or sharing the code needs the author's permission. A June 2026 commit corrected its calibration; it predates SQAT's September 2026 fixes. |

**See also:** [Tonality from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tonality-ecma-418-2.html)

## How they were validated

As reported by each project; LISQM has not run the code. Two implementations that agree can still share the same error.

- **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)**, Aures (1985b): standard or paper data (v1.3: one signal-to-noise comparison)
  - v1.3 is checked with one signal-to-noise comparison.
  - The September 2026 fixes on `main` add checks against Aures's Figs. 5 and 6.
- [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/metasona.html), Aures (1985b): compared with **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** (its source)
  - Ported or adapted from **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)**. It was compared with the code it was ported from, which checks the port only.
  - The project calls its source-based Python comparisons "development checks, not an executed MATLAB/Octave validation"; exact agreement with MATLAB is not established.
  - The results are not published.
- [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/pysqat.html), Aures (1985b): compared with **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** (its source)
  - Ported or adapted from **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)**. It was compared with the code it was ported from, which checks the port only.
  - Compared with SQAT v1.3, run in MATLAB, by `validation/FINAL_VAL.py`; the generated reports are not committed.

Not stated by MoSQITo.

## Project map

The lines of the project map for tonality (Aures) only (the whole map: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/map.md). Agreement between a project and the code it was ported or adapted from only checks the port.

### Ported or adapted from another project

- From **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)**: [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/metasona.html) (Aures (1985b)); [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/pysqat.html) (Aures (1985b))

On the map without a line, as no relation is recorded for them: **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)**.

## Before you compare numbers

Implementations of the same metric can give different numbers without either being wrong. Check these choices first.

What the projects state:

- **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)**: Statistics such as N5 take the nearest rank of the sorted time series, without interpolation (`get_exceeded_value`), and leave out the first `time_skip` seconds of the signal.
- [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/metasona.html): Expects calibrated sound pressure in pascals. The C functions require 48 kHz input; the Python interface resamples other rates to 48 kHz (SciPy `resample_poly`). `time_skip_s` (default 0 s) leaves out the start of the signal from the reported frames; the computation still runs over the whole signal. Time-varying results include every complete frame, labelled at frame centres, which differs from SQAT's handling of the last frame and of time stamps.

## References

1. Terhardt, E., Stoll, G., & Seewann, M. (1982). Algorithm for extraction of pitch and pitch salience from complex tonal signals. *The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America*, 71(3), 679–688. https://doi.org/10.1121/1.387544
2. Aures, W. (1985). Berechnungsverfahren für den sensorischen Wohlklang beliebiger Schallsignale [A model for calculating the sensory euphony of various sounds]. *Acustica*, 59, 130–141.

# Tonality from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tonality-ecma-418-2.html

**Quantity:** Tonality · **Unit:** tu_HMS · **Also known as:** ECMA-418-2 tonality, psychoacoustic tonality, tu_HMS, Sottek tonality, SHM tonality

Psychoacoustic tonality from the Sottek Hearing Model, Clause 6 of ECMA-418-2, with specific tonality and tonal frequency over time. The method came from ECMA-74 (17th edition, 2019) when ECMA-418-2 was first published in 2020.

The current edition is ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.). Open-source implementations of it: **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** (MATLAB; unreleased), **[sottek-hearing-model](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sottek-hearing-model.html)** (Python), [refmap-psychoacoustics](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/refmap-psychoacoustics.html) (MATLAB, Python), [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/metasona.html) (C, Python; newly released, not yet seen to be widely used; mono or stereo), and [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html) (Python; newly released, not yet seen to be widely used; mono only). Implementations of earlier editions or related models: **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** (MATLAB; ECMA-418-2:2024 (3rd ed.)).

## Editions and who implements them

| Date | Edition | Status | What changed | Implemented by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2025-06 | [ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_4th_edition_june_2025.pdf) | current | Hearing-model and conformance updates (48 kHz sampling). | **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** (unreleased), **[sottek-hearing-model](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sottek-hearing-model.html)**, [refmap-psychoacoustics](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/refmap-psychoacoustics.html), [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/metasona.html), [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html) |
| 2024-12 | [ECMA-418-2:2024 (3rd ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_3rd_edition_december_2024.pdf) | superseded | Diffuse-field outer and middle ear filter added (affects all metrics); refinements mainly to roughness. | **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** |
| 2022-12 | [ECMA-418-2:2022 (2nd ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_2nd_edition_december_2022.pdf) | superseded | Refined calculation. | — |
| 2020-12 | [ECMA-418-2:2020 (1st ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_1st_edition_december_2020.pdf) | superseded | Clause 6 tonality. | — |
| 2019-12 | [ECMA-74:2019 (17th ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-74/) | superseded | Hearing model and tonality before ECMA-418-2 existed. | — |

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** | MATLAB | [ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_4th_edition_june_2025.pdf) | `Tonality_ECMA418_2` | compared with ArtemiS SUITE (HEAD acoustics) | Unreleased. |

| [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html) | Python | [ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_4th_edition_june_2025.pdf) (mono only; since 3.1.0) | `tonality_ecma` | standard or paper data (calibration signal only) | Newly released project, not yet seen to be widely used. |

Also available through tools that call one of these implementations: [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/pysqat.html) (via sottek-hearing-model, ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.)).

**See also:** [Tonality, Aures/Terhardt model](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tonality-aures.html), [Tone-to-noise ratio and prominence ratio (ECMA-418-1)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tone-to-noise-prominence-ratio.html), [Loudness from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-ecma-418-2.html)

On the map without a line, as no relation is recorded for them: [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html).

## Before you compare numbers

Implementations of the same metric can give different numbers without either being wrong. Check these choices first.

- **Edition and start.** Compare implementations of the same edition; overall values leave out the first 304 ms, where the filters settle.
- **Tonal annoyance weighting.** RefMap and sottek-hearing-model offer an optional weighting after Sottek & Becker (2019), which is not part of ECMA-418-2; leave it off when comparing with other implementations.

What the projects state:

- **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)**: Statistics take the nearest rank of the sorted time series, without interpolation (`get_exceeded_value`), and leave out the first `time_skip` seconds; the code enforces at least 304 ms (it cites ECMA-418-2:2025, Section 8.1.4).
- **[sottek-hearing-model](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sottek-hearing-model.html)**: Input at other sample rates is resampled to 48 kHz.
- [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/metasona.html): Expects calibrated sound pressure in pascals. The C functions require 48 kHz input; the Python interface resamples other rates to 48 kHz (SciPy `resample_poly`). `time_skip_s` (default 0 s) leaves out the start of the signal from the reported frames; the computation still runs over the whole signal. Time-varying results include every complete frame, labelled at frame centres, which differs from SQAT's handling of the last frame and of time stamps.

## References

1. ECMA-74:2019 (17th ed.). Measurement of airborne noise emitted by information technology and telecommunications equipment. https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-74/
2. ECMA-418-2:2020 (1st ed.). Psychoacoustic metrics for ITT equipment — Part 2 (models based on human perception). https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_1st_edition_december_2020.pdf
3. ECMA-418-2:2022 (2nd ed.). Psychoacoustic metrics for ITT equipment — Part 2 (models based on human perception). https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_2nd_edition_december_2022.pdf
4. ECMA-418-2:2024 (3rd ed.). Psychoacoustic metrics for ITT equipment — Part 2 (methods for describing human perception based on the Sottek Hearing Model). https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_3rd_edition_december_2024.pdf
5. ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.). Psychoacoustic metrics for ITT equipment — Part 2 (methods for describing human perception based on the Sottek Hearing Model). https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_4th_edition_june_2025.pdf

# Tone-to-noise ratio and prominence ratio (ECMA-418-1)

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tone-to-noise-prominence-ratio.html

**Quantity:** Tonality · **Unit:** dB · **Also known as:** TNR, PR, ECMA-418-1, ECMA-74 Annex D, prominent discrete tones, ANSI S1.13 Annex

Tone-to-noise ratio (TNR) and prominence ratio (PR) decide whether a discrete tone is prominent: TNR compares the tone with the noise in its critical band, PR compares the critical band with its neighbours. ECMA-418-1 took the method over from Annex D of ECMA-74 in 2020; its 3rd edition (2024) revised the TNR procedure.

The current edition is ECMA-418-1:2024 (3rd ed.). Open-source implementations of it: [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html) (Python; newly released, not yet seen to be widely used). So far, only newly released projects, not yet seen to be widely used in the community, have released an implementation of it. Check their validation before relying on them. Implementations of earlier editions or related models: **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)** (Python; ECMA-74:2019 (17th ed.)), [Mosqito.NET](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito-net.html) (C#; newly released, not yet seen to be widely used; ECMA-74:2019 (17th ed.)), and [MoSQITo-FDP](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito-fdp.html) (Python; legacy, archived; ECMA-74:2019 (17th ed.); Annex D).

## Editions and who implements them

| Date | Edition | Status | What changed | Implemented by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2024-12 | [ECMA-418-1:2024 (3rd ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-1_3rd_edition_december_2024.pdf) | current | TNR procedure revised for repeatable results across FFT resolutions; terms rewritten. | [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html) |
| 2022-12 | [ECMA-418-1:2022 (2nd ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-1_2nd_edition_december_2022.pdf) | superseded | Maximum tone bandwidth for TNR set to 15 % of the critical band; corrections. | — |
| 2020-12 | [ECMA-418-1:2020 (1st ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-1_1st_edition_december_2020.pdf) | superseded | Based on, and mostly identical to, ECMA-74 Annex D. | — |
| 2019-12 | [ECMA-74:2019 (17th ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-74/) | superseded | Annex D, before ECMA-418-1 existed. | **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)**, [Mosqito.NET](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito-net.html), [MoSQITo-FDP](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito-fdp.html) |

## Implementations

| Project | Language | Edition | Functions | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)** | Python | [ECMA-74:2019 (17th ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-74/) (since 1.0.2) | `tnr_ecma_st`, `tnr_ecma_perseg`, `tnr_ecma_freq`, `pr_ecma_st`, `pr_ecma_perseg`, `pr_ecma_freq` | not stated | Docstrings say "ECMA 418-1" without an edition; the helper code and the bibliography cite ECMA-74 Annex D (17th edition, 2019). |
| [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html) | Python | [ECMA-418-1:2024 (3rd ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-1_3rd_edition_december_2024.pdf) (since 3.1.0) | `tone_to_noise_ratio`, `prominence_ratio`, `assess_tones` | standard or paper data (formula examples; no published TNR or PR value) | Newly released project, not yet seen to be widely used. The "prominent" flag applies the numeric criterion only. |
| [Mosqito.NET](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito-net.html) | C# | [ECMA-74:2019 (17th ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-74/) | `Sq.TnrEcmaSt`, `Sq.TnrEcmaFreq`, `Sq.TnrEcmaPerSeg`, `Sq.PrEcmaSt`, `Sq.PrEcmaFreq`, `Sq.PrEcmaPerSeg` | compared with MoSQITo (its source) | Newly released project, not yet seen to be widely used. The README cites ECMA-74 Annex D. |
| [MoSQITo-FDP](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito-fdp.html) | Python | [ECMA-74:2019 (17th ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-74/) (Annex D) | `comp_tnr`, `comp_pr` | own tests only | Legacy project, no longer maintained. |

**See also:** [Tonality from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tonality-ecma-418-2.html), [Audibility of tones in noise (ISO/TS 20065)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tonal-audibility-iso-20065.html)

## How they were validated

As reported by each project; LISQM has not run the code. Two implementations that agree can still share the same error.

- **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)**, ECMA-74:2019 (17th ed.): not stated
  - The documentation marks it as available but not validated.
- [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html), ECMA-418-1:2024 (3rd ed.): standard or paper data (formula examples; no published TNR or PR value)
  - Tests check worked examples printed in ECMA-418-1:2024: the critical band at 500 Hz and 1 kHz (Clause 10, Formula 2), its band edges at 1 kHz (Clause 12.2) and the proximity spacing at 150 and 850 Hz (Clause 11.6, Formula 14).
  - TNR and PR of a 1 kHz tone in white noise are compared with the values expected from the standard's formulas (within 0.4 dB for TNR and 0.1 dB for PR); no TNR or PR value published in the standard is checked.
- [Mosqito.NET](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito-net.html), ECMA-74:2019 (17th ed.): compared with **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)** (its source)
  - Ported or adapted from **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)**. It was compared with the code it was ported from, which checks the port only.
  - Every public function is compared with the output of Python MoSQITo for seven WAV files (three of them ISO 532-1 test signals), within 1 % (0.5 dB for levels); MoSQITo's unit tests are ported too.
- [MoSQITo-FDP](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito-fdp.html), ECMA-74:2019 (17th ed.): own tests only
  - Ported or adapted from **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)**.
  - The README lists TNR/PR as available but not validated; the tests use synthetic tones in white noise.

# Tonal components and tone adjustment (DIN 45681)

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tonality-din-45681.html

**Quantity:** Tonality · **Unit:** dB · **Also known as:** DIN 45681, tone adjustment, K_T, Tonzuschlag

German method that detects tonal components in noise from narrow-band spectra and derives a tone adjustment for the assessment of noise immissions. DIN 45681:2005, corrected by Berichtigung 2:2006-08 (which replaced Berichtigung 1:2005-08), is current.

The current edition is DIN 45681:2005. No open-source implementation of it has been found. Implementations of earlier editions or related models: [ITA-Toolbox](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/ita-toolbox.html) (MATLAB; E DIN 45681:2002-11; maximum tonal audibility and its frequency).

## Editions and who implements them

| Date | Edition | Status | What changed | Implemented by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2005-03 | [DIN 45681:2005](https://www.dinmedia.de/en/standard/din-45681/76463232) | current | Current; Berichtigung 2:2006-08 replaced Berichtigung 1:2005-08. | — |
| 2002-11 | [E DIN 45681:2002-11](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/standards.html#ref-din-45681-2002-draft) | superseded | — | [ITA-Toolbox](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/ita-toolbox.html) |

## Implementations

| Project | Language | Edition | Functions | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [ITA-Toolbox](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/ita-toolbox.html) | MATLAB | [E DIN 45681:2002-11](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/standards.html#ref-din-45681-2002-draft) (maximum tonal audibility and its frequency) | `ita_tonality` | not stated | The header cites "DIN 45681 (2002)", the draft that preceded DIN 45681:2005. A code comment says that no A-weighting is applied. |

**See also:** [Audibility of tones in noise (ISO/TS 20065)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tonal-audibility-iso-20065.html)

## How they were validated

# Audibility of tones in noise (ISO/TS 20065)

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tonal-audibility-iso-20065.html

**Quantity:** Tonality · **Unit:** dB · **Also known as:** ISO/TS 20065, ISO/PAS 20065, tonal audibility, decisive audibility, ΔL_ta

Engineering method for the audibility of tones in noise, from critical-band analysis of narrow-band spectra. First published as ISO/PAS 20065:2016 and turned into ISO/TS 20065:2022, which notes that the method is not validated below 50 Hz.

The current edition is ISO/TS 20065:2022. No open-source implementation of it has been found. Implementations of earlier editions or related models: [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html) (Python; newly released, not yet seen to be widely used; ISO/PAS 20065:2016).

## Editions and who implements them

| Date | Edition | Status | What changed | Implemented by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2022-12 | [ISO/TS 20065:2022](https://www.iso.org/standard/81518.html) | current | Technical specification; adds that the method is not validated below 50 Hz. | — |
| 2016-07 | [ISO/PAS 20065:2016](https://www.iso.org/standard/66941.html) | withdrawn | Publicly available specification; withdrawn in 2022. | [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html) |

## Implementations

| Project | Language | Edition | Functions | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html) | Python | [ISO/PAS 20065:2016](https://www.iso.org/standard/66941.html) (since 3.1.0) | `tone_audibility`, `analyze_spectrum`, `audibility_from_levels`, `mean_audibility`, `audibility_uncertainty` | standard or paper data; also compared with DIN 45681 Annex J reference program | Newly released project, not yet seen to be widely used. Follows the 2016 PAS, not the 2022 TS. Does not apply the A-weighting required by clause 5.3.2. DIN 45681 itself is not implemented. |

**See also:** [Tonal components and tone adjustment (DIN 45681)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tonality-din-45681.html), [Tonal audibility in environmental noise (ISO 1996-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tonal-audibility-iso-1996-2.html)

## How they were validated

As reported by each project; LISQM has not run the code. Two implementations that agree can still share the same error.

- [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html), ISO/PAS 20065:2016: standard or paper data; also compared with DIN 45681 Annex J reference program
  - Reproduces the Annex E worked example.
  - Parts are checked against DIN 45681:2005 and its Annex J reference program.

## References

1. ISO/PAS 20065:2016. Acoustics — Objective method for assessing the audibility of tones in noise — Engineering method. https://www.iso.org/standard/66941.html
2. ISO/TS 20065:2022. Acoustics — Objective method for assessing the audibility of tones in noise — Engineering method. https://www.iso.org/standard/81518.html

# Tonal audibility in environmental noise (ISO 1996-2)

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tonal-audibility-iso-1996-2.html

**Quantity:** Tonality · **Unit:** dB · **Also known as:** ISO 1996-2 Annex C, ISO 1996-2 Annex J, ISO 1996-2 Annex K, tonal adjustment, environmental noise tonality

Objective tonal audibility and tone adjustment for environmental noise assessment. ISO 1996-2:2007 gave a method in Annex C; ISO 1996-2:2017 replaced it with an engineering method (Annex J) and a survey method (Annex K).

The current edition is ISO 1996-2:2017. Open-source implementations of it: **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)** (Python; Annex K prominent-tone detection; PR, not merged) and [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html) (Python; newly released, not yet seen to be widely used; Annex K survey method and Table J.1; in the `phonometry.environment` namespace). So far, only newly released projects, not yet seen to be widely used in the community, have released an implementation of it. Check their validation before relying on them. Implementations of earlier editions or related models: [acoustic-toolbox](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/acoustic-toolbox.html) (Python; ISO 1996-2:2007; tonal audibility and tonal adjustment), [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html) (Python; newly released, not yet seen to be widely used; ISO 1996-2:2007; Annex C; in the `phonometry.environment` namespace), and [python-acoustics](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/python-acoustics.html) (Python; legacy, archived; ISO 1996-2:2007; tonal audibility and tonal adjustment).

## Editions and who implements them

| 2017-07 | [ISO 1996-2:2017](https://www.iso.org/standard/59766.html) | current; ISO Open Data (2026-09-30) links it to a successor project (ISO 86954), which has not been published yet. | Annex J engineering method and Annex K survey method. | **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)** (PR), [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html) |
| 2007-03 | [ISO 1996-2:2007](https://www.iso.org/standard/41860.html) | withdrawn | Annex C tonal audibility. | [acoustic-toolbox](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/acoustic-toolbox.html), [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html), [python-acoustics](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/python-acoustics.html) |

# Tonal audibility of wind turbine noise (IEC 61400-11)

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tonal-audibility-iec-61400-11.html

**Quantity:** Tonality · **Unit:** dB · **Also known as:** IEC 61400-11, wind turbine tonality, tonal audibility

Tonality analysis in the acoustic noise measurement of wind turbines: tones are identified in narrow-band spectra and their tonal audibility is reported.

The current edition is IEC 61400-11:2012+AMD1:2018. Open-source implementations of it: [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html) (Python; newly released, not yet seen to be widely used). So far, only newly released projects, not yet seen to be widely used in the community, have released an implementation of it. Check their validation before relying on them.

## Editions and who implements them

| Date | Edition | Status | What changed | Implemented by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2012-11 | [IEC 61400-11:2012+AMD1:2018](https://webstore.iec.ch/en/publication/63367) | current | Edition 3 with Amendment 1 (2018); tonal audibility in clause 9.5. | [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html) |
| 2002-12 | [IEC 61400-11:2002](https://webstore.iec.ch/en/publication/19736) | superseded | Edition 2 (Amendment 1 in 2006); already has a tonal audibility procedure. | — |

# Prominence of impulsive sounds (ISO/PAS 1996-3, NT ACOU 112)

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/impulsiveness.html

**Quantity:** Impulsiveness · **Unit:** dB · **Also known as:** ISO/PAS 1996-3, NT ACOU 112, impulsiveness, impulse adjustment, impulsive sound prominence

Objective prominence of impulsive sounds and the corresponding adjustment of the equivalent level in environmental noise assessment: Nordtest method NT ACOU 112 and ISO/PAS 1996-3:2022 (adjustment of 0 to 9 dB). Hearing-model impulsiveness metrics are not standardised and no open implementation is listed.

The current edition is ISO/PAS 1996-3:2022. Open-source implementations of it: [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html) (Python; newly released, not yet seen to be widely used; in the `phonometry.environment` namespace). So far, only newly released projects, not yet seen to be widely used in the community, have released an implementation of it. Check their validation before relying on them. Implementations of earlier editions or related models: [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html) (Python; newly released, not yet seen to be widely used; NT ACOU 112; in the `phonometry.environment` namespace).

## Editions and who implements them

| Date | Edition | Status | What changed | Implemented by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2022-07 | [ISO/PAS 1996-3:2022](https://www.iso.org/standard/77035.html) | current; ISO Open Data (2026-09-30) links it to a successor project (ISO 95221), which has not been published yet. | Publicly available specification. | [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html) |
| 2002-05 | [NT ACOU 112](http://www.nordtest.info/wp/2002/05/01/acoustics-prominence-of-impulsive-sounds-and-for-adjustment-of-laeq-nt-acou-112/) | current | Nordic test method. | [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html) |

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html) | Python | [NT ACOU 112](http://www.nordtest.info/wp/2002/05/01/acoustics-prominence-of-impulsive-sounds-and-for-adjustment-of-laeq-nt-acou-112/) (in the `phonometry.environment` namespace) | — | not stated | Newly released project, not yet seen to be widely used. |

# Psychoacoustic annoyance (Widmann, Zwicker & Fastl, More, Di et al.)

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/psychoacoustic-annoyance.html

**Quantity:** Psychoacoustic annoyance · **Unit:** dimensionless · **Also known as:** PA, psychoacoustic annoyance, Zwicker annoyance, Widmann annoyance, More annoyance, Di annoyance

Psychoacoustic annoyance (PA) combines percentile loudness N5 with sharpness, roughness and fluctuation strength (Widmann 1992; Zwicker & Fastl 1999). More (2010) added tonality and Di et al. (2016) adapted the model for tonal noise. None of these is standardised; ISO/AWI 26573, registered in 2026, covers the assessment of annoyance through listening tests, including prediction models.

There is no standard; the reference models are Widmann (1992), Zwicker & Fastl (1999), More (2010), and Di et al. (2016). In development: ISO/AWI 26573. Open-source implementations of it: **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** (MATLAB; Di et al. (2016)), **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** (MATLAB; More (2010)), **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** (MATLAB; Zwicker & Fastl (1999)), **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** (MATLAB; Widmann (1992); unreleased), [refmap-psychoacoustics](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/refmap-psychoacoustics.html) (MATLAB, Python; Di et al. (2016); Python, from precomputed metric values), [refmap-psychoacoustics](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/refmap-psychoacoustics.html) (MATLAB, Python; More (2010); Python, from precomputed metric values), [refmap-psychoacoustics](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/refmap-psychoacoustics.html) (MATLAB, Python; Widmann (1992)), [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html) (Python; newly released, not yet seen to be widely used; Zwicker & Fastl (1999)), [PsychoacousticMetrics.jl](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psychoacousticmetrics-jl.html) (Julia; newly released, not yet seen to be widely used; Widmann (1992); percentile convention (N5, S5, R5, FS5) and a stationary approximation), [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/pysqat.html) (Python; developing; Di et al. (2016)), [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/pysqat.html) (Python; developing; More (2010)), [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/pysqat.html) (Python; developing; Zwicker & Fastl (1999)), and [PsychoacousticParametersMeasurer](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psychoacoustic-parameters-measurer.html) (Python; legacy, no commit since 2021-06; Zwicker & Fastl (1999)).

| 2010 | [More (2010)](https://docs.lib.purdue.edu/dissertations/AAI3453255) | published | Adds tonality. | **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)**, [refmap-psychoacoustics](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/refmap-psychoacoustics.html), [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/pysqat.html) |

## How they were validated

As reported by each project; LISQM has not run the code. Two implementations that agree can still share the same error.

- **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)**, Di et al. (2016); More (2010): not stated
  - No verification routine (README).
- [refmap-psychoacoustics](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/refmap-psychoacoustics.html), Widmann (1992): standard or paper data
  - A validation script (`validation/metrics/mlab/acousticPsychAnnoyValidation.m`) compares the MATLAB version with values from Widmann (1992).
- [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html), Zwicker & Fastl (1999): own tests only
  - Tests compare one set of inputs (N5 = 30 sone, S = 2.0 acum, F = 0.5 vacil, R = 0.3 asper) with the value worked out by hand from Eqs. 16.2–16.4 (37.0478, within 0.001) and check the terms of the formula; no published example is used.
- [PsychoacousticMetrics.jl](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psychoacousticmetrics-jl.html), Widmann (1992): compared with **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)**
  - Cross-checked against SQAT's `PsychoacousticAnnoyance_Widmann1992`: an 840-case formula grid, reproduced bit-exactly, and six signal-level cases with SQAT's own N5, S5, R5 and FS5 vendored, so that every deviation is attributed to a component.
  - Checked at the published 1 au anchor (a 1 kHz tone at 40 dB SPL): on the 4 s cross-check case, the percentile convention lands 0.1 % from it and the stationary approximation 0.8 %; on the README's 5 s examples, 0.3 % and 1.4 %.
- [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/pysqat.html), Di et al. (2016); More (2010); Zwicker & Fastl (1999): compared with **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** (its source)
  - Ported or adapted from **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)**. It was compared with the code it was ported from, which checks the port only.
  - Compared with SQAT v1.3, run in MATLAB, by `validation/FINAL_VAL.py`; the generated reports are not committed.

Not stated by SQAT for Zwicker & Fastl (1999) and Widmann (1992); refmap-psychoacoustics for Di et al. (2016) and More (2010); PsychoacousticParametersMeasurer.

## Project map

The lines of the project map for psychoacoustic annoyance only (the whole map: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/map.md). Agreement between a project and the code it was ported or adapted from only checks the port.

### Ported or adapted from another project

- From **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)**: [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/pysqat.html) (Di et al. (2016), More (2010), and Zwicker & Fastl (1999))

### Used at run time

- [PsychoacousticMetrics.jl](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psychoacousticmetrics-jl.html) needs [ZwickerLoudness.jl](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/zwickerloudness-jl.html) (Widmann (1992))

### Results checked against another project

- [PsychoacousticMetrics.jl](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psychoacousticmetrics-jl.html) against **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** (Widmann (1992))

### Same contributor

- **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** and [refmap-psychoacoustics](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/refmap-psychoacoustics.html) (Mike Lotinga)

On the map without a line, as no relation is recorded for them: [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html) and [PsychoacousticParametersMeasurer](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psychoacoustic-parameters-measurer.html).

## Before you compare numbers

Implementations of the same metric can give different numbers without either being wrong. Check these choices first.

- **Inputs.** The models combine percentile values of loudness, sharpness, roughness and fluctuation strength (N5, S5, R5 and F5 in SQAT and PsychoacousticMetrics.jl). The percentile definition and the sharpness, roughness and fluctuation-strength models used change the result, and so does using whole-signal values instead (a stationary approximation).
- **Same model, two names.** Zwicker & Fastl (1999) give Widmann's (1992) model; SQAT lists it under both names. More (2010) and Di et al. (2016) are different models.

What the projects state:

- **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)**: Statistics such as N5 take the nearest rank of the sorted time series, without interpolation (`get_exceeded_value`), and leave out the first `time_skip` seconds of the signal.
- [PsychoacousticMetrics.jl](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psychoacousticmetrics-jl.html): The percentile form needs 48 kHz input. Percentiles are Hyndman–Fan type 7 quantiles (linear interpolation); SQAT takes the nearest rank, which the README says differs by a full order-statistic step on the coarse fluctuation-strength track.

## References

1. Widmann, U. (1992). *Ein Modell der psychoakustischen Lästigkeit von Schallen und seine Anwendung in der Praxis der Lärmbeurteilung* [Doctoral dissertation, Technische Universität München].
2. Zwicker, E., & Fastl, H. (1999). *Psychoacoustics: Facts and models* (2nd ed.). Springer. https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-662-09562-1
3. More, S. R. (2010). *Aircraft noise characteristics and metrics* [Doctoral dissertation, Purdue University]. PARTNER report PARTNER-COE-2011-004. https://docs.lib.purdue.edu/dissertations/AAI3453255
4. Di, G., Chen, X., Song, K., Zhou, B., & Pei, C. (2016). Improvement of Zwicker's psychoacoustic annoyance model aiming at tonal noises. *Applied Acoustics*, 105, 164–170. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.apacoust.2015.12.006
5. ISO/AWI 26573. Acoustics — Procedures for assessment and prediction of noise-induced perceptual annoyance through laboratory-based listening tests. https://www.iso.org/standard/93922.html

# Equal-loudness-level contours (ISO 226)

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/equal-loudness-contours.html

**Quantity:** Related quantities · **Unit:** dB SPL, phon · **Also known as:** ISO 226, equal-loudness contours, phon curves, threshold of hearing

Normal equal-loudness-level contours for pure tones in free-field listening. ISO 226:2023 replaced ISO 226:2003; ECMA-418-2:2025 still refers to the 2003 edition.

The current edition is ISO 226:2023. Open-source implementations of it: [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html) (Python; newly released, not yet seen to be widely used). So far, only newly released projects, not yet seen to be widely used in the community, have released an implementation of it. Check their validation before relying on them. Implementations of earlier editions or related models: **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)** (Python; ISO 226:2003), [PSYCHO](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/pd-psycho.html) (Pure Data, C; ISO 226:2003), [PyDSM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/pydsm.html) (Python; ISO 226:2003; tabled and interpolated contours; optional 20 kHz extension), [Mosqito.NET](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito-net.html) (C#; newly released, not yet seen to be widely used; ISO 226:2003), and [IoSR Matlab Toolbox](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/iosr-matlab-toolbox.html) (MATLAB; legacy, no commit since 2017-08; ISO 226:2003).

## Editions and who implements them

| Date | Edition | Status | What changed | Implemented by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2023-03 | [ISO 226:2023](https://www.iso.org/standard/83117.html) | current | Third edition. | [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html) |
| 2003-08 | [ISO 226:2003](https://www.iso.org/standard/34222.html) | withdrawn | Second edition; withdrawn in 2023. | **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)**, [PSYCHO](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/pd-psycho.html), [PyDSM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/pydsm.html), [Mosqito.NET](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito-net.html), [IoSR Matlab Toolbox](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/iosr-matlab-toolbox.html) |

## Implementations

| Project | Language | Edition | Functions | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)** | Python | [ISO 226:2003](https://www.iso.org/standard/34222.html) (since 0.3.5) | `equal_loudness_contours` | not stated | The docstring gives no edition; it is based on Jeff Tackett's MATLAB code for ISO 226:2003. |
| [PSYCHO](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/pd-psycho.html) | Pure Data, C | [ISO 226:2003](https://www.iso.org/standard/34222.html) | `[iso226]` | not stated | The help patch names ISO 226:2003. Related objects convert between phon and dB (`[phon2db]`, `[db2phon]`) and between phon and sone (`[phon2sone]`, `[sone2phon]`). |
| [PyDSM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/pydsm.html) | Python | [ISO 226:2003](https://www.iso.org/standard/34222.html) (tabled and interpolated contours; optional 20 kHz extension) | `pydsm.iso226` | not stated | — |
| [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html) | Python | [ISO 226:2023](https://www.iso.org/standard/83117.html) (since 3.1.0) | `equal_loudness_contour`, `equal_loudness_contours`, `loudness_level`, `hearing_threshold` | standard or paper data | Newly released project, not yet seen to be widely used. |
| [Mosqito.NET](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito-net.html) | C# | [ISO 226:2003](https://www.iso.org/standard/34222.html) | `Sq.EqualLoudnessContours` | not stated | Newly released project, not yet seen to be widely used. Code comments say ISO 226:1987, but the tables are ported from MoSQITo, whose code follows Jeff Tackett's ISO 226:2003 implementation. |
| [IoSR Matlab Toolbox](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/iosr-matlab-toolbox.html) | MATLAB | [ISO 226:2003](https://www.iso.org/standard/34222.html) | `iosr.auditory.iso226` | not stated | Legacy project, no longer maintained. |

## How they were validated

As reported by each project; LISQM has not run the code. Two implementations that agree can still share the same error.

- [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html), ISO 226:2023: standard or paper data
  - Tests compare 17 points of Table B.1 (20 to 90 phon, 20 Hz to 12.5 kHz) and 6 points of Table B.2 with the computed contours and loudness levels, within 0.05 dB or phon, and the hearing threshold with Table 1.

Not stated by MoSQITo, PSYCHO, PyDSM, Mosqito.NET, and IoSR Matlab Toolbox.

## Project map

The lines of the project map for equal-loudness contours only (the whole map: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/map.md). Agreement between a project and the code it was ported or adapted from only checks the port.

### Ported or adapted from another project

- From **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)**: [Mosqito.NET](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito-net.html) (ISO 226:2003)

On the map without a line, as no relation is recorded for them: [PSYCHO](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/pd-psycho.html), [PyDSM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/pydsm.html), [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html), and [IoSR Matlab Toolbox](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/iosr-matlab-toolbox.html).

## References

2. ISO 226:2023. Acoustics — Normal equal-loudness-level contours. https://www.iso.org/standard/83117.html

# Perceived noise level, PNLT and EPNL (ICAO Annex 16, 14 CFR Part 36)

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/epnl.html

**Quantity:** Related quantities · **Unit:** PNdB, EPNdB · **Also known as:** EPNL, EPNdB, PNL, PNLT, perceived noisiness, noy, aircraft noise certification

Effective perceived noise level for aircraft noise certification: perceived noisiness in noy, the tone-corrected perceived noise level (PNLT) and a duration correction. Defined in ICAO Annex 16, Volume I, and in the US regulation 14 CFR Part 36.

The current edition is ICAO Annex 16, Vol. I and 14 CFR Part 36. Open-source implementations of it: **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** (MATLAB; 14 CFR Part 36), [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html) (Python; newly released, not yet seen to be widely used; ICAO Annex 16, Vol. I; PNL, PNLT and EPNL, in the `phonometry.aircraft` namespace), [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/pysqat.html) (Python; developing; 14 CFR Part 36), and [SUAVE](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/suave.html) (Python; legacy, no commit since 2022-12; ICAO Annex 16, Vol. I; PNL, PNLT and EPNL; the code cites no edition).

## Editions and who implements them

| Date | Edition | Status | What changed | Implemented by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2017-07 | [ICAO Annex 16, Vol. I](https://store.icao.int/en/annex-16-environmental-protection-volume-i-aircraft-noise) | current; Amendment 15 was adopted on 2026-03-27 and applies from 2027-01-01 (new noise limits and supersonic aeroplanes); whether it changes the EPNL procedure itself has not been confirmed. | International standard for aircraft noise certification. | [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html), [SUAVE](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/suave.html), [Zhen-Ni/epnl](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/zhen-ni-epnl.html) |
| 2002-07 | [14 CFR Part 36](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-36) | current | US regulation (Appendices A and B). | **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)**, [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/pysqat.html) |

## Implementations

| Project | Language | Edition | Functions | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** | MATLAB | [14 CFR Part 36](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-36) (since v1.1) | `EPNL_FAR_Part36`, `get_PNL`, `get_PNLT`, `get_Duration_Correction` | compared with published EPNL values (Rizzi et al., 2020) | The releases do not allow commercial use; the default branch has another licence. Follows Amendment 36-26 (2005). |
| [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html) | Python | [ICAO Annex 16, Vol. I](https://store.icao.int/en/annex-16-environmental-protection-volume-i-aircraft-noise) (PNL, PNLT and EPNL, in the `phonometry.aircraft` namespace) | — | standard or paper data | Newly released project, not yet seen to be widely used. |
| [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/pysqat.html) | Python | [14 CFR Part 36](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-36) | `EPNL_FAR_Part36` | compared with SQAT (its source) | Developing project: no publication or documented use by others. No licence file: by default, copying, changing or sharing the code needs the author's permission. |
| [SUAVE](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/suave.html) | Python | [ICAO Annex 16, Vol. I](https://store.icao.int/en/annex-16-environmental-protection-volume-i-aircraft-noise) (PNL, PNLT and EPNL; the code cites no edition) | `pnl_noise`, `noise_tone_correction`, `epnl_noise` | not stated | Legacy project, no longer maintained. EPNL is computed from a PNLT time history. The noise tools cite neither ICAO Annex 16 nor 14 CFR Part 36, nor an edition; their docstrings give "Source: None". |
| [Zhen-Ni/epnl](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/zhen-ni-epnl.html) | Rust | [ICAO Annex 16, Vol. I](https://store.icao.int/en/annex-16-environmental-protection-volume-i-aircraft-noise) (PNL and PNLT only; no duration correction to EPNL) | `SPL`, `Noy`, `PNL`, `PNLT` | not stated | Legacy project, no longer maintained. No licence file: by default, copying, changing or sharing the code needs the author's permission. Partial: computes only part of the metric. Code comments cite "Annex 16 - Volume I, APP 2-16 / 2-17" and number the 24 bands "consistent with ICAO ANNEX 16". The quantities are Rust types converted into each other with `From`. |

## How they were validated

As reported by each project; LISQM has not run the code. Two implementations that agree can still share the same error.

- **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)**, 14 CFR Part 36: compared with published EPNL values (Rizzi et al., 2020)
  - The README says that no reference implementation or test signals exist, so the verification is partial.
  - Perceived noisiness is checked at its definition (a third-octave band of noise at 1 kHz and 40 dB SPL gives 1 noy), and the tone correction factor against Table 3.7 of ICAO Doc 9501.
  - EPNL is cross-checked with Table 4 of Rizzi et al. (2020), AIAA 2020-2582, for 15 flyover sounds (five cases auralised by three tools): the largest difference is about 0.6 EPNdB.
- [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html), ICAO Annex 16, Vol. I: standard or paper data
  - Tested with the EPNL example of ICAO Doc 9501 (Environmental Technical Manual).
- [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/pysqat.html), 14 CFR Part 36: compared with **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** (its source)
  - Ported or adapted from **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)**. It was compared with the code it was ported from, which checks the port only.
  - Compared with SQAT v1.3, run in MATLAB, by `validation/FINAL_VAL.py`; the generated reports are not committed.

Not stated by SUAVE and Zhen-Ni/epnl.

## Project map

The lines of the project map for perceived noise level and EPNL only (the whole map: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/map.md). Agreement between a project and the code it was ported or adapted from only checks the port.

### Ported or adapted from another project

- From **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)**: [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/pysqat.html) (14 CFR Part 36)

On the map without a line, as no relation is recorded for them: [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html), [SUAVE](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/suave.html), and [Zhen-Ni/epnl](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/zhen-ni-epnl.html).

## References

1. 14 CFR Part 36. Noise standards: aircraft type and airworthiness certification (Appendix A: EPNL). https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-36
2. ICAO Annex 16, Vol. I. Annex 16 to the Convention on International Civil Aviation — Environmental Protection — Volume I: Aircraft Noise. https://store.icao.int/en/annex-16-environmental-protection-volume-i-aircraft-noise

# Aural detectability of sounds in background noise

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/aural-detectability.html

**Quantity:** Related quantities · **Unit:** d′ (detectability index), dB · **Also known as:** detectability, d-prime, signal detection, aural detection, audibility of aircraft

How likely a listener is to detect a sound in background noise, from signal-to-noise ratios in auditory filters and signal-detection theory. Used for aircraft, drone and urban air mobility noise. Not standardised.

There is no standard; the reference model is Fidell et al. (1974). Open-source implementations of it: [refmap-psychoacoustics](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/refmap-psychoacoustics.html) (MATLAB, Python; MATLAB and Python). Implementations of earlier editions or related models: [refmap-psychoacoustics](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/refmap-psychoacoustics.html) (MATLAB, Python; Rizzi et al. (2025); MATLAB and Python).

## Editions and who implements them

| Date | Edition | Status | What changed | Implemented by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2025-07 | [Rizzi et al. (2025)](https://doi.org/10.2514/1.C038188) | published | NASA's use of the model in annoyance assessments of urban air mobility, with audibility as a factor. | [refmap-psychoacoustics](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/refmap-psychoacoustics.html) |
| 1974 | [Fidell et al. (1974)](https://doi.org/10.1177/001872087401600405) | published | Model paper. | [refmap-psychoacoustics](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/refmap-psychoacoustics.html) |

## Implementations

| Project | Language | Edition | Functions | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [refmap-psychoacoustics](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/refmap-psychoacoustics.html) | MATLAB, Python | [Rizzi et al. (2025)](https://doi.org/10.2514/1.C038188) (MATLAB and Python) | `auralDetectability`, `aural_detect` | not stated | The same functions; the README cites this paper for the NASA development of the model. |
| [refmap-psychoacoustics](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/refmap-psychoacoustics.html) | MATLAB, Python | [Fidell et al. (1974)](https://doi.org/10.1177/001872087401600405) (MATLAB and Python) | `auralDetectability`, `auralDetectFromLeq`, `aural_detect`, `aural_detect_from_lzeqt` | not stated | Code headers describe the Fidell, Pearsons & Bennett (1974) model as "developed further by NASA" and cite "Rizzi, SA et al, 2024"; the README cites Rizzi et al. (2025), *Journal of Aircraft*, doi:10.2514/1.C038188. |

## How they were validated

As reported by each project; LISQM has not run the code. Two implementations that agree can still share the same error.

None of these projects says how its code was validated.

## References

1. Fidell, S., Pearsons, K. S., & Bennett, R. (1974). Prediction of aural detectability of noise signals. *Human Factors*, 16(4), 373–383. https://doi.org/10.1177/001872087401600405
2. Rizzi, S. A., Christian, A. W., Letica, S. J., & Lympany, S. V. (2026). Annoyance model assessments of urban air mobility vehicle operations. *Journal of Aircraft*, 63(1). Published online 2025-07-02. https://doi.org/10.2514/1.C038188

# SQAT

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html

MATLAB toolbox for sound quality analysis that bundles most psychoacoustic metrics in one place: ISO 532-1 and ECMA-418-2 loudness, DIN 45692 sharpness, Daniel & Weber and ECMA-418-2 roughness, Osses fluctuation strength, Aures and ECMA-418-2 tonality, three psychoacoustic annoyance models (Zwicker & Fastl, which `main` also provides under its original attribution to Widmann; More; Di et al.) and EPNL. Every metric except the annoyance models has its own verification routine.

- **Repository:** https://github.com/ggrecow/SQAT
- **Documentation:** https://github.com/ggrecow/SQAT#readme
- **Language:** MATLAB
- **Kind:** Library/Toolbox (Functions to call from your own code: a Python package, a MATLAB toolbox, or a C, C++, C#, Rust or Julia library.)
- **Group:** established (Described in a publication, used by others, or written by the authors of the model, with more than a year of history. A widely used project.)
- **Licence:** GPL-3.0-or-later (main) / CC-BY-NC-4.0 (releases) — The default branch has been GPL-3.0-or-later since 2026-09-15, with BSD-3-Clause (ISO 532-1 loudness), MIT (Daniel & Weber roughness and nine utilities) and CC0-1.0 (colour maps) exceptions. Every release up to and including v1.3 is CC-BY-NC-4.0 (non-commercial) at repository level, while 21 metric files in v1.3 carry BSD-style notices and the ECMA-418-2 files say GPL-3.0.
- **Latest release:** v1.3 (2025-04)
- **Last commit:** 2026-10-02 (active)
- **GitHub stars:** 100
- **Maintainers:** Gil Felix Greco, Roberto Merino-Martínez, Alejandro Osses, Mike Lotinga
- **AI assistance:** disclosed — Header comments in 20 files changed in August and September 2026 say the changes were assisted by Claude (Anthropic) and verified by the authors; 32 commits carry AI co-author trailers. The README has no AI statement.
- **Paper:** Felix Greco, G., Merino-Martínez, R., Osses, A., & Langer, S. C. (2023). SQAT: a MATLAB-based toolbox for quantitative sound quality analysis. *Proceedings of INTER-NOISE 2023*, Chiba, Japan. https://doi.org/10.3397/IN_2023_1075
- **How to cite:** The README asks for the toolbox itself: Felix Greco, G., Merino-Martínez, R., Osses, A., & Lotinga, M. J. B. (2025). *SQAT: a sound quality analysis toolbox for MATLAB*. Zenodo. It recommends citing the specific version used, since results differ between releases; each release has its own DOI. The paper above describes the first release. Software DOI: [10.5281/zenodo.7934709](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.7934709). The repository has a [CITATION.cff](https://github.com/ggrecow/SQAT/blob/main/citation.cff) file. Name the version or commit you used.
- **Entry checked:** 2026-10-08

## What it implements

| Metric | Edition | Functions | Status | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Zwicker loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html) | [ISO 532-1:2017](https://www.iso.org/standard/63077.html) (stationary and time-varying; since v1.0) | `Loudness_ISO532_1`, `Loudness_ISO532_1_from_wavfile` | available | standard or paper data (in v1.3, test signal 10 is off by 18.14 %) | Fixes to the time-varying procedure are on `main` only (PR #48). |
