## How it was validated

As reported by the project; LISQM has not run the code. Two implementations that agree can still share the same error.

- [Zwicker loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html), ISO 532-1:2017: standard or paper data (in v1.3, test signal 10 is off by 18.14 %)
  - Ported or adapted from [AARAE](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/aarae.html).
  - Checked with the 25 test signals of Annex B.2–B.5 against the standard's tolerances.
- [Sottek Hearing Model loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-ecma-418-2.html), ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.): compared with ArtemiS SUITE (HEAD acoustics)
  - Ported or adapted from [refmap-psychoacoustics](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/refmap-psychoacoustics.html) (the author's own code).
  - On `main`, checked for the 4th edition against the ISO 226:2003 equal-loudness contours and against reference results from HEAD acoustics ArtemiS SUITE 17.1 (named in the source of SQAT's validation page) for a binaural recording of a train station (last checked in November 2025).
- [Sottek Hearing Model loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-ecma-418-2.html), ECMA-418-2:2024 (3rd ed.): compared with ArtemiS SUITE (HEAD acoustics)
  - Ported or adapted from [refmap-psychoacoustics](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/refmap-psychoacoustics.html) (the author's own code).
  - Checked against the ISO 226:2003 equal-loudness contours and against reference results from HEAD acoustics ArtemiS SUITE 15.7 (named in the source of SQAT's validation page) for a binaural recording of a train station.
- [Sharpness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/sharpness.html), DIN 45692:2009: standard or paper data
  - Checked with the narrowband and broadband test signals of DIN 45692.
- [Roughness (Daniel & Weber)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/roughness-daniel-weber.html), Daniel & Weber (1997): standard or paper data
  - Ported or adapted from [AARAE](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/aarae.html).
  - Checked against amplitude- and frequency-modulation dependences from the literature.
- [Sottek Hearing Model roughness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/roughness-ecma-418-2.html), ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.): compared with ArtemiS SUITE (HEAD acoustics)
  - Ported or adapted from [refmap-psychoacoustics](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/refmap-psychoacoustics.html) (the author's own code).
  - On `main`, checked for the 4th edition for the dependence of the roughness of AM tones on modulation frequency, and against reference results from HEAD acoustics ArtemiS SUITE 17.1 (named in the source of SQAT's validation page) for a binaural recording of a train station.
- [Sottek Hearing Model roughness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/roughness-ecma-418-2.html), ECMA-418-2:2024 (3rd ed.): compared with ArtemiS SUITE (HEAD acoustics)
  - Ported or adapted from [refmap-psychoacoustics](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/refmap-psychoacoustics.html) (the author's own code).
  - Checked for the dependence of the roughness of AM tones on modulation frequency, and against reference results from HEAD acoustics ArtemiS SUITE 15.7 (named in the source of SQAT's validation page) for a binaural recording of a train station.
- [Fluctuation strength (Osses et al.)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/fluctuation-strength-osses.html), Osses et al. (2016): standard or paper data
  - Ported or adapted from [fluctuation-strength-TUe](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/fluctuation-strength-tue.html) (the author's own code).
  - Checked against amplitude- and frequency-modulation dependences from the literature.
- [Tonality (Aures)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tonality-aures.html), Aures (1985b): standard or paper data (v1.3: one signal-to-noise comparison)
  - v1.3 is checked with one signal-to-noise comparison.
  - The September 2026 fixes on `main` add checks against Aures's Figs. 5 and 6.
- [Sottek Hearing Model tonality](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tonality-ecma-418-2.html), ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.): compared with ArtemiS SUITE (HEAD acoustics)
  - Ported or adapted from [refmap-psychoacoustics](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/refmap-psychoacoustics.html) (the author's own code).
  - On `main`, checked for the 4th edition against reference results from HEAD acoustics ArtemiS SUITE 17.1 (named in the source of SQAT's validation page) for a binaural recording of a train station.
  - A verification against Annex B.2 (PR #79) was merged and reverted on 2026-09-21 because the Annex B values of the 2025 edition appear to be out of date.
- [Sottek Hearing Model tonality](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tonality-ecma-418-2.html), ECMA-418-2:2024 (3rd ed.): compared with ArtemiS SUITE (HEAD acoustics)
  - Ported or adapted from [refmap-psychoacoustics](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/refmap-psychoacoustics.html) (the author's own code).
  - Checked against reference results from HEAD acoustics ArtemiS SUITE 15.7 (named in the source of SQAT's validation page) for a binaural recording of a train station.
- [Psychoacoustic annoyance](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/psychoacoustic-annoyance.html), Di et al. (2016); [Psychoacoustic annoyance](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/psychoacoustic-annoyance.html), More (2010): not stated
  - No verification routine (README).
- [Perceived noise level and EPNL](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/epnl.html), 14 CFR Part 36: compared with published EPNL values (Rizzi et al., 2020)
  - The README says that no reference implementation or test signals exist, so the verification is partial.
  - Perceived noisiness is checked at its definition (a third-octave band of noise at 1 kHz and 40 dB SPL gives 1 noy), and the tone correction factor against Table 3.7 of ICAO Doc 9501.
  - EPNL is cross-checked with Table 4 of Rizzi et al. (2020), AIAA 2020-2582, for 15 flyover sounds (five cases auralised by three tools): the largest difference is about 0.6 EPNdB.

Not stated for Sottek Hearing Model fluctuation strength · ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.); Psychoacoustic annoyance · Zwicker & Fastl (1999); Psychoacoustic annoyance · Widmann (1992).

## Before you compare numbers

Implementations of the same metric can give different numbers without either being wrong. Check these choices first.

- Statistics such as N5 take the nearest rank of the sorted time series, without interpolation (`get_exceeded_value`), and leave out the first `time_skip` seconds of the signal.
- Statistics take the nearest rank of the sorted time series, without interpolation (`get_exceeded_value`), and leave out the first `time_skip` seconds; the code enforces at least 304 ms (it cites ECMA-418-2:2025, Section 8.1.4).
- The single value is the 90th percentile from MATLAB's `prctile`, which interpolates; the other statistics take the nearest rank (`get_exceeded_value`). The first `time_skip` seconds are left out; the code enforces at least 320 ms (it cites ECMA-418-2:2025, Section 7.1.8).


## Notes

- The README lists 61 studies and theses that use SQAT.
- The latest release is v1.3 (2025-04-04); about 200 commits have been made on `main` since. Most of the metric-correctness work of August–September 2026 came from an external contributor through about 20 pull requests.
- The ECMA-418-2 functions come from the RefMap MATLAB code by Lotinga and Torjussen (University of Salford); the ISO 532-1 loudness was adapted in 2023 from Ella Manor's 2015 MATLAB code for AARAE.
- Open pull requests: [#78](https://github.com/ggrecow/SQAT/pull/78) (ECMA-418-2 fluctuation strength) and [#84](https://github.com/ggrecow/SQAT/pull/84) (graphical interface).

## Before you rely on it

- The latest release (v1.3) is licensed for non-commercial use only; the GPL licence applies to the unreleased `main` branch.
- `main` contains breaking fixes that are not in any release: six deviations in ISO 532-1 time-varying loudness ([#48](https://github.com/ggrecow/SQAT/pull/48); test signal 10 deviated by 18.14 % in v1.3), eight defects in Aures tonality ([#67](https://github.com/ggrecow/SQAT/issues/67)), a rewrite of Daniel & Weber roughness ([#65](https://github.com/ggrecow/SQAT/pull/65)), the sound level meter time weighting ([#51](https://github.com/ggrecow/SQAT/pull/51)) and a faster annoyance calculation ([#42](https://github.com/ggrecow/SQAT/pull/42)). Results from v1.3 and `main` differ.
- The README warns that `main` may contain changes that are not yet fully verified and recommends using a release.

# MoSQITo

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html

Python library for sound quality metrics: ISO 532-1 loudness, DIN 45692 sharpness, Daniel & Weber roughness, ECMA-418-2 hearing-model loudness (Clause 5) and roughness (2nd edition), tone-to-noise and prominence ratios, and the speech intelligibility index. Widely used, but without a release or a commit since April 2024.

- **Repository:** https://github.com/Eomys/MoSQITo
- **Documentation:** https://mosqito.readthedocs.io/en/latest/
- **Language:** Python
- **Kind:** Library/Toolbox (Functions to call from your own code: a Python package, a MATLAB toolbox, or a C, C++, C#, Rust or Julia library.)
- **Group:** established (Described in a publication, used by others, or written by the authors of the model, with more than a year of history. A widely used project.)
- **Licence:** Apache-2.0
- **Package:** PyPI `mosqito` (https://pypi.org/project/mosqito/)
- **Install:** `pip install mosqito`
- **Latest release:** v1.2.1 (2024-04)
- **Last commit:** 2024-04-22 (inactive since 2024-04)
- **GitHub stars:** 178
- **Maintainers:** Eomys / Green Forge Coop
- **AI assistance:** not stated
- **Paper:** San Millán-Castillo, R., Latorre-Iglesias, E., Glesser, M., Wanty, S., Jiménez-Caminero, D., & Álvarez-Jimeno, J. M. (2021). MOSQITO: an open-source and free toolbox for sound quality metrics in the industry and education. *INTER-NOISE 2021*, INCE Conference Proceedings 263(5), 1164–1175. https://doi.org/10.3397/IN-2021-1767
- **How to cite:** Cite the paper above. Software DOI: [10.5281/zenodo.11026796](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.11026796). The repository has a [CITATION.cff](https://github.com/Eomys/MoSQITo/blob/master/CITATION.cff) file. Name the version or commit you used.
- **Entry checked:** 2026-10-08

## What it implements

| Metric | Edition | Functions | Status | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Zwicker loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html) | [ISO 532-1:2017](https://www.iso.org/standard/63077.html) (stationary (also per segment and from a spectrum) and time-varying; since 1.0.0) | `loudness_zwst`, `loudness_zwst_perseg`, `loudness_zwst_freq`, `loudness_zwtv` | available | standard or paper data (outcome not stated) | — |
| [Sottek Hearing Model loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-ecma-418-2.html) | [ECMA-418-2:2022 (2nd ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_2nd_edition_december_2022.pdf) (Clause 5 hearing-model specific and total loudness only; the Clause 8 loudness added in the 2nd edition is not implemented; since 1.2.0) | `loudness_ecma` | available | standard or paper data (outcome not stated) | Followed the 1st edition (2020) in versions 1.0.0–1.1.1 and the 2nd edition (2022) from 1.2.0. It grew out of the hearing model that Daniel Jiménez-Caminero added in May 2021, which is also kept in MoSQITo-FDP. |
| [Sharpness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/sharpness.html) | [DIN 45692:2009](https://www.dinmedia.de/en/standard/din-45692/117635111) (weightings: DIN 45692, Aures, von Bismarck, Fastl; since 1.0.2) | `sharpness_din_st`, `sharpness_din_tv`, `sharpness_din_perseg`, `sharpness_din_from_loudness`, `sharpness_din_freq` | available | standard or paper data (outcome not stated) | — |
| [Roughness (Daniel & Weber)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/roughness-daniel-weber.html) | [Daniel & Weber (1997)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/standards.html#ref-daniel-weber-1997) (since 1.0.0) | `roughness_dw`, `roughness_dw_freq` | available | standard or paper data (outcome not stated) | — |
| [Sottek Hearing Model roughness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/roughness-ecma-418-2.html) | [ECMA-418-2:2022 (2nd ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_2nd_edition_december_2022.pdf) (since 1.2.0) | `roughness_ecma` | available | standard or paper data; also compared with ArtemiS SUITE (HEAD acoustics) | The documentation still lists it as under development. An open pull request (#95) fixes the low-pass filter range, which caused discrepancies with SQAT for time-varying signals. |
| [Tonality (Aures)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tonality-aures.html) | [Aures (1985b)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/standards.html#ref-aures-1985-euphony) | — | PR | not stated | Pull request from April 2026 following the improved Aures metric of Estreder et al. (2023); no maintainer reply. |
| [Tone-to-noise ratio and prominence ratio](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tone-to-noise-prominence-ratio.html) | [ECMA-74:2019 (17th ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-74/) (since 1.0.2) | `tnr_ecma_st`, `tnr_ecma_perseg`, `tnr_ecma_freq`, `pr_ecma_st`, `pr_ecma_perseg`, `pr_ecma_freq` | available | not stated | Docstrings say "ECMA 418-1" without an edition; the helper code and the bibliography cite ECMA-74 Annex D (17th edition, 2019). |
| [Tonal audibility (ISO 1996-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tonal-audibility-iso-1996-2.html) | [ISO 1996-2:2017](https://www.iso.org/standard/59766.html) (Annex K prominent-tone detection) | — | PR | not stated | Pull request from May 2022; no maintainer reply. |
| [Equal-loudness contours](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/equal-loudness-contours.html) | [ISO 226:2003](https://www.iso.org/standard/34222.html) (since 0.3.5) | `equal_loudness_contours` | available | not stated | The docstring gives no edition; it is based on Jeff Tackett's MATLAB code for ISO 226:2003. |

## How it was validated

As reported by the project; LISQM has not run the code. Two implementations that agree can still share the same error.

- [Zwicker loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html), ISO 532-1:2017: standard or paper data (outcome not stated)
  - Ported or adapted from BASIC program of DIN 45631 (Zwicker et al., 1991).
  - Validation scripts use the ISO 532-1 Annex B test signals; the documentation marks it as validated.
- [Sottek Hearing Model loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-ecma-418-2.html), ECMA-418-2:2022 (2nd ed.): standard or paper data (outcome not stated)
  - Validation scripts compare with figures of the standard.
- [Sharpness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/sharpness.html), DIN 45692:2009: standard or paper data (outcome not stated)
  - Validation scripts use the DIN 45692 test signals; the documentation marks it as validated.
- [Roughness (Daniel & Weber)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/roughness-daniel-weber.html), Daniel & Weber (1997): standard or paper data (outcome not stated)
  - The documentation marks it as validated against reference data.
- [Sottek Hearing Model roughness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/roughness-ecma-418-2.html), ECMA-418-2:2022 (2nd ed.): standard or paper data; also compared with ArtemiS SUITE (HEAD acoustics)
  - A unit test checks the standard's reference signal (1 kHz tone, 100 % amplitude-modulated at 70 Hz, 60 dB), which should give 1 asper, within ±0.1 asper.
  - A validation script compares the specific roughness of amplitude-modulated tones (carriers from 125 Hz to 4 kHz, 65 dB) with values computed in HEAD acoustics ArtemiS SUITE, within ±10 %.
- [Tone-to-noise ratio and prominence ratio](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tone-to-noise-prominence-ratio.html), ECMA-74:2019 (17th ed.): not stated
  - The documentation marks it as available but not validated.

Not stated for Tonality (Aures) · Aures (1985b); Tonal audibility (ISO 1996-2) · ISO 1996-2:2017; Equal-loudness contours · ISO 226:2003.

## Before you compare numbers

Implementations of the same metric can give different numbers without either being wrong. Check these choices first.

- [Zwicker loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html) (ISO 532-1:2017): Signals sampled below 48 kHz are resampled to 48 kHz (FFT method) with a warning; time-varying loudness rejects rates above 48 kHz.

## Notes

- Started by EOMYS in 2020. The default branch is `master`; its last commit and the last release (1.2.1) are both from 2024-04-22.
- The documentation lists Soundscapy as a user; several other projects (PsychoBox, Sonemeter and others) wrap it.
- Also computes the ANSI S3.5 speech intelligibility index (`sii_ansi`), which is outside the scope of this list.
- Open, unanswered pull requests add Aures tonality ([#97](https://github.com/Eomys/MoSQITo/pull/97), 2026), ECMA-418-2 roughness fixes ([#95](https://github.com/Eomys/MoSQITo/pull/95), 2026) and an ISO 1996-2 Annex K tone detector ([#52](https://github.com/Eomys/MoSQITo/pull/52), 2022).
- A C#/.NET port, Mosqito.NET, is listed separately; it was announced in issue [#98](https://github.com/Eomys/MoSQITo/issues/98).
- The documentation lists hearing-model tonality (citing ECMA-74) as under development; there is no function for it.

## Before you rely on it

- No maintainer has answered issues or pull requests opened since 2024, including bug reports on TNR/PR (#80, #81, #99) and on the ECMA-418-2 roughness low-pass filter (#92, #95).
- `import mosqito` fails when matplotlib is not installed, because it is imported but not declared as a dependency ([#100](https://github.com/Eomys/MoSQITo/issues/100)); install matplotlib yourself.
- Its ECMA-418-2 functions follow the 2nd edition (2022), two editions behind the current one.

# sottek-hearing-model

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sottek-hearing-model.html

Python implementation of the ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th edition) Sottek Hearing Model metrics: loudness and roughness (with binaural combination), tonality (per channel), and fluctuation strength on the main branch. Translated from the MATLAB code used in SQAT and the RefMap project.

- **Repository:** https://github.com/mlotinga/sottek-hearing-model
- **Language:** Python
- **Kind:** Library/Toolbox (Functions to call from your own code: a Python package, a MATLAB toolbox, or a C, C++, C#, Rust or Julia library.)
- **Group:** established (Described in a publication, used by others, or written by the authors of the model, with more than a year of history. A very good implementation.)
- **Licence:** GPL-3.0-only — The LICENSE file has always been GPL-3.0 and the project metadata was changed to GPL-3.0-only on 2026-08-31; the metadata of the current PyPI release (0.1.14) still says AGPL-3.0-only.
- **Package:** PyPI `sottek-hearing-model` (https://pypi.org/project/sottek-hearing-model/)
- **Install:** `pip install sottek-hearing-model`
- **Latest release:** v0.1.14 (2026-03)
- **Last commit:** 2026-09-18 (active)
- **GitHub stars:** 23
- **Maintainers:** Mike Lotinga
- **AI assistance:** not stated
- **Paper:** Lotinga, M. J. B., Torjussen, M., & Felix Greco, G. (2025). Verified implementations of the Sottek psychoacoustic Hearing Model standardised sound quality metrics (ECMA-418-2 loudness, tonality and roughness). *Forum Acusticum / Euronoise 2025*, Málaga. https://doi.org/10.61782/fa.2025.0951
- **How to cite:** The README asks for the paper above, which published the MATLAB code the package was translated from, and gives a BibTeX entry for it. Name the version or commit you used.
- **Entry checked:** 2026-10-08

## What it implements

| Metric | Edition | Functions | Status | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Sottek Hearing Model loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-ecma-418-2.html) | [ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_4th_edition_june_2025.pdf) (mono or stereo, with combined binaural output; since 0.1.9) | `shm_loudness_ecma`, `shm_loudness_ecma_from_comp` | available | standard or paper data (calibration signals and one recording); also compared with ArtemiS SUITE (HEAD acoustics) | — |
| [Sottek Hearing Model roughness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/roughness-ecma-418-2.html) | [ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_4th_edition_june_2025.pdf) (with combined binaural output; since 0.1.9) | `shm_roughness_ecma` | available | standard or paper data (reference signal and one recording); also compared with ArtemiS SUITE (HEAD acoustics) | — |
| [Sottek Hearing Model fluctuation strength](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/fluctuation-strength-ecma-418-2.html) | [ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_4th_edition_june_2025.pdf) (needs at least 1.37 s of signal; binaural option) | `shm_fluctuation_ecma` | unreleased | compared with refmap-psychoacoustics (its source) and ArtemiS SUITE (HEAD acoustics) | Merged on 2026-09-18. Five departures from the printed text are documented (four equations and one interpretation of Section 9.1.8). |
| [Sottek Hearing Model tonality](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tonality-ecma-418-2.html) | [ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_4th_edition_june_2025.pdf) (since 0.1.9) | `shm_tonality_ecma` | available | standard or paper data (reference signal and one recording); also compared with ArtemiS SUITE (HEAD acoustics) | Optional experimental tonal-annoyance weighting (Sottek & Becker, 2019) since 0.1.14. |

## How it was validated

As reported by the project; LISQM has not run the code. Two implementations that agree can still share the same error.

**Checked by the maintainer of LISQM:** In personal use, Zhenxian LI found its results in very good agreement with those of HEAD acoustics ArtemiS SUITE. This is a personal check, not a published comparison.

- [Sottek Hearing Model loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-ecma-418-2.html), ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.): standard or paper data (calibration signals and one recording); also compared with ArtemiS SUITE (HEAD acoustics)
  - Ported or adapted from [refmap-psychoacoustics](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/refmap-psychoacoustics.html) (the author's own code).
  - Unit tests check the standard's calibration signals (1 kHz, 40 dB gives 1 sone_HMS).
  - RefMap's verification compared the Python code, before it became this package, and the MATLAB original with HEAD acoustics ArtemiS v17.1 for the two calibration signals and a 30 s binaural street recording.
- [Sottek Hearing Model roughness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/roughness-ecma-418-2.html), ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.): standard or paper data (reference signal and one recording); also compared with ArtemiS SUITE (HEAD acoustics)
  - Ported or adapted from [refmap-psychoacoustics](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/refmap-psychoacoustics.html) (the author's own code).
  - Unit tests check the standard's reference signal, which should give 1 asper_HMS, at 48 and 44.1 kHz.
  - RefMap's verification against ArtemiS v17.1, as for loudness.
- [Sottek Hearing Model fluctuation strength](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/fluctuation-strength-ecma-418-2.html), ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.): compared with [refmap-psychoacoustics](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/refmap-psychoacoustics.html) (its source) and ArtemiS SUITE (HEAD acoustics)
  - Ported or adapted from [refmap-psychoacoustics](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/refmap-psychoacoustics.html) (the author's own code). It was compared with the code it was ported from, which checks the port only.
  - A draft report (18 September 2026) compares it with `acousticSHMFluctuation.m`, the MATLAB code it was translated from: equal to floating-point precision on the synthetic signals and on one channel of each recording, with a small difference in a short time window on the other channel.
  - Against HEAD acoustics ArtemiS SUITE v17: 0.994 against 1.003 vacil_HMS for the calibration signal (the standard's target is 1.0), −8 % to +12 % for the overall values of three binaural recordings, and correlations of 0.91 to 0.998 for the time-dependent values.
- [Sottek Hearing Model tonality](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tonality-ecma-418-2.html), ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.): standard or paper data (reference signal and one recording); also compared with ArtemiS SUITE (HEAD acoustics)
  - Ported or adapted from [refmap-psychoacoustics](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/refmap-psychoacoustics.html) (the author's own code).
  - Unit tests check the standard's reference signal, which should give 1 tu_HMS, at 48 and 44.1 kHz.
  - RefMap's verification against ArtemiS v17.1, as for loudness.

## Before you compare numbers

Implementations of the same metric can give different numbers without either being wrong. Check these choices first.

- Input at other sample rates is resampled to 48 kHz.
- Overall roughness and fluctuation strength are 90th percentiles computed with NumPy (linear interpolation, Hyndman–Fan type 7). The MATLAB code it was translated from uses `prctile`, which interpolates differently, so single values can differ slightly from RefMap and SQAT.


## Notes

- The paper verifies the MATLAB implementations of the 3rd edition, from which this package was translated; it does not cover the Python package itself.
- Maintained by one person at the University of Salford (RefMap project). Requires Python 3.11 or newer.
- pySQAT calls this package for its ECMA-418-2 metrics.

## Before you rely on it

- Fluctuation strength is only on the main branch (not on PyPI yet) and its verification report is marked as a draft.
- Versions up to 0.1.13 are affected by an empty-array bug fixed in 0.1.14 ([#9](https://github.com/mlotinga/sottek-hearing-model/issues/9)).

## Sources

- https://github.com/mlotinga/sottek-hearing-model/blob/main/README.md
- https://github.com/mlotinga/sottek-hearing-model/blob/main/LICENSE
- https://github.com/mlotinga/sottek-hearing-model/blob/main/docs/validation/fluctuation_strength_verification.md
- https://pypi.org/project/sottek-hearing-model/
- https://github.com/mlotinga/sottek-hearing-model/issues/9
- https://github.com/mlotinga/sottek-hearing-model/tree/main/tests
- https://github.com/acoustics-code-salford/refmap-psychoacoustics/blob/main/validation/ECMA-418-2/README.md

# acoustic-toolbox

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/acoustic-toolbox.html

Python acoustics library under the Université Gustave Eiffel GitHub organisation, continuing python-acoustics. For this list it is relevant for its tonal audibility and tonal adjustment after ISO 1996-2:2007.

- **Repository:** https://github.com/Universite-Gustave-Eiffel/acoustic-toolbox
- **Documentation:** https://acoustic-toolbox.readthedocs.io/
- **Language:** Python
- **Kind:** Library/Toolbox (Functions to call from your own code: a Python package, a MATLAB toolbox, or a C, C++, C#, Rust or Julia library.)
- **Group:** established (Described in a publication, used by others, or written by the authors of the model, with more than a year of history.)
- **Licence:** BSD-3-Clause
- **Package:** PyPI `acoustic-toolbox` (https://pypi.org/project/acoustic-toolbox/)
- **Install:** `pip install acoustic-toolbox`
- **Latest release:** v0.2.2 (2026-01)
- **Last commit:** 2026-02-12 (active)
- **GitHub stars:** 30
- **Maintainers:** Valentin Le Bescond, Andrew Mitchell
- **AI assistance:** not stated
- **How to cite:** The project does not say how to cite it. Cite the repository with the version or commit you used.
- **Entry checked:** 2026-10-08

## What it implements

| Metric | Edition | Functions | Status | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Tonal audibility (ISO 1996-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tonal-audibility-iso-1996-2.html) | [ISO 1996-2:2007](https://www.iso.org/standard/41860.html) (tonal audibility and tonal adjustment) | `Tonality`, `tonal_audibility`, `tonal_adjustment` | available | own tests only | Module `acoustic_toolbox.standards.iso_1996_2_2007`, the same code lineage as python-acoustics. |

## How it was validated

As reported by the project; LISQM has not run the code. Two implementations that agree can still share the same error.

- [Tonal audibility (ISO 1996-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tonal-audibility-iso-1996-2.html), ISO 1996-2:2007: own tests only
  - Ported or adapted from [python-acoustics](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/python-acoustics.html).
  - As in python-acoustics, the test of the examples in the standard is commented out.

## Notes

- Based on python-acoustics (per the README) and keeps its git history; development under the new name started in July 2024.
- It has no loudness, sharpness or roughness modules.

## Before you rely on it

- It follows ISO 1996-2:2007, which has been withdrawn; ISO 1996-2:2017 replaced its tonal audibility method with those of Annexes J and K.

# AMT

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/amt.html

MATLAB/Octave toolbox of auditory models for reproducible research. Its loudness models include the Moore–Glasberg models for stationary sounds (`moore1997`, `chen2011`), time-varying sounds (`glasberg2002`) and binaural loudness (`moore2016`).

- **Full name:** Auditory Modeling Toolbox
- **Repository:** https://sourceforge.net/p/amtoolbox/code/
- **Homepage:** https://amtoolbox.org
- **Language:** MATLAB, Octave
- **Kind:** Library/Toolbox (Functions to call from your own code: a Python package, a MATLAB toolbox, or a C, C++, C#, Rust or Julia library.)
- **Group:** established (Described in a publication, used by others, or written by the authors of the model, with more than a year of history. A widely used toolbox for auditory modelling that also includes some psychoacoustic functions.)
- **Licence:** GPL-3.0 — SourceForge lists the licence as GPLv3. The COPYING file of release 1.6.0 says that most files are under GPL 3.0 and some under other licences, each file stating its own; the headers of the loudness models (moore1997, glasberg2002, moore2016) allow version 3 or any later version.
- **Package:** package `amtoolbox` (https://sourceforge.net/projects/amtoolbox/files/)
- **Latest release:** 1.6.0 (2024-10)
- **Last commit:** 2026-06-14 (active)
- **Maintainers:** AMT Team, Acoustics Research Institute (Austrian Academy of Sciences)
- **AI assistance:** not stated
- **Paper:** Majdak, P., Hollomey, C., & Baumgartner, R. (2022). AMT 1.x: A toolbox for reproducible research in auditory modeling. *Acta Acustica*, 6, 19. https://doi.org/10.1051/aacus/2022011
- **How to cite:** Cite the paper above. Name the version or commit you used.
- **Entry checked:** 2026-10-08

## What it implements

| Metric | Edition | Functions | Status | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Moore–Glasberg loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg.html) | [Chen et al. (2011)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.heares.2011.08.001) | `chen2011` | available | standard or paper data | Listed as "CHEN2011 - Fast excitation pattern estimation". |
| [Moore–Glasberg loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg.html) | [Moore, Glasberg & Baer (1997)](https://aes2.org/publications/elibrary-page/?id=10272) | `moore1997` | available | standard or paper data | Listed as "MOORE1997 - Loudness model for stationary signals" in models/Contents.m. |
| [Time-varying loudness (Moore–Glasberg–Schlittenlacher)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg-time-varying.html) | [Moore et al. (2016)](https://doi.org/10.1177/2331216516682698) (binaural) | `moore2016` | available | not stated | Listed as "MOORE2016 - Binaural loudness model". The header says Josef Schlittenlacher provided the original implementation for the AMT in 2018, from code written for ANSI S3.4-2007 and ISO 532-2:2017. |
| [Time-varying loudness (Moore–Glasberg–Schlittenlacher)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg-time-varying.html) | [Glasberg & Moore (2002)](https://aes2.org/publications/elibrary-page/?id=11081) | `glasberg2002` | available | standard or paper data | Listed as "GLASBERG2002 - Loudness model for time-variant signals". |

## How it was validated

As reported by the project; LISQM has not run the code. Two implementations that agree can still share the same error.

- [Moore–Glasberg loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg.html), Chen et al. (2011): standard or paper data
  - Has the experiment script `exp_chen2011`; AMT's experiment scripts reproduce the results of the publication they are named after.
- [Moore–Glasberg loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg.html), Moore, Glasberg & Baer (1997): standard or paper data
  - AMT's experiment scripts (`exp_…`) reproduce published results; this model has `exp_moore1997`.
- [Time-varying loudness (Moore–Glasberg–Schlittenlacher)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg-time-varying.html), Moore et al. (2016): not stated
  - There is no `exp_moore2016` experiment script on the develop branch.
- [Time-varying loudness (Moore–Glasberg–Schlittenlacher)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg-time-varying.html), Glasberg & Moore (2002): standard or paper data
  - Has the experiment script `exp_glasberg2002`; AMT's experiment scripts reproduce the results of the publication they are named after.

## Notes

- Releases are published as downloads on SourceForge (`amtoolbox` and `amtoolbox-full`); the git repository's default branch is `develop`. The SourceForge project page mentions no GitHub or GitLab mirror.
- Also contains `bramslow2004`, a loudness model considering hearing loss (AUDMOD), with the experiment script `exp_bramslow2004`; it has no reference entry in this list.
- Neither the develop branch nor release 1.6.0 has a roughness, fluctuation strength, sharpness, tonality or annoyance model (`osses2021` is a monaural perceptual-similarity model).
- Python ports of some of its loudness models exist: [torch_amt](https://github.com/StefanoGiacomelli/torch_amt) (`glasberg2002`, `moore2016`) and [NumpyLibforPsychoAcoustic](https://github.com/Ryrybros/NumpyLibforPsychoAcoustic) (`moore1997`, `glasberg2002`). There is no official Python package (amtoolbox and pyamtoolbox are not on PyPI).
- The validation entries rest on AMT's design: each `exp_…` script is meant to reproduce figures of the model paper. The scripts' output was not checked for this list.

## Sources

- https://sourceforge.net/projects/amtoolbox/
- https://sourceforge.net/projects/amtoolbox/files/
- https://sourceforge.net/p/amtoolbox/code/ci/develop/tree/models/
- https://sourceforge.net/p/amtoolbox/code/ci/1.6.0/tree/models/
- https://sourceforge.net/p/amtoolbox/code/ci/develop/tree/experiments/
- https://sourceforge.net/p/amtoolbox/code/ci/develop/log/
- https://github.com/StefanoGiacomelli/torch_amt/blob/main/README.md
- https://sourceforge.net/projects/amtoolbox/files/AMT%201.x/

# PSYCHO

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/pd-psycho.html

Pure Data library of psychoacoustic objects (C externals and abstractions) from the author's research on dissonance models. Includes ISO 226:2003 equal-loudness contours and phon, sone and dB conversions, as well as roughness, sharpness and tonalness objects.

- **Repository:** https://github.com/porres/pd-psycho
- **Language:** Pure Data, C
- **Kind:** Plug-in (Runs inside other software: a plug-in for an audio workstation, or a Pure Data external.)
- **Group:** established (Described in a publication, used by others, or written by the authors of the model, with more than a year of history.)
- **Licence:** GPL-3.0-or-later — LICENSE.txt holds the GPL v3 text; the only licence notice in the sources (roughness.c) allows any later version.
- **Latest release:** 1.1 (2025-10)
- **Last commit:** 2025-10-14 (active)
- **GitHub stars:** 22
- **Maintainers:** Alexandre Torres Porres
- **AI assistance:** not stated
- **Paper:** Porres, A. T. (2011). Dissonance Model Toolbox in Pure Data. *Proceedings of the 4th Pure Data International Convention (PdCon11)*, Berlin.
- **How to cite:** Cite the paper above. Name the version or commit you used.
- **Entry checked:** 2026-10-06

## What it implements

| Metric | Edition | Functions | Status | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Equal-loudness contours](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/equal-loudness-contours.html) | [ISO 226:2003](https://www.iso.org/standard/34222.html) | `[iso226]` | available | not stated | The help patch names ISO 226:2003. Related objects convert between phon and dB (`[phon2db]`, `[db2phon]`) and between phon and sone (`[phon2sone]`, `[sone2phon]`). |

## How it was validated

As reported by the project; LISQM has not run the code. Two implementations that agree can still share the same error.

The project does not say how any of these were validated.

## Notes

- The roughness objects (`[roughness]`, `[roughcurve]`) compute the sensory dissonance of a spectrum given as lists of frequencies and amplitudes, with a model "derived from the work of Parncutt, Sethares, Vassilakis & Barlow"; this is not one of the signal-based roughness metrics in this list.
- `[sharpness~]` is an abstraction built on `[barks~]` (24 Bark bands) and names no sharpness model.
- Tonalness, pitch salience and commonality follow Parncutt & Strasburger (1994), after Terhardt; they are not tonality metrics in the sense of this list.
- From the author's MSc and PhD work (2005–2012). Version 1.1 was released on 2025-10-14 (git tags 1.0 of 2019 and 1.1; no GitHub releases). It builds with pd-lib-builder.

## Before you rely on it

- The README calls the library "still a work in progress".

## Sources

- https://github.com/porres/pd-psycho
- https://github.com/porres/pd-psycho/blob/master/README.md
- https://github.com/porres/pd-psycho/blob/master/LICENSE.txt
- https://github.com/porres/pd-psycho/tree/master/Classes
- https://github.com/porres/pd-psycho/tree/master/Help-files

# refmap-psychoacoustics

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/refmap-psychoacoustics.html

Research code of the REFMAP project at the University of Salford, in MATLAB with Python ports. Implements ECMA-418-2:2025 loudness, tonality and roughness, and also sharpness, impulsiveness, psychoacoustic annoyance and aural detectability models.

- **Repository:** https://github.com/acoustics-code-salford/refmap-psychoacoustics
- **Language:** MATLAB, Python
- **Kind:** Research code (Code published with a study, a thesis or a student project, to run or adapt; not packaged as a library.)
- **Group:** established (Described in a publication, used by others, or written by the authors of the model, with more than a year of history.)
- **Licence:** GPL-3.0 — The licences disagree: the LICENSE file holds the GPL-3.0 text, while pyproject.toml declares "AGPL-3.0-only". Neither says whether later GPL versions are allowed.
- **Latest release:** no release
- **Last commit:** 2026-10-06 (active)
- **GitHub stars:** 23
- **Maintainers:** Mike Lotinga
- **AI assistance:** not stated
- **Paper:** Lotinga, M. J. B., Torjussen, M., & Felix Greco, G. (2025). Verified implementations of the Sottek psychoacoustic Hearing Model standardised sound quality metrics (ECMA-418-2 loudness, tonality and roughness). *Forum Acusticum / Euronoise 2025*, Málaga. https://doi.org/10.61782/fa.2025.0951
- **How to cite:** The README asks for "Lotinga, M.J.B. (2026). refmap-psychoacoustics. GitHub." with the repository URL; the ECMA-418-2 code is described in the paper above. The repository has a [CITATION.cff](https://github.com/acoustics-code-salford/refmap-psychoacoustics/blob/main/citation.cff) file. Name the version or commit you used.
- **Entry checked:** 2026-10-07

## What it implements

| Metric | Edition | Functions | Status | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Sottek Hearing Model loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-ecma-418-2.html) | [ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_4th_edition_june_2025.pdf) (binaural and specific loudness) | `acousticSHMLoudness`, `acousticSHMLoudnessFromComponent` | available | compared with ArtemiS SUITE (HEAD acoustics) | — |
| [Sharpness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/sharpness.html) | [DIN 45692:2009](https://www.dinmedia.de/en/standard/din-45692/117635111) (DIN 45692 weighting applied to ECMA-418-2 loudness) | `acousticSharpnessSHM`, `acousticSharpFromSHMLoud` | available | not stated | The DIN 45692 weighting is the option `widmann`; Aures (the default) and von Bismarck weightings are also offered. DIN 45692 itself is defined on Zwicker specific loudness. A further variant works from a Zwicker-based quasi-loudness (`acousticSharpFromQuasiLoud`). An inaccuracy in the Aures weighting was fixed on 2026-09-18. |
| [Sottek Hearing Model roughness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/roughness-ecma-418-2.html) | [ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_4th_edition_june_2025.pdf) | `acousticSHMRoughness` | available | compared with ArtemiS SUITE (HEAD acoustics) | — |
| [Sottek Hearing Model tonality](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tonality-ecma-418-2.html) | [ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_4th_edition_june_2025.pdf) | `acousticSHMTonality` | available | compared with ArtemiS SUITE (HEAD acoustics) | — |
| [Psychoacoustic annoyance](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/psychoacoustic-annoyance.html) | [Di et al. (2016)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.apacoust.2015.12.006) (Python, from precomputed metric values) | `diPA` | available | not stated | — |
| [Psychoacoustic annoyance](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/psychoacoustic-annoyance.html) | [More (2010)](https://docs.lib.purdue.edu/dissertations/AAI3453255) (Python, from precomputed metric values) | `morePA` | available | not stated | — |
| [Psychoacoustic annoyance](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/psychoacoustic-annoyance.html) | [Widmann (1992)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/standards.html#ref-widmann-1992) | `acousticPsychAnnoy`, `widmannPA` | available | standard or paper data | The MATLAB header names the model Widmann (1992), "commonly misattributed to Zwicker". The Python `widmannPA` takes precomputed metric values. |
| [Aural detectability](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/aural-detectability.html) | [Rizzi et al. (2025)](https://doi.org/10.2514/1.C038188) (MATLAB and Python) | `auralDetectability`, `aural_detect` | available | not stated | The same functions; the README cites this paper for the NASA development of the model. |
| [Aural detectability](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/aural-detectability.html) | [Fidell et al. (1974)](https://doi.org/10.1177/001872087401600405) (MATLAB and Python) | `auralDetectability`, `auralDetectFromLeq`, `aural_detect`, `aural_detect_from_lzeqt` | available | not stated | Code headers describe the Fidell, Pearsons & Bennett (1974) model as "developed further by NASA" and cite "Rizzi, SA et al, 2024"; the README cites Rizzi et al. (2025), *Journal of Aircraft*, doi:10.2514/1.C038188. |

## How it was validated

As reported by the project; LISQM has not run the code. Two implementations that agree can still share the same error.

- [Sottek Hearing Model loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-ecma-418-2.html), ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.): compared with ArtemiS SUITE (HEAD acoustics)
  - MATLAB and Python verified against HEAD acoustics ArtemiS v17.1 for a 1 kHz tone at 40 dB SPL, a 1 kHz tone amplitude-modulated at 70 Hz at 60 dB SPL and a 30 s binaural street recording.
  - The audio and reference results are on Zenodo (doi:10.5281/zenodo.18849587).
- [Sottek Hearing Model roughness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/roughness-ecma-418-2.html), ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.); [Sottek Hearing Model tonality](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tonality-ecma-418-2.html), ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.): compared with ArtemiS SUITE (HEAD acoustics)
  - Verified against HEAD acoustics ArtemiS v17.1 with the same three signals as loudness.
- [Psychoacoustic annoyance](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/psychoacoustic-annoyance.html), Widmann (1992): standard or paper data
  - A validation script (`validation/metrics/mlab/acousticPsychAnnoyValidation.m`) compares the MATLAB version with values from Widmann (1992).

Not stated for Sharpness · DIN 45692:2009; Psychoacoustic annoyance · Di et al. (2016); Psychoacoustic annoyance · More (2010); Aural detectability · Rizzi et al. (2025); Aural detectability · Fidell et al. (1974).

## Notes

- Its MATLAB ECMA-418-2 code is the origin of SQAT's ECMA-418-2 functions, of the Python package sottek-hearing-model, and through SQAT of MetaSona's ECMA-418-2 kernels. The Python functions `shm_loudness_ecma`, `shm_tonality_ecma` and `shm_roughness_ecma` in this repository import parts of the sottek-hearing-model package, so they are listed under that package rather than here.
- The Python package defined in pyproject.toml (refmap-psychoacoustics 0.1.0) is not on PyPI.
- Tonality has an optional tonal annoyance weighting after Sottek & Becker (2019), which is not part of ECMA-418-2.
- Further metrics without an entry in this list: partial loudness and partial tonality of a target in a masker ("based on ECMA-418-2:2025", an extension of the standard), quasi-loudness from the spectral elements of ISO 532-1 with optional ISO 532-3:2023 or ECMA-418-2:2025 ear filters, tonal sharpness, and impulsiveness after Willemsen & Rao (2010) from ISO 532-1:2017 or ECMA-418-2:2025 loudness.
- The Python code also has annoyance models after Willemsen et al. (2010), Torija et al. (2022) and Boucher et al. (2024), which have no reference entry in this list.
- Also contains listening-test apps and analysis notebooks.
- sottek-hearing-model's fluctuation strength was translated from `acousticSHMFluctuation.m`, which its verification report places in this repository; the file is not on the `main` branch (checked 2026-10-07).

## Before you rely on it

- The README calls it "'work in progress' code for a research project. It is not a completed package or code library."
- Some code comments still cite clauses of "ECMA 418-2:2022".

## Sources

- https://github.com/acoustics-code-salford/refmap-psychoacoustics
- https://github.com/acoustics-code-salford/refmap-psychoacoustics/blob/main/README.md
- https://github.com/acoustics-code-salford/refmap-psychoacoustics/blob/main/validation/ECMA-418-2/README.md
- https://github.com/acoustics-code-salford/refmap-psychoacoustics/blob/main/pyproject.toml
- https://github.com/acoustics-code-salford/refmap-psychoacoustics/blob/main/LICENSE
- https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18849587
- https://pypi.org/project/sottek-hearing-model/

# AARAE

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/aarae.html

Audio and Acoustical Response Analysis Environment: a MATLAB environment with a graphical interface, made to support teaching and research in acoustics. Its analysers include ISO 532-1 and Chalupper–Fastl loudness, Moore–Glasberg loudness (stationary, time-varying and binaural), sharpness and Daniel & Weber roughness.

- **Repository:** https://github.com/densilcabrera/aarae
- **Language:** MATLAB
- **Kind:** Application (A program to run, with a graphical or command-line interface; no programming needed.)
- **Group:** established (Described in a publication, used by others, or written by the authors of the model, with more than a year of history.)
- **Licence:** BSD-3-Clause — License for AARAE.txt says that contributed files may carry their own licences; for example, the ISO 226 calculator iso226.m comes with its own license.txt.
- **Latest release:** no release
- **Last commit:** 2024-08-09 (inactive since 2024-08)
- **GitHub stars:** 36
- **Maintainers:** Densil Cabrera, Jonothan Holmes, Ella Manor
- **AI assistance:** not stated
- **Paper:** Cabrera, D., Jimenez, D., & Martens, W. L. (2014). Audio and Acoustical Response Analysis Environment (AARAE): a tool to support education and research in acoustics. *Proceedings of Inter-Noise 2014*, Melbourne, Australia. https://www.acoustics.asn.au/conference_proceedings/INTERNOISE2014/papers/p235.pdf
- **How to cite:** Cite the paper above. Name the version or commit you used.
- **Entry checked:** 2026-10-08

## What it implements

| Metric | Edition | Functions | Status | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Zwicker loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html) | [ISO 532-1:2017](https://www.iso.org/standard/63077.html) (stationary and time-varying) | `Loudness_ISO532_1` | available | standard or paper data (time-varying signals only) | The header cites a 2014 draft of ISO 532-1 and describes the code as Ella Manor's 2015 MATLAB port, with adjustments, of the Annex A C code. |
| [Zwicker loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html) | [Chalupper & Fastl (2002)](https://www.ingentaconnect.com/contentone/dav/aaua/2002/00000088/00000003/art00009) (time-varying) | `LoudnessCF` | available | not stated | Also outputs loudness fluctuation and time-varying sharpness. Josef Chalupper's code (2000) in its PsySound3 version (2007), adjusted for AARAE by Ella Manor in 2015. |
| [Moore–Glasberg loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg.html) | [Moore, Glasberg & Baer (1997)](https://aes2.org/publications/elibrary-page/?id=10272) (one channel, or two channels for binaural loudness) | `Loudness_MGB2b` | available | not stated | A port and extension of PsySound3's code by Densil Cabrera and Doheon Lee, version 1.02 (27 October 2015). Two-channel input gives binaural loudness after Moore & Glasberg (2007). The audio is resampled to 32 kHz. |
| [Time-varying loudness (Moore–Glasberg–Schlittenlacher)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg-time-varying.html) | [Glasberg & Moore (2002)](https://aes2.org/publications/elibrary-page/?id=11081) (time-varying; one channel, or two channels for binaural loudness) | `Loudness_MGB2b` | available | not stated | Same function as the stationary model; the binaural extension follows Moore & Glasberg (2007). |
| [Sharpness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/sharpness.html) | [Fastl & Zwicker (2007)](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-540-68888-4) (from the specific loudness of `LoudnessCF`) | `sharpness_Fastl` | available | not stated | The header describes a weighting fitted to data in Zwicker & Fastl's *Psychoacoustics: Facts and Models* (edition not stated), names the method "Fastl (1991)" and credits Claire Churchill (2004). |
| [Roughness (Daniel & Weber)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/roughness-daniel-weber.html) | [Daniel & Weber (1997)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/standards.html#ref-daniel-weber-1997) | `RoughnessDW` | available | not stated | Ported from PsySound3's `@RoughnessDW` by Ella Manor and Densil Cabrera (2015). |

## How it was validated

As reported by the project; LISQM has not run the code. Two implementations that agree can still share the same error.

- [Zwicker loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html), ISO 532-1:2017: standard or paper data (time-varying signals only)
  - Ported or adapted from ISO 532-1 Annex A reference program.
  - A commit of 2017-12-11 says the code was verified with the time-varying test signals of Annex B.5; no check of the stationary method is stated.
- [Zwicker loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html), Chalupper & Fastl (2002); [Moore–Glasberg loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg.html), Moore, Glasberg & Baer (1997); [Time-varying loudness (Moore–Glasberg–Schlittenlacher)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg-time-varying.html), Glasberg & Moore (2002); [Roughness (Daniel & Weber)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/roughness-daniel-weber.html), Daniel & Weber (1997): not stated
  - Ported or adapted from [PsySound3](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psysound3.html) (the author's own code).

Not stated for Sharpness · Fastl & Zwicker (2007).

## Notes

- `LoudnessZwickerISO532.m` computes Zwicker loudness with the ISO 532 one-third-octave filter bank; the edition is not stated.
- `Fluctuation.m` (Ella Manor, 2017) implements the fluctuation-strength model of Zhou et al., "A Model for Calculating Psychoacoustical Fluctuation Strength" (JAES, September 2015), with 75 ERB channels and generalized modulation depth.
- `Tonality_thirdoctmethod.m` (May 2015) implements the one-third-octave tonality methods of ISO 1996-2 (edition not stated) and AS/NZS 2107.
- `iso226.m` calculates ISO 226 equal-loudness contours; the edition is not stated in its header.

## Before you rely on it

- Runs inside MATLAB and needs several commercial toolboxes: Audio, DSP System, Signal Processing, and Statistics and Machine Learning; some parts also use others, such as Curve Fitting.
- Apart from the ISO 532-1 analyser, the project does not state how the analysers were validated.

## Sources

- https://github.com/densilcabrera/aarae
- https://github.com/densilcabrera/aarae/blob/master/README.txt
- https://github.com/densilcabrera/aarae/blob/master/License%20for%20AARAE.txt
- https://github.com/densilcabrera/aarae/tree/master/Analysers/Level%20and%20Strength
- https://github.com/densilcabrera/aarae/commits/master/Analysers/Level%20and%20Strength/Loudness_ISO532_1.m
- https://github.com/densilcabrera/aarae/blob/master/Analysers/Level%20and%20Strength/Loudness_MGB2b.m
- https://github.com/densilcabrera/aarae/blob/master/Analysers/Level%20and%20Strength/LoudnessCF.m

# iso532-3 (tv2018.m)

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/js2251-iso532-3.html

MATLAB code by Brian C. J. Moore, Brian R. Glasberg and Josef Schlittenlacher (Cambridge Hearing Group) for the loudness of time-varying sounds: the model of Moore et al. (2016) with the revised time constants of Moore et al. (2018). Its readme calls `tv2018.m` "the reference Matlab code referred to in ISO 532-3".

- **Repository:** https://github.com/js2251/iso532-3
- **Documentation:** https://github.com/js2251/iso532-3/blob/main/readme%20TVL%202018.pdf
- **Language:** MATLAB
- **Kind:** Reference program (Code published with a standard or by the authors of the model, as the reference for it.)
- **Group:** established (Described in a publication, used by others, or written by the authors of the model, with more than a year of history.)
- **Licence:** none — No licence file. The readme PDF says: "The code is provided free for any research purposes. For commercial use please contact Brian C. J. Moore."
- **Latest release:** no release
- **Last commit:** 2021-10-08 (inactive since 2021-10)
- **GitHub stars:** 2
- **Maintainers:** Brian C. J. Moore, Brian R. Glasberg, Josef Schlittenlacher
- **AI assistance:** not stated
- **How to cite:** The project does not say how to cite it. Cite the repository with the version or commit you used.
- **Entry checked:** 2026-10-07

## What it implements

| Metric | Edition | Functions | Status | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Time-varying loudness (Moore–Glasberg–Schlittenlacher)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg-time-varying.html) | [ISO 532-3:2023](https://www.iso.org/standard/69856.html) (reference MATLAB code referred to in ISO 532-3, per its readme) | `tv2018` | available | not stated | Written by the model's authors (per the readme PDF). |

## How it was validated

As reported by the project; LISQM has not run the code. Two implementations that agree can still share the same error.

- [Time-varying loudness (Moore–Glasberg–Schlittenlacher)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg-time-varying.html), ISO 532-3:2023: not stated
  - The folder "code for tables" has scripts that compute Table 5 (sone to phon) and the values of Annexes B and C (AnnexC.m is headed "Signals numbered as in ISO 532-2 Annex B"); the scripts do not name ISO 532-3.

## Notes

- There is no README.md; the documentation is the PDF "readme TVL 2018", which includes a worked example with the file 1k100ms.wav.
- Takes a WAV file or a MATLAB variable with one or two channels and resamples it to 32 kHz. Outer- and middle-ear transfer functions for free-field, diffuse-field and eardrum presentation are included. Returns short-term and long-term loudness and the instantaneous loudness of each ear.
- Also contains sone/phon conversion functions for the TV2015 and TV2018 tables (`Phon2SoneTV2015`, `Sone2PhonTV2015`, `Phon2SoneTV2018`, `Sone2PhonTV2018`).
- The Python project LoudnessModel is a translation of the Cambridge MATLAB code for the same model.
- An [archived copy](https://web.archive.org/web/20251123130736/https://www.psychol.cam.ac.uk/hearing) of the Cambridge Hearing Group's programs page (November 2025) offers the TVL 2018 MATLAB code as a ZIP file: 23 of its 28 MATLAB files are identical to this repository, which adds the TV2018 conversion tables and the scripts for the standard's tables. The page itself now needs a University of Cambridge login.

## Before you rely on it

- The code was last changed in October 2021, before ISO 532-3 was published (July 2023); the readme refers to "ISO 532-3 (2021)". Whether it is identical to the source code supplied with the published standard is not stated.
- For its text-file output, `tv2018.m` converts sone to phon with `Sone2PhonTV2015`, although TV2018 conversion tables were added in October 2021.
- The WAV files that the Annex B script reads are not in the repository, and no computed tables are stored.

## Sources

- https://github.com/js2251/iso532-3
- https://github.com/js2251/iso532-3/blob/main/readme%20TVL%202018.pdf
- https://github.com/js2251/iso532-3/blob/main/tv2018.m
- https://github.com/js2251/iso532-3/tree/main/code%20for%20tables

# ITA-Toolbox

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/ita-toolbox.html

MATLAB toolbox for acoustic measurements and signal processing from the Institute of Technical Acoustics, RWTH Aachen University, open source since 2010. Its psychoacoustics application computes stationary loudness after DIN 45631 / ISO 532 B, time-varying loudness after DIN 45631/A1, Daniel & Weber roughness and DIN 45681 tonality (2002 draft).

- **Repository:** https://git.rwth-aachen.de/ita/toolbox
- **Homepage:** https://www.ita-toolbox.org/
- **Language:** MATLAB
- **Kind:** Library/Toolbox (Functions to call from your own code: a Python package, a MATLAB toolbox, or a C, C++, C#, Rust or Julia library.)
- **Group:** established (Described in a publication, used by others, or written by the authors of the model, with more than a year of history. A widely used toolbox for acoustic measurements and signal processing that also includes some psychoacoustic functions.)
- **Licence:** BSD-4-Clause — The root license.txt (2011) is the four-clause BSD licence: advertising material that mentions the software must acknowledge the Institute of Technical Acoustics (RWTH Aachen University). The psychoacoustics files refer to a licence in their own folder, which contains none.
- **Latest release:** no release
- **Last commit:** 2025-09-22 (inactive since 2025-09)
- **Maintainers:** Institute of Technical Acoustics (ITA), RWTH Aachen University
- **AI assistance:** not stated
- **Paper:** Berzborn, M., Bomhardt, R., Klein, J., Richter, J.-G., & Vorländer, M. (2017). The ITA-Toolbox: An open source MATLAB toolbox for acoustic measurements and signal processing. *Fortschritte der Akustik – DAGA 2017*, Kiel, 222–225. https://publications.rwth-aachen.de/record/687308
- **How to cite:** Cite the paper above. Name the version or commit you used.
- **Entry checked:** 2026-10-07

## What it implements

| Metric | Edition | Functions | Status | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Zwicker loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html) | [DIN 45631/A1:2010](https://www.dinmedia.de/en/standard/din-45631-a1/122476084) (time-varying, with N5) | `ita_loudness_timevariant` | available | standard or paper data (results plotted, not checked) | The header says "DIN 45631/A1" without a year; the function was written in August 2010, after the amendment was published. A code comment says the C code of the nonlinearity block was copied from the DIN document, "without its errors". |
| [Zwicker loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html) | [DIN 45631:1991](https://www.dinmedia.de/en/standard/din-45631/1666531) (stationary; free or diffuse field) | `ita_loudness` | available | standard or paper data | The header says "DIN 45631 / ISO 532 B". The C core (`private/DIN45631.c`) is Aaron Hastings' version (2000) of the BASIC program published by Zwicker, Fastl, Widmann, Kurakata, Kuwano and Namba in J. Acoust. Soc. Jpn (E) 12(1), 1991. |
| [Roughness (Daniel & Weber)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/roughness-daniel-weber.html) | [Daniel & Weber (1997)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/standards.html#ref-daniel-weber-1997) | `ita_roughness_daniel` | available | standard or paper data (a code comment only) | Uses sub-functions written by Martin Klemenz in 2000 (`external_packages/roughness_daniel`). |
| [Tonal components (DIN 45681)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tonality-din-45681.html) | [E DIN 45681:2002-11](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/standards.html#ref-din-45681-2002-draft) (maximum tonal audibility and its frequency) | `ita_tonality` | available | not stated | The header cites "DIN 45681 (2002)", the draft that preceded DIN 45681:2005. A code comment says that no A-weighting is applied. |

## How it was validated

As reported by the project; LISQM has not run the code. Two implementations that agree can still share the same error.

- [Zwicker loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html), DIN 45631/A1:2010: standard or paper data (results plotted, not checked)
  - A test script plots the results for the amendment's test signals A to D (1 kHz tone pulses of 10 ms to 500 ms) against its tolerance bands; it does not check them automatically.
- [Zwicker loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html), DIN 45631:1991: standard or paper data
  - Ported or adapted from BASIC program of DIN 45631 (Zwicker et al., 1991).
  - A test compares the loudness of a generated pink noise with 95.09 sone (GF), a value the test attributes to DIN 45631, within 5 %, with third-octave levels computed both by FFT and by filter bank.
- [Roughness (Daniel & Weber)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/roughness-daniel-weber.html), Daniel & Weber (1997): standard or paper data (a code comment only)
  - A code comment says that after major bug fixes the values "more or less match those of the paper by Daniel"; no test or comparison script is included.

Not stated for Tonal components (DIN 45681) · E DIN 45681:2002-11.

## Before you compare numbers

Implementations of the same metric can give different numbers without either being wrong. Check these choices first.

- [Zwicker loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html) (DIN 45631/A1:2010): N5 is MATLAB's `prctile(N, 95)`. Blocks are 2 ms long without overlap by default, and the signal is processed at its own sample rate.
- [Zwicker loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html) (DIN 45631:1991): Third-octave levels come from an FFT by default, or from a filter bank (`'mode', 'filter'`).

## Notes

- The psychoacoustic functions were written in 2010 (Martin Guski: loudness; Daniel Cragg: roughness, tonality and sharpness) and are in `applications/Psychoacoustics`, last changed in September 2022.
- `ita_sharpness` names no method; its weighting has the form of the DIN 45692 weighting, but as the code does not say which standard it follows, it is not listed as an implementation of DIN 45692.
- The repository is on RWTH Aachen University's GitLab, which announces a move to gitlab.git.nrw, so its address may change.

## Before you rely on it

- `ita_roughness_daniel` and `ita_sharpness` print that a newer version exists (`ita_psychoacoustic_roughness`, `ita_psychoacoustic_sharpness`). Those functions, like `ita_psychoacoustic_loudness` and `ita_psychoacoustic_fluctuationStrength` (2021), call the MATLAB Audio Toolbox, which is closed source, so they are not listed here.
- There are no releases; use the default branch.

## Sources

- https://git.rwth-aachen.de/ita/toolbox
- https://git.rwth-aachen.de/ita/toolbox/-/blob/master/license.txt
- https://git.rwth-aachen.de/ita/toolbox/-/tree/master/applications/Psychoacoustics
- https://www.ita-toolbox.org/
- https://publications.rwth-aachen.de/record/687308

# PyDSM

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/pydsm.html

Python toolbox for the design and simulation of delta-sigma modulators. It contains a helper module, `pydsm.iso226`, with ISO 226:2003 equal-loudness contours.

- **Repository:** https://github.com/sergiocallegari/PyDSM
- **Documentation:** https://pythonhosted.org/pydsm/pydsm.iso226.html
- **Language:** Python
- **Kind:** Library/Toolbox (Functions to call from your own code: a Python package, a MATLAB toolbox, or a C, C++, C#, Rust or Julia library.)
- **Group:** established (Described in a publication, used by others, or written by the authors of the model, with more than a year of history.)
- **Licence:** GPL-3.0-or-later
- **Package:** PyPI `pydsm` (https://pypi.org/project/pydsm/)
- **Install:** `pip install pydsm`
- **Latest release:** 0.15.2 (2025-08)
- **Last commit:** 2025-08-22 (inactive since 2025-08)
- **GitHub stars:** 22
- **Maintainers:** Sergio Callegari
- **AI assistance:** not stated
- **How to cite:** The README asks users to cite two papers by Callegari and Bizzarri on the design of ΔΣ modulators (the journal versions). Name the version or commit you used.
- **Entry checked:** 2026-10-06

## What it implements

| Metric | Edition | Functions | Status | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Equal-loudness contours](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/equal-loudness-contours.html) | [ISO 226:2003](https://www.iso.org/standard/34222.html) (tabled and interpolated contours; optional 20 kHz extension) | `pydsm.iso226` | available | not stated | — |

## How it was validated

As reported by the project; LISQM has not run the code. Two implementations that agree can still share the same error.

The project does not say how any of these were validated.

## Notes

- The `pydsm.iso226` module was added in August 2013 and cites Jeff Tackett's 2005 MATLAB ISO 226 code. Its tables can optionally be extended with a data point at 20 kHz.
- A standalone extraction of the module, [jacobbaylesssmc/iso226](https://github.com/jacobbaylesssmc/iso226) (GPL-3.0, two commits on 2019-07-09), also exists.

## Before you rely on it

- ISO 226:2003 was withdrawn in 2023 and replaced by ISO 226:2023; the module follows the 2003 edition.

## Sources

- https://github.com/sergiocallegari/PyDSM
- https://github.com/sergiocallegari/PyDSM/blob/main/README.md
- https://github.com/sergiocallegari/PyDSM/blob/main/src/pydsm/iso226.py
- https://pypi.org/project/pydsm/
- https://github.com/jacobbaylesssmc/iso226
