# MetaSona

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/metasona.html

**Newly released project.** First released in September 2026. Not yet seen to be widely used in the community. Check its validation before relying on it.

C library with a typed Python interface and prebuilt wheels, written to make repeated psychoacoustic analysis fast. Covers Zwicker loudness, DIN 45692 sharpness, Daniel–Weber roughness, Aures tonality and ECMA-418-2:2025 loudness, roughness and tonality.

- **Repository:** https://github.com/huaaudio/metasona
- **Documentation:** https://github.com/huaaudio/metasona/tree/main/docs
- **Language:** C, Python
- **Kind:** Library/Toolbox (Functions to call from your own code: a Python package, a MATLAB toolbox, or a C, C++, C#, Rust or Julia library.)
- **Group:** newly released (First released less than about a year ago, and not yet seen to be widely used in the community.)
- **Licence:** GPL-3.0-only AND Apache-2.0 AND BSD-3-Clause AND MIT — The combined distribution is GPL-3.0. MetaSona's own code is Apache-2.0; the ECMA-418-2 kernels (from SQAT/RefMap) and the current Aures tonality port are GPL-3.0; SQAT's ISO 532-1 filtering (BSD-3-Clause), SQAT's Daniel & Weber roughness (MIT), MoSQITo data (Apache-2.0) and PocketFFT (BSD-3-Clause) keep their notices.
- **Package:** PyPI `metasona` (https://pypi.org/project/metasona/)
- **Install:** `pip install metasona`
- **Latest release:** v0.2.2 (2026-09)
- **Last commit:** 2026-09-25 (active)
- **GitHub stars:** 1
- **Maintainers:** Jiahua Zhang
- **AI assistance:** disclosed — README and NOTICE state that it was developed with assistance from OpenAI Codex.
- **How to cite:** The project does not say how to cite it. Cite the repository with the version or commit you used.
- **Entry checked:** 2026-10-08

## What it implements

| Metric | Edition | Functions | Status | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Zwicker loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html) | [ISO 532-1:2017](https://www.iso.org/standard/63077.html) (stationary and time-varying; also from 28 third-octave levels; since 0.1.0) | `stationary_loudness`, `time_varying_loudness`, `loudness_from_levels` | available | compared with MoSQITo (its source) | — |
| [Sottek Hearing Model loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-ecma-418-2.html) | [ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_4th_edition_june_2025.pdf) (Clause 8 loudness with tonal/noise separation; mono or stereo; since 0.2.0) | `loudness_ecma`, `ecma_tonal_analysis` | available | compared with SQAT (its source) | Adapted from the SQAT/RefMap MATLAB code by Lotinga and Torjussen. |
| [Sharpness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/sharpness.html) | [DIN 45692:2009](https://www.dinmedia.de/en/standard/din-45692/117635111) (from specific loudness; since 0.1.0) | `sharpness_din45692` | available | not stated | — |
| [Roughness (Daniel & Weber)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/roughness-daniel-weber.html) | [Daniel & Weber (1997)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/standards.html#ref-daniel-weber-1997) (since 0.1.0) | `roughness_daniel_weber` | available | compared with SQAT (its source) | Follows SQAT revision `e6228b78`, which includes SQAT's September 2026 rewrite but not its later fix to the Terhardt filter bank (PR #77). |
| [Sottek Hearing Model roughness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/roughness-ecma-418-2.html) | [ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_4th_edition_june_2025.pdf) (mono or stereo; optional entropy weighting not applied; since 0.2.0) | `roughness_ecma` | available | compared with SQAT (its source) | Uses the standard's 20 ms grid and nominal calibration factor, where SQAT uses a slightly adjusted calibration. |
| [Tonality (Aures)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tonality-aures.html) | [Aures (1985b)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/standards.html#ref-aures-1985-euphony) (since 0.1.0) | `tonality_aures` | available | compared with SQAT (its source) | Follows SQAT's September 2026 revision (250 ms Hann windows, 125 ms hop). |
| [Sottek Hearing Model tonality](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tonality-ecma-418-2.html) | [ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_4th_edition_june_2025.pdf) (mono or stereo; since 0.2.0) | `tonality_ecma`, `ecma_tonal_analysis` | available | compared with SQAT (its source) | — |

## How it was validated

As reported by the project; LISQM has not run the code. Two implementations that agree can still share the same error.

- [Zwicker loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html), ISO 532-1:2017: compared with **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)** (its source)
  - Ported or adapted from **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)** and **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)**. It was compared with the code it was ported from, which checks the port only.
  - Model tables taken from MoSQITo were checked element by element; one upper-slope value (0.22) follows the ISO 532-1 reference C table where MoSQITo uses 0.24.
  - The project says that detailed validation and reference comparisons are kept outside the repository; the results are not published. The README says standards conformance has not been established.
- [Sottek Hearing Model loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-ecma-418-2.html), ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.); [Sottek Hearing Model roughness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/roughness-ecma-418-2.html), ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.); [Sottek Hearing Model tonality](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tonality-ecma-418-2.html), ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.): compared with **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** (its source)
  - Ported or adapted from **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)**. It was compared with the code it was ported from, which checks the port only.
  - The project says that detailed validation and reference comparisons are kept outside the repository; the results are not published.
- [Roughness (Daniel & Weber)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/roughness-daniel-weber.html), Daniel & Weber (1997): compared with **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** (its source)
  - Ported or adapted from **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** and **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)**. It was compared with the code it was ported from, which checks the port only.
  - The project says that detailed validation and reference comparisons are kept outside the repository; the results are not published.
  - The API documentation calls the function experimental and says normative validation remains open.
- [Tonality (Aures)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tonality-aures.html), Aures (1985b): compared with **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** (its source)
  - Ported or adapted from **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)**. It was compared with the code it was ported from, which checks the port only.
  - The project calls its source-based Python comparisons "development checks, not an executed MATLAB/Octave validation"; exact agreement with MATLAB is not established.
  - The results are not published.

Not stated for Sharpness · DIN 45692:2009.

## Before you compare numbers

Implementations of the same metric can give different numbers without either being wrong. Check these choices first.

- Expects calibrated sound pressure in pascals.
- The C functions require 48 kHz input; the Python interface resamples other rates to 48 kHz (SciPy `resample_poly`).
- `time_skip_s` (default 0 s) leaves out the start of the signal from the reported frames; the computation still runs over the whole signal. Time-varying results include every complete frame, labelled at frame centres, which differs from SQAT's handling of the last frame and of time stamps.


## Notes

- First commit and first PyPI release on 2026-09-16.
- Ports SQAT revision `e6228b78` (2026-09-15), which includes the Daniel & Weber rewrite (#65) and the Aures tonality fixes (#66–#73) but not PR #77 (2026-09-17), a fix to the Terhardt filter bank that Daniel & Weber roughness uses. Model data come from MoSQITo; differences to both are listed in [THIRD_PARTY.md](https://github.com/huaaudio/metasona/blob/main/THIRD_PARTY.md).
- The README reports speed-ups over MoSQITo 1.2.1 (e.g. 73× for time-varying loudness on its benchmark signal).

## Before you rely on it

- Very new (first released in September 2026) and not yet seen to be widely used in the community; no independent verification has been published.
- The README calls the current version experimental, particularly roughness and tonality, and says standards conformance has not been established.
- Comparisons with SQAT and MoSQITo are described as kept outside the package repository, and the third-party notes say exact agreement with the MATLAB code is not established.

## Sources

- https://github.com/huaaudio/metasona/blob/main/README.md
- https://github.com/huaaudio/metasona/blob/main/THIRD_PARTY.md
- https://github.com/huaaudio/metasona/blob/main/NOTICE
- https://pypi.org/project/metasona/
- https://github.com/huaaudio/metasona/blob/main/python/metasona/_abi.py
- https://github.com/huaaudio/metasona/blob/main/docs/c-api.md
- https://github.com/huaaudio/metasona/blob/main/docs/python-api.md

# iso532-1-rs

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/iso532-1-rs.html

**Newly released project.** First version tagged in July 2026. Not yet seen to be widely used in the community. Check its validation before relying on it.

Rust engine (README title "ISO532") for ISO 532-1:2017 Zwicker loudness: stationary, time-varying and a streaming interface, with a C ABI and a Python binding (PyO3/maturin). Only ISO 532-1 loudness is implemented.

- **Repository:** https://github.com/cclin99/iso532-1-rs
- **Language:** Rust, C, Python
- **Kind:** Library/Toolbox (Functions to call from your own code: a Python package, a MATLAB toolbox, or a C, C++, C#, Rust or Julia library.)
- **Group:** newly released (First released less than about a year ago, and not yet seen to be widely used in the community.)
- **Licence:** Apache-2.0
- **Latest release:** 0.1.0 (2026-07)
- **Last commit:** 2026-07-21 (active)
- **GitHub stars:** 1
- **Maintainers:** cclin99
- **AI assistance:** disclosed — The README describes "An AI-assisted Rust engine" developed "through human-directed AI collaboration"; 16 commits from July 2026 carry Claude co-author lines, and the repository contains Codex agent configuration.
- **How to cite:** The repository has a [CITATION.cff](https://github.com/cclin99/iso532-1-rs/blob/main/CITATION.cff) file. Name the version or commit you used.
- **Entry checked:** 2026-10-06

## What it implements

| Metric | Edition | Functions | Status | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Zwicker loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html) | [ISO 532-1:2017](https://www.iso.org/standard/63077.html) (stationary, time-varying and streaming; since 0.1.0) | `loudness_zwst`, `loudness_zwtv`, `ZwtvStream` | available | standard or paper data; also compared with MoSQITo | Python uses the same names (`iso532.loudness_zwst` …); the C API has `iso532_loudness_zwst`, `iso532_loudness_zwtv` and `iso532_stream_*`. |

## How it was validated

As reported by the project; LISQM has not run the code. Two implementations that agree can still share the same error.

- [Zwicker loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html), ISO 532-1:2017: standard or paper data; also compared with **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)**
  - Parity tests with MoSQITo 1.2.1 on nine synthetic and Annex B signals (worst reported difference 1.3e-9).
  - Checked separately against ISO 532-1 Annex B: the README reports stationary offsets of about +0.82 % and −0.76 % for signals 3 and 5, inside the standard's tolerance, and details signals 3, 5 and 10 in docs/ISO-ANNEXB-NUMERICAL-ERROR-2026-07-04.md.

## Notes

- Not published on crates.io or PyPI (the crate and the Python module are named `iso532`). Version 0.1.0 exists as a git tag of 2026-07-19 and in CHANGELOG.md and CITATION.cff; there is no GitHub release.
- MoSQITo 1.2.1 is the reference implementation, credited in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md; the stationary front end follows MoSQITo's `noct_spectrum` path.
- Expects calibrated pressure in pascals at 48 kHz. The stream outputs sone, phon and status flags on a 2 ms grid and marks the first 580 frames as warm-up.

## Before you rely on it

- The MoSQITo golden data and the ISO Annex B fixtures are gitignored and must be regenerated locally; the README says "Hosted CI does not by itself prove the local MoSQITo/Annex B golden chain".

## Sources

- https://github.com/cclin99/iso532-1-rs
- https://github.com/cclin99/iso532-1-rs/blob/main/README.md
- https://github.com/cclin99/iso532-1-rs/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
- https://github.com/cclin99/iso532-1-rs/blob/main/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md
- https://github.com/cclin99/iso532-1-rs/blob/main/docs/ISO-ANNEXB-NUMERICAL-ERROR-2026-07-04.md

# Kirin Hypha

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/kirin-hypha.html

**Newly released project.** First public commit in April 2026; v1.0.0 was released in May 2026. Not yet seen to be widely used in the community. Check its validation before relying on it.

Free PRE/POST measurement plug-in for mixing and mastering. Besides programme loudness (LUFS, ITU-R BS.1770), true peak and spectrum, it computes ISO 532-1 time-varying Zwicker loudness and DIN 45692 sharpness, ported from MoSQITo to Rust.

- **Repository:** https://github.com/heyalohaloha/kirin_hypha
- **Language:** Rust
- **Kind:** Plug-in (Runs inside other software: a plug-in for an audio workstation, or a Pure Data external.)
- **Group:** newly released (First released less than about a year ago, and not yet seen to be widely used in the community.)
- **Licence:** GPL-3.0
- **Latest release:** v1.1.50 (2026-09)
- **Last commit:** 2026-10-07 (active)
- **Maintainers:** Daisuke Nishio
- **AI assistance:** disclosed — The repository contains `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` files (instructions for AI coding agents), and its design notes refer to Claude Code and Codex work branches.
- **How to cite:** The project does not say how to cite it. Cite the repository with the version or commit you used.
- **Entry checked:** 2026-10-07

## What it implements

| Metric | Edition | Functions | Status | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Zwicker loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html) | [ISO 532-1:2017](https://www.iso.org/standard/63077.html) (time-varying, per channel at 48 kHz; stored in the recorded data; since 1.0.0) | `kirin_measure::phase_d` | available | compared with MoSQITo (its source) | Ported from MoSQITo v1.2.1. |
| [Sharpness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/sharpness.html) | [DIN 45692:2009](https://www.dinmedia.de/en/standard/din-45692/117635111) (from the time-varying specific loudness; shown in the plug-in; since 1.0.0) | `kirin_measure::phase_d::sharpness` | available | compared with MoSQITo (its source) | — |

## How it was validated

As reported by the project; LISQM has not run the code. Two implementations that agree can still share the same error.

- [Zwicker loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html), ISO 532-1:2017: compared with **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)** (its source)
  - Ported or adapted from **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)**. It was compared with the code it was ported from, which checks the port only.
  - Tests assert specific loudness within a relative 1e-3 of MoSQITo.
- [Sharpness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/sharpness.html), DIN 45692:2009: compared with **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)** (its source)
  - Ported or adapted from **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)**. It was compared with the code it was ported from, which checks the port only.
  - Tests assert agreement with MoSQITo within 0.05 acum.

## Notes

- The loudness and sharpness code is a port of MoSQITo v1.2.1 (`loudness_zwtv` and its stages); the sources and changes are listed in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.
- Zwicker loudness N is computed and stored in the recorded data but is not one of the plug-in's display cells; sharpness is shown. For several channels, both are computed per channel and averaged.
- Programme loudness (LUFS) and true peak follow ITU-R BS.1770, which is outside the scope of this list.

## Before you rely on it

- The loudness engine works on mono audio at 48 kHz; the plug-in measures each input channel separately.

## Sources

- https://github.com/heyalohaloha/kirin_hypha/blob/main/README.md

- https://github.com/heyalohaloha/kirin_hypha/tree/main/crates/kirin_measure/src/phase_d

# Mosqito.NET

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito-net.html

**Newly released project.** First published on GitHub in April 2026. Not yet seen to be widely used in the community. Check its validation before relying on it.

C# (.NET 8) port of MoSQITo 1.2.1 with the same metrics: ISO 532-1 loudness, ECMA-418-2 (2nd edition) loudness and roughness, DIN 45692 sharpness, Daniel & Weber roughness, and ECMA-74 tone-to-noise and prominence ratios.

- **Repository:** https://github.com/onur-akaydin/Mosqito.NET
- **Language:** C#
- **Kind:** Library/Toolbox (Functions to call from your own code: a Python package, a MATLAB toolbox, or a C, C++, C#, Rust or Julia library.)
- **Group:** newly released (First released less than about a year ago, and not yet seen to be widely used in the community.)
- **Licence:** Apache-2.0 — NOTICE.md states that it is derived from MoSQITo 1.2.1 (Apache-2.0).
- **Latest release:** no release
- **Last commit:** 2026-06-07 (active)
- **Maintainers:** onur-akaydin
- **AI assistance:** disclosed — The README says the port "was produced largely with AI assistance (Claude)"; most commits of 16 and 17 April 2026 have Claude as co-author.
- **How to cite:** The project does not say how to cite it. Cite the repository with the version or commit you used.
- **Entry checked:** 2026-10-07

## What it implements

| Metric | Edition | Functions | Status | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Zwicker loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html) | [ISO 532-1:2017](https://www.iso.org/standard/63077.html) (stationary (also per segment and from a spectrum) and time-varying) | `Sq.LoudnessZwst`, `Sq.LoudnessZwstFreq`, `Sq.LoudnessZwstPerSeg`, `Sq.LoudnessZwtv` | available | standard or paper data; also compared with MoSQITo (its source) | — |
| [Sottek Hearing Model loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-ecma-418-2.html) | [ECMA-418-2:2022 (2nd ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_2nd_edition_december_2022.pdf) (Clause 5 hearing-model loudness only, as in MoSQITo) | `Sq.LoudnessEcma` | available | compared with MoSQITo (its source) | — |
| [Sharpness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/sharpness.html) | [DIN 45692:2009](https://www.dinmedia.de/en/standard/din-45692/117635111) (weightings: DIN 45692, Aures, von Bismarck, Fastl) | `Sq.SharpnessDinSt`, `Sq.SharpnessDinTv`, `Sq.SharpnessDinPerSeg`, `Sq.SharpnessDinFreq` | available | compared with MoSQITo (its source) | — |
| [Roughness (Daniel & Weber)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/roughness-daniel-weber.html) | [Daniel & Weber (1997)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/standards.html#ref-daniel-weber-1997) | `Sq.RoughnessDw`, `Sq.RoughnessDwFreq` | available | compared with MoSQITo (its source) | — |
| [Sottek Hearing Model roughness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/roughness-ecma-418-2.html) | [ECMA-418-2:2022 (2nd ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_2nd_edition_december_2022.pdf) | `Sq.RoughnessEcma` | available | compared with MoSQITo (its source) | — |
| [Tone-to-noise ratio and prominence ratio](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tone-to-noise-prominence-ratio.html) | [ECMA-74:2019 (17th ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-74/) | `Sq.TnrEcmaSt`, `Sq.TnrEcmaFreq`, `Sq.TnrEcmaPerSeg`, `Sq.PrEcmaSt`, `Sq.PrEcmaFreq`, `Sq.PrEcmaPerSeg` | available | compared with MoSQITo (its source) | The README cites ECMA-74 Annex D. |
| [Equal-loudness contours](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/equal-loudness-contours.html) | [ISO 226:2003](https://www.iso.org/standard/34222.html) | `Sq.EqualLoudnessContours` | available | not stated | Code comments say ISO 226:1987, but the tables are ported from MoSQITo, whose code follows Jeff Tackett's ISO 226:2003 implementation. |

## How it was validated

As reported by the project; LISQM has not run the code. Two implementations that agree can still share the same error.

- [Zwicker loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html), ISO 532-1:2017: standard or paper data; also compared with **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)** (its source)
  - Ported or adapted from **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)**. It was compared with the code it was ported from, which checks the port only.
  - Unit tests ported from MoSQITo compare stationary loudness with ISO 532-1 Annex B values.
  - Every public function is compared with the output of Python MoSQITo for seven WAV files (three of them ISO 532-1 test signals), within 1 % (0.5 dB for levels).
- [Sottek Hearing Model loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-ecma-418-2.html), ECMA-418-2:2022 (2nd ed.); [Sharpness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/sharpness.html), DIN 45692:2009; [Roughness (Daniel & Weber)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/roughness-daniel-weber.html), Daniel & Weber (1997); [Sottek Hearing Model roughness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/roughness-ecma-418-2.html), ECMA-418-2:2022 (2nd ed.); [Tone-to-noise ratio and prominence ratio](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tone-to-noise-prominence-ratio.html), ECMA-74:2019 (17th ed.): compared with **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)** (its source)
  - Ported or adapted from **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)**. It was compared with the code it was ported from, which checks the port only.
  - Every public function is compared with the output of Python MoSQITo for seven WAV files (three of them ISO 532-1 test signals), within 1 % (0.5 dB for levels); MoSQITo's unit tests are ported too.

Not stated for Equal-loudness contours · ISO 226:2003.

## Before you compare numbers

Implementations of the same metric can give different numbers without either being wrong. Check these choices first.

- Time-varying loudness and ECMA-418-2 roughness resample input at any other rate to 48 kHz, and stationary loudness resamples rates below 48 kHz; MoSQITo rejects rates above 48 kHz for time-varying loudness.


## Notes

- First commit on 2026-04-16; 16 commits, the latest on 2026-06-07. There is no GitHub release.
- Also ports MoSQITo's speech intelligibility index (ANSI S3.5), which is outside the scope of this list.

## Before you rely on it

- Very new and not yet seen to be widely used in the community; the README asks users to validate results against their own reference data before relying on them.
- Its ECMA-418-2 functions follow the 2nd edition (2022), two editions behind the current one, as in MoSQITo.

## Sources

- https://github.com/onur-akaydin/Mosqito.NET
- https://github.com/onur-akaydin/Mosqito.NET/blob/master/README.md
- https://github.com/onur-akaydin/Mosqito.NET/blob/master/NOTICE.md
- https://github.com/onur-akaydin/Mosqito.NET/commits/master/
- https://github.com/Eomys/MoSQITo/issues/98

# NumpyLibforPsychoAcoustic

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/numpylib-psychoacoustic.html

**Newly released project.** First published on GitHub in November 2025. Not yet seen to be widely used in the community. Check its validation before relying on it.

Python (NumPy) adaptation of loudness models from the Auditory Modeling Toolbox (AMT), written as a second-year student project at Mines School of Nancy: the stationary model of Moore, Glasberg & Baer (1997) and the time-varying model of Glasberg & Moore (2002).

- **Repository:** https://github.com/Ryrybros/NumpyLibforPsychoAcoustic
- **Language:** Python
- **Kind:** Research code (Code published with a study, a thesis or a student project, to run or adapt; not packaged as a library.)
- **Group:** newly released (First released less than about a year ago, and not yet seen to be widely used in the community.)
- **Licence:** none
- **Latest release:** no release
- **Last commit:** 2026-06-07 (active)
- **GitHub stars:** 0
- **Maintainers:** Ryrybros
- **AI assistance:** not stated
- **How to cite:** The project does not say how to cite it. Cite the repository with the version or commit you used.
- **Entry checked:** 2026-10-06

## What it implements

| Metric | Edition | Functions | Status | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Moore–Glasberg loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg.html) | [Moore, Glasberg & Baer (1997)](https://aes2.org/publications/elibrary-page/?id=10272) | `model.moore1997`, `equalSones.getEqualSones` | available | standard or paper data; also compared with AMT (its source) | — |
| [Time-varying loudness (Moore–Glasberg–Schlittenlacher)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg-time-varying.html) | [Glasberg & Moore (2002)](https://aes2.org/publications/elibrary-page/?id=11081) | `model.glasberg2002` | available | not stated | Present in the code but not described in the implementation document. |

## How it was validated

As reported by the project; LISQM has not run the code. Two implementations that agree can still share the same error.

- [Moore–Glasberg loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg.html), Moore, Glasberg & Baer (1997): standard or paper data; also compared with [AMT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/amt.html) (its source)
  - Ported or adapted from [AMT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/amt.html). It was compared with the code it was ported from, which checks the port only.
  - The implementation document says the model is compared with the results shown in the original article (plots of its Fig. 8 and Fig. 12).
  - Numerical error reports (PDF) compare intermediate arrays, such as the outer- and middle-ear filter, with AMT's MATLAB output.

Not stated for Time-varying loudness (Moore–Glasberg–Schlittenlacher) · Glasberg & Moore (2002).

## Notes

- The implementation document says the Moore (1997) model is "the same code as the amt-toolbox one"; the data preparation follows AMT's Glasberg (2002) data function.
- GitHub labels the repository TypeScript because of the React/Vite user interface in UI/Model_UI; the models are Python.

## Before you rely on it

- No licence file, so reuse is not permitted by default.
- The implementation document describes only the Moore (1997) model as implemented; `glasberg2002` is in the code (with data/Glasberg2002.json) but not documented.

## Sources

- https://github.com/Ryrybros/NumpyLibforPsychoAcoustic
- https://github.com/Ryrybros/NumpyLibforPsychoAcoustic/blob/main/README.md
- https://github.com/Ryrybros/NumpyLibforPsychoAcoustic/blob/main/Documentation/Implementation_documentation.pdf
- https://github.com/Ryrybros/NumpyLibforPsychoAcoustic/tree/main/Numerical_error_report

# phonometry

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html

**Newly released project.** Its psychoacoustics module was first released in July 2026 (version 3.1.0). Not yet seen to be widely used in the community. Check its validation before relying on it.

Python acoustics library (formerly PyOctaveBand) that added a large psychoacoustics module in July 2026: ISO 532-1, -2 and -3 loudness, ECMA-418-2:2025 loudness, tonality, roughness and fluctuation strength (monaural), DIN 45692 sharpness, Osses fluctuation strength, ECMA-418-1:2024 TNR/PR, tonal audibility, impulsiveness, EPNL and ISO 226:2023. Only NumPy and SciPy are required.

- **Repository:** https://github.com/jmrplens/phonometry
- **Documentation:** https://jmrplens.github.io/phonometry/
- **Language:** Python
- **Kind:** Library/Toolbox (Functions to call from your own code: a Python package, a MATLAB toolbox, or a C, C++, C#, Rust or Julia library.)
- **Group:** newly released (First released less than about a year ago, and not yet seen to be widely used in the community.)
- **Licence:** MIT
- **Package:** PyPI `phonometry` (https://pypi.org/project/phonometry/)
- **Install:** `pip install phonometry`
- **Latest release:** v3.3.0 (2026-07); pre-release 4.0.0rc1 (2026-09)
- **Last commit:** 2026-10-06 (active)
- **GitHub stars:** 119
- **Maintainers:** José M. Requena Plens
- **AI assistance:** disclosed — The draft paper (`paper/paper.md`) has an AI usage disclosure: language models drafted code, tests and documentation from the author's clause-by-clause readings, under the author's direction and review. 34 commits from July 2026 contain Claude Code session links.
- **How to cite:** Software DOI: [10.5281/zenodo.21215280](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21215280). The repository has a [CITATION.cff](https://github.com/jmrplens/phonometry/blob/main/CITATION.cff) file. Name the version or commit you used.
- **Entry checked:** 2026-10-08

## What it implements

| Metric | Edition | Functions | Status | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Zwicker loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html) | [ISO 532-1:2017](https://www.iso.org/standard/63077.html) (stationary and time-varying; since 3.1.0) | `loudness_zwicker`, `loudness_zwicker_from_spectrum` | available | standard or paper data | — |
| [Moore–Glasberg loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg.html) | [ISO 532-2:2017](https://www.iso.org/standard/63078.html) (with binaural inhibition; since 3.1.0) | `loudness_moore_glasberg`, `loudness_moore_glasberg_from_spectrum`, `loudness_moore_glasberg_from_third_octave` | available | standard or paper data | — |
| [Time-varying loudness (Moore–Glasberg–Schlittenlacher)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg-time-varying.html) | [ISO 532-3:2023](https://www.iso.org/standard/69856.html) (since 3.1.0) | `loudness_moore_glasberg_time` | available | standard or paper data | — |
| [Sottek Hearing Model loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-ecma-418-2.html) | [ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_4th_edition_june_2025.pdf) (mono only; since 3.1.0) | `loudness_ecma` | available | standard or paper data (calibration signal only; outside the allowed adjustment) | — |
| [Sharpness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/sharpness.html) | [DIN 45692:2009](https://www.dinmedia.de/en/standard/din-45692/117635111) (also the informative Aures and von Bismarck variants; since 3.1.0) | `sharpness_din`, `sharpness_din_from_specific` | available | standard or paper data | — |
| [Sottek Hearing Model roughness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/roughness-ecma-418-2.html) | [ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_4th_edition_june_2025.pdf) (mono only; no entropy weighting; since 3.1.0) | `roughness_ecma` | available | standard or paper data (calibration signal only) | — |
| [Fluctuation strength (Osses et al.)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/fluctuation-strength-osses.html) | [Osses et al. (2016)](https://doi.org/10.1121/2.0000410) (since 3.1.0) | `fluctuation_strength` | available | standard or paper data; also compared with SQAT | — |
| [Fluctuation strength (Osses et al.)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/fluctuation-strength-osses.html) | [Fastl & Zwicker (2007)](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-540-68888-4) (closed-form expression for amplitude-modulated noise; since 3.1.0) | `fluctuation_strength_am_noise` | available | standard or paper data | — |
| [Sottek Hearing Model fluctuation strength](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/fluctuation-strength-ecma-418-2.html) | [ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_4th_edition_june_2025.pdf) (mono only; since 3.3.0) | `fluctuation_strength_ecma` | available | standard or paper data (calibration signal only) | Misprints found in Clause 9 are listed in the project's errata. |
| [Sottek Hearing Model tonality](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tonality-ecma-418-2.html) | [ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_4th_edition_june_2025.pdf) (mono only; since 3.1.0) | `tonality_ecma` | available | standard or paper data (calibration signal only) | — |
| [Tone-to-noise ratio and prominence ratio](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tone-to-noise-prominence-ratio.html) | [ECMA-418-1:2024 (3rd ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-1_3rd_edition_december_2024.pdf) (since 3.1.0) | `tone_to_noise_ratio`, `prominence_ratio`, `assess_tones` | available | standard or paper data (formula examples; no published TNR or PR value) | The "prominent" flag applies the numeric criterion only. |
| [Audibility of tones in noise (ISO/TS 20065)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tonal-audibility-iso-20065.html) | [ISO/PAS 20065:2016](https://www.iso.org/standard/66941.html) (since 3.1.0) | `tone_audibility`, `analyze_spectrum`, `audibility_from_levels`, `mean_audibility`, `audibility_uncertainty` | available | standard or paper data; also compared with DIN 45681 Annex J reference program | Follows the 2016 PAS, not the 2022 TS. Does not apply the A-weighting required by clause 5.3.2. DIN 45681 itself is not implemented. |
| [Tonal audibility (ISO 1996-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tonal-audibility-iso-1996-2.html) | [ISO 1996-2:2017](https://www.iso.org/standard/59766.html) (Annex K survey method and Table J.1; in the `phonometry.environment` namespace) | — | available | not stated | — |
| [Tonal audibility (ISO 1996-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tonal-audibility-iso-1996-2.html) | [ISO 1996-2:2007](https://www.iso.org/standard/41860.html) (Annex C; in the `phonometry.environment` namespace) | — | available | not stated | — |
| [Tonal audibility of wind turbines (IEC 61400-11)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tonal-audibility-iec-61400-11.html) | [IEC 61400-11:2012+AMD1:2018](https://webstore.iec.ch/en/publication/63367) | `wind_turbine_tonality` | available | not stated | — |
| [Impulse prominence](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/impulsiveness.html) | [ISO/PAS 1996-3:2022](https://www.iso.org/standard/77035.html) (in the `phonometry.environment` namespace) | — | available | not stated | — |
| [Impulse prominence](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/impulsiveness.html) | [NT ACOU 112](http://www.nordtest.info/wp/2002/05/01/acoustics-prominence-of-impulsive-sounds-and-for-adjustment-of-laeq-nt-acou-112/) (in the `phonometry.environment` namespace) | — | available | not stated | — |
| [Psychoacoustic annoyance](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/psychoacoustic-annoyance.html) | [Zwicker & Fastl (1999)](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-662-09562-1) (since 3.1.0) | `psychoacoustic_annoyance`, `psychoacoustic_annoyance_from_signal` | available | own tests only | Follows Eqs. 16.2–16.4 of Fastl & Zwicker (2007), the textbook form of Widmann's model. |
| [Equal-loudness contours](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/equal-loudness-contours.html) | [ISO 226:2023](https://www.iso.org/standard/83117.html) (since 3.1.0) | `equal_loudness_contour`, `equal_loudness_contours`, `loudness_level`, `hearing_threshold` | available | standard or paper data | — |
| [Perceived noise level and EPNL](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/epnl.html) | [ICAO Annex 16, Vol. I](https://store.icao.int/en/annex-16-environmental-protection-volume-i-aircraft-noise) (PNL, PNLT and EPNL, in the `phonometry.aircraft` namespace) | — | available | standard or paper data | — |

## How it was validated

As reported by the project; LISQM has not run the code. Two implementations that agree can still share the same error.

- [Zwicker loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html), ISO 532-1:2017: standard or paper data
  - Ported or adapted from ISO 532-1 Annex A reference program.
  - Annex B test signals are used in the tests.
- [Moore–Glasberg loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg.html), ISO 532-2:2017: standard or paper data
  - The documentation says it reproduces the Annex B tone and broadband cases to within a percent or two.
- [Time-varying loudness (Moore–Glasberg–Schlittenlacher)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg-time-varying.html), ISO 532-3:2023: standard or paper data
  - A documented deviation: the Annex B WAV-file cases are not reproduced, and Annex C values are used instead.
- [Sottek Hearing Model loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-ecma-418-2.html), ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.): standard or paper data (calibration signal only; outside the allowed adjustment)
  - Checked at the calibration signal only, where it gives 0.9843 sone_HMS (−1.55 %).
- [Sharpness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/sharpness.html), DIN 45692:2009: standard or paper data
  - Checked with the DIN 45692 reference signal and Tables A.2 and A.3.
- [Sottek Hearing Model roughness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/roughness-ecma-418-2.html), ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.); [Sottek Hearing Model tonality](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tonality-ecma-418-2.html), ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.): standard or paper data (calibration signal only)
  - Checked at the calibration signal only.
- [Fluctuation strength (Osses et al.)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/fluctuation-strength-osses.html), Osses et al. (2016): standard or paper data; also compared with **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)**
  - Compared with the literature values in Table 1 of Osses et al. (2016): for amplitude-modulated 70 dB tones the Pearson correlation is about 0.98, within a factor of about 2.1 at every point. SQAT's `FluctuationStrength_Osses2016` was consulted as a numeric reference for the shape of the sweep.
  - Validated for amplitude modulation only; a steady 1 kHz tone reads about 0.09 vacil.
- [Fluctuation strength (Osses et al.)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/fluctuation-strength-osses.html), Fastl & Zwicker (2007): standard or paper data
  - A conformance row checks Eq. (10.2) of Fastl & Zwicker for amplitude-modulated broadband noise.
- [Sottek Hearing Model fluctuation strength](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/fluctuation-strength-ecma-418-2.html), ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.): standard or paper data (calibration signal only)
  - Checked at the calibration signal only (0.993 vacil_HMS).
- [Tone-to-noise ratio and prominence ratio](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tone-to-noise-prominence-ratio.html), ECMA-418-1:2024 (3rd ed.): standard or paper data (formula examples; no published TNR or PR value)
  - Tests check worked examples printed in ECMA-418-1:2024: the critical band at 500 Hz and 1 kHz (Clause 10, Formula 2), its band edges at 1 kHz (Clause 12.2) and the proximity spacing at 150 and 850 Hz (Clause 11.6, Formula 14).
  - TNR and PR of a 1 kHz tone in white noise are compared with the values expected from the standard's formulas (within 0.4 dB for TNR and 0.1 dB for PR); no TNR or PR value published in the standard is checked.
- [Audibility of tones in noise (ISO/TS 20065)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tonal-audibility-iso-20065.html), ISO/PAS 20065:2016: standard or paper data; also compared with DIN 45681 Annex J reference program
  - Reproduces the Annex E worked example.
  - Parts are checked against DIN 45681:2005 and its Annex J reference program.
- [Psychoacoustic annoyance](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/psychoacoustic-annoyance.html), Zwicker & Fastl (1999): own tests only
  - Tests compare one set of inputs (N5 = 30 sone, S = 2.0 acum, F = 0.5 vacil, R = 0.3 asper) with the value worked out by hand from Eqs. 16.2–16.4 (37.0478, within 0.001) and check the terms of the formula; no published example is used.
- [Equal-loudness contours](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/equal-loudness-contours.html), ISO 226:2023: standard or paper data
  - Tests compare 17 points of Table B.1 (20 to 90 phon, 20 Hz to 12.5 kHz) and 6 points of Table B.2 with the computed contours and loudness levels, within 0.05 dB or phon, and the hearing threshold with Table 1.
- [Perceived noise level and EPNL](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/epnl.html), ICAO Annex 16, Vol. I: standard or paper data
  - Tested with the EPNL example of ICAO Doc 9501 (Environmental Technical Manual).

Not stated for Tonal audibility (ISO 1996-2) · ISO 1996-2:2017; Tonal audibility (ISO 1996-2) · ISO 1996-2:2007; Tonal audibility of wind turbines (IEC 61400-11) · IEC 61400-11:2012+AMD1:2018; Impulse prominence · ISO/PAS 1996-3:2022; Impulse prominence · NT ACOU 112.

## Before you compare numbers

Implementations of the same metric can give different numbers without either being wrong. Check these choices first.

- [Time-varying loudness (Moore–Glasberg–Schlittenlacher)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg-time-varying.html) (ISO 532-3:2023): Documented deviation: it runs at the native sample rate instead of resampling to 32 kHz.

## Notes

- Renamed from PyOctaveBand (octave-band filtering) at 3.0.0 on 2026-07-06; the psychoacoustics module arrived in 3.1.0 on 2026-07-13. 873 of its 905 commits are from 2026.
- The README reports 1793 of 1793 conformance checks passing across 519 standards, generated by the project's own CI ([CONFORMANCE.md](https://github.com/jmrplens/phonometry/blob/main/docs/CONFORMANCE.md)).
- Keeps a public errata list of misprints found in standards, including ECMA-418-1:2024 and ECMA-418-2:2025 ([ERRATA.md](https://github.com/jmrplens/phonometry/blob/main/docs/ERRATA.md)).
- A JOSS-format paper draft exists in the repository; no published paper yet. Version 4.0 (release candidate since 2026-09-10) moves modules.
- Not implemented: Daniel & Weber roughness, Aures tonality, More and Di annoyance, and binaural combination for ECMA-418-2.

## Before you rely on it

- Very new (psychoacoustics module first released in July 2026) and not yet seen to be widely used in the community; no independent verification has been published.
- Single maintainer; all validation comes from the project's own tests.
- The ECMA-418-2 checks only use the calibration signals, and no comparison with another implementation is reported. Its loudness reads 0.984 sone_HMS at the calibration point, which its own documentation says is outside the adjustment the standard allows.
- Requires Python 3.13 or newer.

## Sources

- https://github.com/jmrplens/phonometry/blob/main/README.md
- https://github.com/jmrplens/phonometry/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
- https://github.com/jmrplens/phonometry/blob/main/docs/CONFORMANCE.md
- https://github.com/jmrplens/phonometry/blob/main/docs/ERRATA.md
- https://github.com/jmrplens/phonometry/blob/main/tests/psychoacoustics/quality/test_tonality.py
- https://github.com/jmrplens/phonometry/blob/main/tests/psychoacoustics/quality/test_annoyance.py
- https://github.com/jmrplens/phonometry/blob/main/tests/psychoacoustics/loudness/test_contours.py
- https://github.com/jmrplens/phonometry/blob/main/CITATION.cff
- https://github.com/jmrplens/phonometry/blob/main/paper/paper.md

# PsychoacousticMetrics.jl

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psychoacousticmetrics-jl.html

**Newly released project.** First registered in July 2026. Not yet seen to be widely used in the community. Check its validation before relying on it.

Julia package for the Zwicker family of sound-quality metrics on top of ZwickerLoudness.jl: DIN 45692:2009 sharpness (with Aures, von Bismarck and Fastl weightings), Daniel & Weber roughness, Osses et al. (2016) fluctuation strength and Widmann (1992) psychoacoustic annoyance.

- **Repository:** https://github.com/slink/PsychoacousticMetrics.jl
- **Language:** Julia
- **Kind:** Library/Toolbox (Functions to call from your own code: a Python package, a MATLAB toolbox, or a C, C++, C#, Rust or Julia library.)
- **Group:** newly released (First released less than about a year ago, and not yet seen to be widely used in the community.)
- **Licence:** MIT — Test data, the roughness implementation and several weighting tables are derived from MoSQITo (Apache-2.0); fluctuation-strength tables and annoyance constants reference SQAT (CC BY-NC 4.0) as factual data, without reusing its code (README, test/data/NOTICE).
- **Package:** Julia General `PsychoacousticMetrics` (https://juliahub.com/ui/Packages/General/PsychoacousticMetrics)
- **Install:** `using Pkg; Pkg.add("PsychoacousticMetrics")`
- **Latest release:** 0.5.0 (2026-09)
- **Last commit:** 2026-09-02 (active)
- **Maintainers:** slink
- **AI assistance:** not stated
- **How to cite:** The README links a [Zenodo DOI](https://zenodo.org/badge/latestdoi/1292553110) for the latest version. Name the version or commit you used.
- **Entry checked:** 2026-10-08

## What it implements

| Metric | Edition | Functions | Status | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Sharpness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/sharpness.html) | [DIN 45692:2009](https://www.dinmedia.de/en/standard/din-45692/117635111) (weightings: DIN 45692 (default), Aures, von Bismarck, Fastl; from a ZwickerLoudness.jl result; since 0.2.0) | `sharpness` | available | standard or paper data; also compared with MoSQITo | — |
| [Roughness (Daniel & Weber)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/roughness-daniel-weber.html) | [Daniel & Weber (1997)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/standards.html#ref-daniel-weber-1997) (since 0.2.0) | `roughness_dw` | available | standard or paper data; also compared with MoSQITo (its source) | — |
| [Fluctuation strength (Osses et al.)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/fluctuation-strength-osses.html) | [Osses et al. (2016)](https://doi.org/10.1121/2.0000410) (since 0.3.0) | `fluctuation_strength_osses` | available | reference code: SQAT | — |
| [Psychoacoustic annoyance](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/psychoacoustic-annoyance.html) | [Widmann (1992)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/standards.html#ref-widmann-1992) (percentile convention (N5, S5, R5, FS5) and a stationary approximation; since 0.4.0) | `psychoacoustic_annoyance_widmann` | available | compared with SQAT | — |

## How it was validated

As reported by the project; LISQM has not run the code. Two implementations that agree can still share the same error.

- [Sharpness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/sharpness.html), DIN 45692:2009: standard or paper data; also compared with **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)**
  - Tested against all 41 reference signals of DIN 45692:2009 chapter 6 (21 narrowband, 20 broadband) within the standard's tolerance of ±max(5 %, 0.05 acum).
  - Cross-checked against MoSQITo for all four weightings.
  - Total loudness N is computed as the Riemann sum over the 240-bin specific loudness (`0.1 * sum`), not taken from `ZwickerResult.loudness` (see the `sharpness` docstring).
- [Roughness (Daniel & Weber)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/roughness-daniel-weber.html), Daniel & Weber (1997): standard or paper data; also compared with **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)** (its source)
  - Ported or adapted from **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)**. It was compared with the code it was ported from, which checks the port only.
  - Tested against the Zwicker & Fastl reference curves on MoSQITo's validation grid (7 carrier × 11 modulation frequencies) within ±0.1 asper, and cross-checked against MoSQITo's `roughness_dw` on identical signals.
  - Five points at a 2 kHz carrier miss the ±0.1 asper gate. MoSQITo misses them by the same amount (and overshoots Daniel & Weber's own curve there by 15–31 %), so these five are checked for agreement with MoSQITo to 5e-3 asper instead.
  - Against the Daniel & Weber curves themselves, 63 of the 77 grid points are within 30 % of the reference (reported, not gated).
- [Fluctuation strength (Osses et al.)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/fluctuation-strength-osses.html), Osses et al. (2016): reference code: **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)**
  - Cross-checked against SQAT's `FluctuationStrength_Osses2016`, run under Octave, on identical signals: 26 cases, including all 18 points of Fastl & Zwicker's AM/FM reference grid (Osses 2018 thesis, Table B.1), each reproduced to a relative tolerance of 1e-6 (measured 3e-9).
  - The grid stimuli are synthesised following the Osses et al. (2016) validation files that SQAT's own validation reads; the tests also check that each synthetic stimulus gives the value SQAT gives on the real file (tones to 5e-3, noise to 25 % across random draws).
  - Against the published curves, 11 of the 18 points are within 30 %, and exactly those 11 are gated. The other seven are misses of the reference model itself (FM tones with a modulation frequency above 4 Hz overestimated three- to fourfold, thesis §B.4.1; the shoulder and tail points of AM tones and noise), which SQAT's own validation figures also show.
- [Psychoacoustic annoyance](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/psychoacoustic-annoyance.html), Widmann (1992): compared with **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)**
  - Cross-checked against SQAT's `PsychoacousticAnnoyance_Widmann1992`: an 840-case formula grid, reproduced bit-exactly, and six signal-level cases with SQAT's own N5, S5, R5 and FS5 vendored, so that every deviation is attributed to a component.
  - Checked at the published 1 au anchor (a 1 kHz tone at 40 dB SPL): on the 4 s cross-check case, the percentile convention lands 0.1 % from it and the stationary approximation 0.8 %; on the README's 5 s examples, 0.3 % and 1.4 %.

## Before you compare numbers

Implementations of the same metric can give different numbers without either being wrong. Check these choices first.

- [Fluctuation strength (Osses et al.)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/fluctuation-strength-osses.html) (Osses et al. (2016)): Needs audio at 44.1 or 48 kHz (an error otherwise); SQAT resamples other rates itself.
- [Psychoacoustic annoyance](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/psychoacoustic-annoyance.html) (Widmann (1992)): The percentile form needs 48 kHz input. Percentiles are Hyndman–Fan type 7 quantiles (linear interpolation); SQAT takes the nearest rank, which the README says differs by a full order-statistic step on the coarse fluctuation-strength track.

## Notes

- Roughness follows MoSQITo's `roughness_dw` ("as implemented by MoSQITo"), not Daniel and Weber's original code.
- Annoyance comes in two forms: the canonical percentile convention (N5, S5, R5 and FS5 from time-varying tracks, since 0.5.0) and a documented stationary approximation from whole-signal values (since 0.4.0).

## Sources

- https://github.com/slink/PsychoacousticMetrics.jl
- https://github.com/slink/PsychoacousticMetrics.jl/blob/main/README.md#conformance
- https://github.com/slink/PsychoacousticMetrics.jl/blob/main/test/data/NOTICE
- https://github.com/slink/PsychoacousticMetrics.jl/blob/main/Project.toml
- https://github.com/JuliaRegistries/General/tree/master/P/PsychoacousticMetrics

# SoundPalette

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/soundpalette.html

**Newly released project.** Its psychoacoustic metrics were added in July 2026 (v0.5.0). Not yet seen to be widely used in the community. Check its validation before relying on it.

C++ tool for game audio that analyses a folder of sound effects and draws each file as a glyph in a palette, built as a static library, a command-line tool (including a lint mode for CI) and a desktop app. Its psychoacoustic block reports ISO 532-1 loudness (N5), DIN 45692 sharpness, Daniel & Weber roughness and an experimental fluctuation strength.

- **Repository:** https://github.com/onyx-prismantium/soundpalette
- **Language:** C++
- **Kind:** Application (A program to run, with a graphical or command-line interface; no programming needed.)
- **Group:** newly released (First released less than about a year ago, and not yet seen to be widely used in the community.)
- **Licence:** FSL-1.1-Apache-2.0 — Functional Source License 1.1, a source-available licence that is not OSI-approved: it allows any use except a competing commercial product or service, and each release becomes Apache-2.0 two years after publication. The README states that releases up to and including v0.7.0 were published under Apache-2.0.
- **Latest release:** v0.8.0 (2026-09)
- **Last commit:** 2026-09-27 (active)
- **GitHub stars:** 0
- **Maintainers:** onyx-prismantium
- **AI assistance:** disclosed — The repository contains a `CLAUDE.md` file, and 49 of its 54 commits carry "Co-Authored-By: Claude" trailers.
- **How to cite:** The project does not say how to cite it. Cite the repository with the version or commit you used.
- **Entry checked:** 2026-10-06

## What it implements

| Metric | Edition | Functions | Status | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Zwicker loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html) | [ISO 532-1:2017](https://www.iso.org/standard/63077.html) (time-varying, reported as N5; monaural; since v0.5.0) | `sp::compute_psycho` | available | compared with MoSQITo | No MoSQITo code is ported. |
| [Sharpness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/sharpness.html) | [DIN 45692:2009](https://www.dinmedia.de/en/standard/din-45692/117635111) (from time-averaged specific loudness; since v0.5.0) | `sp::compute_psycho` | available | compared with MoSQITo | — |
| [Roughness (Daniel & Weber)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/roughness-daniel-weber.html) | [Daniel & Weber (1997)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/standards.html#ref-daniel-weber-1997) (since v0.5.0) | `sp::compute_psycho` | available | compared with MoSQITo | — |

## How it was validated

As reported by the project; LISQM has not run the code. Two implementations that agree can still share the same error.

- [Zwicker loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html), ISO 532-1:2017: compared with **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)**
  - Compared with MoSQITo 1.2.1 on calibrated test signals, used as a development-time reference (`NOTES.md`, `tools/psycho_oracle`).
- [Sharpness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/sharpness.html), DIN 45692:2009: compared with **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)**
  - Compared with MoSQITo 1.2.1 (tolerance ±5 %).
- [Roughness (Daniel & Weber)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/roughness-daniel-weber.html), Daniel & Weber (1997): compared with **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)**
  - Compared with MoSQITo 1.2.1 with a wider tolerance (±15 %); the README notes that published Daniel & Weber implementations differ by about 10–20 %.

## Notes

- The psychoacoustic metrics were added in v0.5.0 (July 2026), with "mapping v2".
- Calibration convention: a signal measuring −23 LUFS is assumed to play at `ref_spl` dB SPL (default 75, allowed range 60–85). The value is stored in every manifest and profile, and comparisons between different `ref_spl` values are refused.
- Also computes fluctuation strength in vacil, flagged as experimental; the README names no model for it.

## Before you rely on it

- The Functional Source License is source-available, not an OSI-approved open-source licence; check its competing-use restriction before reusing the code.
- `NOTES.md` documents simplifications: the third-octave bands come from an STFT rather than the standard's filter bank, the temporal processing was tuned to MoSQITo's N5 values, and roughness uses a fixed 70 Hz weighting and 28 instead of 47 channels. Tolerances (±5 % for stationary loudness and sharpness, ±10 % for N5, ±15 % for roughness) are the acceptance criterion.
- Loudness in sones depends on the declared playback level (`ref_spl`), not on a measured calibration.

## Sources

- https://github.com/onyx-prismantium/soundpalette
- https://github.com/onyx-prismantium/soundpalette/blob/main/README.md
- https://github.com/onyx-prismantium/soundpalette/blob/main/LICENSE.md
- https://github.com/onyx-prismantium/soundpalette/blob/main/NOTES.md
- https://github.com/onyx-prismantium/soundpalette/blob/main/core/include/soundpalette/psycho.h

# torch_amt

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/torch-amt.html

**Newly released project.** First released in February 2026. Not yet seen to be widely used in the community. Check its validation before relying on it.

PyTorch implementations of models from the MATLAB Auditory Modeling Toolbox (AMT), differentiable and able to run on GPU. For loudness it has the time-varying models of Glasberg & Moore (2002) and Moore et al. (2016, binaural).

- **Repository:** https://github.com/StefanoGiacomelli/torch_amt
- **Documentation:** https://torch-amt.readthedocs.io/
- **Language:** Python
- **Kind:** Library/Toolbox (Functions to call from your own code: a Python package, a MATLAB toolbox, or a C, C++, C#, Rust or Julia library.)
- **Group:** newly released (First released less than about a year ago, and not yet seen to be widely used in the community.)
- **Licence:** GPL-3.0-or-later
- **Package:** PyPI `torch-amt` (https://pypi.org/project/torch-amt/)
- **Install:** `pip install torch-amt`
- **Latest release:** 0.2.0 (2026-02)
- **Last commit:** 2026-03-19 (active)
- **GitHub stars:** 3
- **Maintainers:** Stefano Giacomelli
- **AI assistance:** not stated
- **How to cite:** The repository has a [CITATION.cff](https://github.com/StefanoGiacomelli/torch_amt/blob/main/CITATION.cff) file. Name the version or commit you used.
- **Entry checked:** 2026-10-06

## What it implements

| Metric | Edition | Functions | Status | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Time-varying loudness (Moore–Glasberg–Schlittenlacher)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg-time-varying.html) | [Moore et al. (2016)](https://doi.org/10.1177/2331216516682698) (binaural) | `torch_amt.models.Moore2016` | available | compared with AMT (its source) | Described as a "1:1 port" of AMT `moore2016`, with outer and middle ear per ANSI S3.4-2007 (docstring). |
| [Time-varying loudness (Moore–Glasberg–Schlittenlacher)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg-time-varying.html) | [Glasberg & Moore (2002)](https://aes2.org/publications/elibrary-page/?id=11081) (short-term and long-term loudness) | `torch_amt.models.Glasberg2002` | available | compared with AMT (its source) | Ported from AMT `glasberg2002`. |

## How it was validated

As reported by the project; LISQM has not run the code. Two implementations that agree can still share the same error.

- [Time-varying loudness (Moore–Glasberg–Schlittenlacher)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg-time-varying.html), Moore et al. (2016); [Time-varying loudness (Moore–Glasberg–Schlittenlacher)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg-time-varying.html), Glasberg & Moore (2002): compared with [AMT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/amt.html) (its source)
  - Ported or adapted from [AMT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/amt.html). It was compared with the code it was ported from, which checks the port only.
  - Agreement with AMT is claimed in the documentation, without stored reference data.

## Notes

- The README asks users to cite both the software and the AMT paper (Majdak, Hollomey & Baumgartner, 2022).
- The other models in the package (Dau1997, King2019, Osses2021, Paulick2024) are not psychoacoustic metrics in the sense of this list. There is no port of AMT's `moore1997`, `chen2011` or `bramslow2004`, and no roughness, sharpness or fluctuation strength.

## Before you rely on it

- The documentation claims "Matching MATLAB AMT v1.6.0 implementations", but the tests contain no stored AMT or MATLAB reference outputs.

## Sources

- https://github.com/StefanoGiacomelli/torch_amt/blob/main/README.md
- https://github.com/StefanoGiacomelli/torch_amt/blob/main/docs/source/index.rst
- https://pypi.org/project/torch-amt/

# ZwickerLoudness.jl

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/zwickerloudness-jl.html

**Newly released project.** First registered in February 2026. Not yet seen to be widely used in the community. Check its validation before relying on it.

Julia package that computes ISO 532-1:2017 Zwicker loudness from one-third-octave band levels: the stationary method (clause 5) from 28 band levels and, since v0.3.0, the time-varying method (clause 6) with N5 and N10 from a band-level time series. It does not take audio; ZwickerLoudnessAudio.jl is its front end for waveforms.

- **Repository:** https://github.com/slink/ZwickerLoudness.jl
- **Language:** Julia
- **Kind:** Library/Toolbox (Functions to call from your own code: a Python package, a MATLAB toolbox, or a C, C++, C#, Rust or Julia library.)
- **Group:** newly released (First released less than about a year ago, and not yet seen to be widely used in the community.)
- **Licence:** MIT
- **Package:** Julia General `ZwickerLoudness` (https://juliahub.com/ui/Packages/General/ZwickerLoudness)
- **Install:** `using Pkg; Pkg.add("ZwickerLoudness")`
- **Latest release:** v0.3.0 (2026-09)
- **Last commit:** 2026-09-02 (active)
- **GitHub stars:** 4
- **Maintainers:** slink
- **AI assistance:** not stated
- **How to cite:** The README links a [Zenodo DOI](https://zenodo.org/badge/latestdoi/1152458596) for the latest version. Name the version or commit you used.
- **Entry checked:** 2026-10-08

## What it implements

| Metric | Edition | Functions | Status | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Zwicker loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html) | [ISO 532-1:2017](https://www.iso.org/standard/63077.html) (stationary, from 28 one-third-octave band levels; since 0.2.0) | `zwicker_loudness` | available | standard or paper data (one Annex B signal); also compared with MoSQITo | — |
| [Zwicker loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html) | [ISO 532-1:2017](https://www.iso.org/standard/63077.html) (time-varying, from band levels at 2000 Hz; N5 and N10; since 0.3.0) | `zwicker_loudness_time_varying` | available | standard or paper data (one Annex B signal); also compared with MoSQITo (its source) | — |

## How it was validated

As reported by the project; LISQM has not run the code. Two implementations that agree can still share the same error.

- [Zwicker loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html), ISO 532-1:2017 (stationary, from 28 one-third-octave band levels): standard or paper data (one Annex B signal); also compared with **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)**
  - Checked against ISO 532-1 Annex B signal 1, the only 28-band reference in Annex B (83.296 sone, tolerance ±5 %).
  - Checked per Bark bin against MoSQITo output (maximum difference below 0.001 sone/Bark).
- [Zwicker loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html), ISO 532-1:2017 (time-varying, from band levels at 2000 Hz; N5 and N10): standard or paper data (one Annex B signal); also compared with **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)** (its source)
  - Ported or adapted from **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)**. It was compared with the code it was ported from, which checks the port only.
  - Stages are tested against MoSQITo `loudness_zwtv` intermediates (agreement about 1e-9 to 1e-15).
  - An Annex B.4 "Test signal 6" test regenerates band levels from a local MoSQITo checkout and is skipped when none is present; CI clones MoSQITo for it.
  - The ISO WAV files are not included.

## Notes

- Version 0.1.0 (February 2026) was described as "ISO 532B" and was never registered; the code was rewritten for ISO 532-1:2017 in 0.2.0, the first version in the Julia General registry (2026-02-11).
- The time-varying kernel takes a 28 × n matrix of band levels at the standard's 2000 Hz block rate. Its transcription reference is MoSQITo's `loudness_zwtv` at commit `d990c33f94f1`.
- Free-field and diffuse-field listening conditions are supported.

## Before you rely on it

- N5 and N10 use Hyndman–Fan type 7 quantiles; the README notes that MATLAB's `prctile` (type 5), used by SQAT, can differ by a few percent on the same data.

## Sources

- https://github.com/slink/ZwickerLoudness.jl
- https://github.com/slink/ZwickerLoudness.jl/blob/main/README.md
- https://github.com/slink/ZwickerLoudness.jl/blob/main/test/fixtures/NOTICE.md
- https://github.com/slink/ZwickerLoudness.jl/releases
- https://github.com/JuliaRegistries/General/tree/master/Z/ZwickerLoudness
- https://github.com/slink/ZwickerLoudness.jl/blob/main/src/method2.jl

# pySQAT

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/pysqat.html

Python port of the MATLAB toolbox SQAT (README title "SQAT4PY") with a PySide6 graphical interface. Covers ISO 532-1 loudness, DIN 45692 sharpness, Daniel & Weber roughness, Osses fluctuation strength, Aures tonality, three psychoacoustic annoyance models and EPNL; its ECMA-418-2 functions call sottek-hearing-model.

- **Repository:** https://github.com/PALILA-TUDelft/pySQAT
- **Language:** Python
- **Kind:** Library/Toolbox (Functions to call from your own code: a Python package, a MATLAB toolbox, or a C, C++, C#, Rust or Julia library.)
- **Group:** developing (Public for more than a year, but without a publication or documented use by others: research, teaching or personal code.)
- **Licence:** none — No licence file at the repository root. The bundled copy of SQAT v1.3 (MATLAB, used as the validation reference) carries SQAT's CC-BY-NC-4.0 licence.
- **Latest release:** no release
- **Last commit:** 2026-06-27 (active)
- **GitHub stars:** 5
- **Maintainers:** Gerard Mendoza Ferrandis
- **AI assistance:** not stated
- **How to cite:** The project does not say how to cite it. Cite the repository with the version or commit you used.
- **Entry checked:** 2026-10-07

## What it implements

| Metric | Edition | Functions | Status | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

## How it was validated

As reported by the project; LISQM has not run the code. Two implementations that agree can still share the same error.

- [Zwicker loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html), ISO 532-1:2017; [Sharpness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/sharpness.html), DIN 45692:2009; [Roughness (Daniel & Weber)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/roughness-daniel-weber.html), Daniel & Weber (1997); [Fluctuation strength (Osses et al.)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/fluctuation-strength-osses.html), Osses et al. (2016); [Tonality (Aures)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tonality-aures.html), Aures (1985b); [Psychoacoustic annoyance](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/psychoacoustic-annoyance.html), Di et al. (2016); [Psychoacoustic annoyance](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/psychoacoustic-annoyance.html), More (2010); [Psychoacoustic annoyance](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/psychoacoustic-annoyance.html), Zwicker & Fastl (1999); [Perceived noise level and EPNL](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/epnl.html), 14 CFR Part 36: compared with **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** (its source)
  - Ported or adapted from **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)**. It was compared with the code it was ported from, which checks the port only.
  - Compared with SQAT v1.3, run in MATLAB, by `validation/FINAL_VAL.py`; the generated reports are not committed.
- [Sottek Hearing Model loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-ecma-418-2.html), ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.); [Sottek Hearing Model roughness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/roughness-ecma-418-2.html), ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.); [Sottek Hearing Model tonality](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tonality-ecma-418-2.html), ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.): compared with **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** (also ported from [refmap-psychoacoustics](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/refmap-psychoacoustics.html))
  - Code ported from the same source is expected to agree, so that comparison is not an independent check.
  - Compared by `validation/FINAL_VAL.py` with the bundled SQAT v1.3 MATLAB code, which follows ECMA-418-2:2024 (3rd edition), so the comparison crosses editions.

## Notes

- Developed since May 2025 under the PALILA-TUDelft GitHub organisation; no release or tag yet.

## Before you rely on it

- Without a licence, reuse rights are unclear, and the bundled MATLAB code is licensed for non-commercial use only.
- The ports follow SQAT v1.3 and do not include SQAT's 2026 fixes to ISO 532-1 time-varying loudness, Daniel & Weber roughness and Aures tonality.

## Sources

- https://github.com/PALILA-TUDelft/pySQAT/blob/main/README.md
- https://github.com/PALILA-TUDelft/pySQAT/tree/main/validation
- https://github.com/PALILA-TUDelft/pySQAT/blob/main/validation/FINAL_VAL.py
- https://github.com/PALILA-TUDelft/pySQAT/issues/1

# LoudnessModel

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/loudnessmodel.html

Python translation of the Cambridge MATLAB code for the TVL2018 loudness model: Moore et al. (2016) with the revised time constants of Moore et al. (2018). Computes instantaneous, short-term and long-term loudness, in a NumPy version and a JAX version.

- **Repository:** https://github.com/MalcolmSlaney/LoudnessModel
- **Language:** Python
- **Kind:** Research code (Code published with a study, a thesis or a student project, to run or adapt; not packaged as a library.)
- **Group:** developing (Public for more than a year, but without a publication or documented use by others: research, teaching or personal code.)
- **Licence:** BSD-2-Clause — The README also says "The source code is provided free for any research purposes"; the readme of the Cambridge MATLAB code tv2018.m (see iso532-3) uses similar wording and asks commercial users to contact Brian C. J. Moore.
- **Latest release:** no release
- **Last commit:** 2025-03-20 (inactive since 2025-03)
- **GitHub stars:** 17
- **Maintainers:** Jeremy JX Hsiao, Malcolm Slaney
- **AI assistance:** not stated
- **How to cite:** The project does not say how to cite it. Cite the repository with the version or commit you used.
- **Entry checked:** 2026-10-06

## What it implements

| Metric | Edition | Functions | Status | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Time-varying loudness (Moore–Glasberg–Schlittenlacher)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg-time-varying.html) | [Moore et al. (2018)](https://doi.org/10.1121/1.5027246) (instantaneous, short-term and long-term loudness; binaural) | `tvl2018.compute_loudness`, `tvl2018_jax.compute_loudness` | available | own tests only | — |

## How it was validated

As reported by the project; LISQM has not run the code. Two implementations that agree can still share the same error.

- [Time-varying loudness (Moore–Glasberg–Schlittenlacher)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg-time-varying.html), Moore et al. (2018): own tests only
  - Ported or adapted from [iso532-3 (tv2018.m)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/js2251-iso532-3.html).
  - Tests run in GitHub Actions compare overall loudness, the first five short-term and long-term values and selected intermediate stages for one input (1 kHz tone, 100 ms, 32 kHz) with hard-coded expected values.
  - The README calls this "a known accurate output", but neither it nor the tests say where the values come from.

## Notes

- The README credits Brian C. J. Moore, Brian R. Glasberg and Josef Schlittenlacher for the MATLAB model and links the original MATLAB code (the first download on https://www.psychol.cam.ac.uk/hearing#programs). That page now needs a University of Cambridge login; an [archived copy](https://web.archive.org/web/20251123130736/https://www.psychol.cam.ac.uk/hearing) from November 2025 still links the code, an earlier version of the code in [iso532-3](https://github.com/js2251/iso532-3).
- The Python function names largely mirror the MATLAB files of tv2018 (see [iso532-3](https://github.com/js2251/iso532-3)), e.g. `agc_next_frame` for `AGCNextFrame.m`. ISO 532-3 is not mentioned in the repository.
- Outer- and middle-ear transfer functions for free-field, diffuse-field and eardrum presentation are included for 32 kHz.
- There is no packaging metadata (no pyproject.toml or setup.py) and no PyPI package; the README installs from a clone with requirements.txt. A Colab notebook with demos is linked.

## Before you rely on it

- The README says the JAX version "does not compile as there are several portions of the implementation that are not pure".

## Sources

- https://github.com/MalcolmSlaney/LoudnessModel
- https://github.com/MalcolmSlaney/LoudnessModel/blob/main/README.md
- https://github.com/MalcolmSlaney/LoudnessModel/blob/main/tvl2018_test.py
- https://github.com/MalcolmSlaney/LoudnessModel/blob/main/LICENSE
