# deeuu/loudness

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/deeuu-loudness.html

**Legacy project.** Not maintained. Its last commit was in August 2019, more than three years ago. Kept here for reference. Its code may follow an older edition and may not run with current software.

C++ library with SWIG Python bindings for building loudness models from cascaded processing modules. Includes Moore–Glasberg models for stationary sounds (ANSI S3.4-2007, Chen et al. 2011) and time-varying sounds (Glasberg & Moore 2002, Chen & Hu 2012), and stationary Zwicker loudness after DIN 45631:1991.

- **Repository:** https://github.com/deeuu/loudness
- **Language:** C++, Python
- **Kind:** Library/Toolbox (Functions to call from your own code: a Python package, a MATLAB toolbox, or a C, C++, C#, Rust or Julia library.)
- **Group:** legacy (Archived, or no commit for three years or more. Kept for reference. The code may follow an older edition and may not run with current software.)
- **Licence:** GPL-3.0-or-later
- **Latest release:** no release
- **Last commit:** 2019-08-08 (inactive since 2019-08)
- **GitHub stars:** 40
- **Maintainers:** Dominic Ward
- **AI assistance:** not stated
- **How to cite:** The project does not say how to cite it. Cite the repository with the version or commit you used.
- **Entry checked:** 2026-10-06

## What it implements

| Metric | Edition | Functions | Status | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Zwicker loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html) | [DIN 45631:1991](https://www.dinmedia.de/en/standard/din-45631/1666531) (stationary only) | `StationaryLoudnessDIN456311991` | available | compared with GENESIS ACOUSTICS code (Python port) | Uses 28 third-octave filters with third-order Butterworth responses after ANSI S1.11:1986; there is no time-varying (DIN 45631/A1) model. |
| [Moore–Glasberg loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg.html) | [Chen et al. (2011)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.heares.2011.08.001) | `StationaryLoudnessCHGM2011` | available | own tests only | — |
| [Moore–Glasberg loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg.html) | [ANSI/ASA S3.4-2007](https://webstore.ansi.org/standards/asa/ANSIASAS32007R2020) (with the binaural inhibition of Moore & Glasberg (2007) for two ears) | `StationaryLoudnessANSIS342007` | available | own tests only | — |
| [Time-varying loudness (Moore–Glasberg–Schlittenlacher)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg-time-varying.html) | [Glasberg & Moore (2002)](https://aes2.org/publications/elibrary-page/?id=11081) | `DynamicLoudnessGM2002` | available | own tests only | Per the header, excitation patterns follow ANSI S3.4-2007, and parameter sets use the modified long-term time constants of Moore et al. (2003) and the ANSI S3.4-2007 equation for specific loudness at high levels. |

## How it was validated

As reported by the project; LISQM has not run the code. Two implementations that agree can still share the same error.

- [Zwicker loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html), DIN 45631:1991: compared with GENESIS ACOUSTICS code (Python port)
  - Ported or adapted from BASIC program of DIN 45631 (Zwicker et al., 1991).
  - Tested against "a quick and dirty Python port of the Matlab code private by GENESIS ACOUSTICS".
- [Moore–Glasberg loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg.html), Chen et al. (2011); [Time-varying loudness (Moore–Glasberg–Schlittenlacher)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg-time-varying.html), Glasberg & Moore (2002): own tests only
- [Moore–Glasberg loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg.html), ANSI/ASA S3.4-2007: own tests only
  - Unit tests cover each module and model.
  - A validation script writes computed and expected loudness of pure tones to CSV; the expected values are labelled "Table 7" and "Example 2" without naming their source.

## Notes

- Also includes the dynamic loudness model of Chen & Hu (2012) (`DynamicLoudnessCH2012`) and partial-loudness stages after Moore, Glasberg & Baer (1997) and Chen et al. (2011) (`SpecificPartialLoudnessMGB1997`, `SpecificPartialLoudnessCHGM2011`); neither has an entry in this list.
- The interface is modelled on AIM-C. Building needs libsndfile, FFTW and zlib; the Python bindings need SWIG 3.
- The last commit touching the source code, bindings or Python package was on 2017-06-01; the last commit (2019-08-08) updated the README.
- `swig/setup.py` names the Python package `loudness` 0.0.1, but it was never published on PyPI.

## Before you rely on it

- The README says "This project is still in heavy development so is not stable".
- The PyPI package named `loudness` is an unrelated LUFS (ITU-R BS.1770) project (iver56/loudness); this library has to be built from source.

## Sources

- https://github.com/deeuu/loudness
- https://github.com/deeuu/loudness/blob/master/README.md
- https://github.com/deeuu/loudness/tree/master/src/models
- https://github.com/deeuu/loudness/tree/master/python/tests
- https://pypi.org/project/loudness/

# HAW loudness tool

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/haw-specific-loudness.html

**Legacy project.** Not maintained. Its last commit was in December 2022, more than three years ago. Kept here for reference. Its code may follow an older edition and may not run with current software.

MATLAB tool with a graphical interface, from HAW Hamburg, that shows the specific loudness of time-varying sounds: a Moore–Glasberg front end on ERB bands with temporal processing after Glasberg & Moore (2002), Chalupper & Fastl (2002) or Baumgarte (2000). Written in 2007 for a diploma thesis and published on Zenodo in 2022.

- **Full name:** Specific loudness of time-varying sounds (MATLAB tool)
- **Repository:** https://zenodo.org/records/7361480
- **Homepage:** https://reposit.haw-hamburg.de/handle/20.500.12738/14892
- **Language:** MATLAB
- **Kind:** Application (A program to run, with a graphical or command-line interface; no programming needed.)
- **Group:** legacy (Archived, or no commit for three years or more. Kept for reference. The code may follow an older edition and may not run with current software.)
- **Licence:** CC-BY-4.0 — Licence of the HAW Hamburg repository record; the archive itself has no licence file.
- **Latest release:** 1 (2022-12)
- **Last commit:** 2022-12-16 (inactive since 2022-12)
- **Maintainers:** Christian Sabrautzky, Robert Mores
- **AI assistance:** not stated
- **Paper:** Sabrautzky, C. (2007). *Erweiterung eines Lautheitsmodells von Moore und Glasberg zur Berechnung der spezifischen Lautheit dynamischer Audiosignale* [Diploma thesis, HAW Hamburg].
- **How to cite:** Cite the paper above. Software DOI: [10.5281/zenodo.7361480](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.7361480). Name the version or commit you used.
- **Entry checked:** 2026-10-07

## What it implements

| Metric | Edition | Functions | Status | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Time-varying loudness (Moore–Glasberg–Schlittenlacher)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg-time-varying.html) | [Glasberg & Moore (2002)](https://aes2.org/publications/elibrary-page/?id=11081) (specific loudness over time on ERB bands; three temporal models) | `loud_gui`, `matlab_loud` | available | reference code: LOUDAES and TVL (Glasberg & Moore's programs) | — |

## How it was validated

As reported by the project; LISQM has not run the code. Two implementations that agree can still share the same error.

- [Time-varying loudness (Moore–Glasberg–Schlittenlacher)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg-time-varying.html), Glasberg & Moore (2002): reference code: LOUDAES and TVL (Glasberg & Moore's programs)
  - The thesis compares the total loudness of pure tones (30–100 dB) with LOUDAES, Glasberg & Moore's program for stationary sounds: mostly within 5 %, with larger deviations at low levels near 50 Hz and above 5 kHz (−9.3 % for 5 kHz at 30 dB).
  - For two equal-level tones at 1 and 2 kHz, the deviation from LOUDAES ranges from −4.4 % to +3.8 % with the Hann-window FFT and reaches +6.7 % with the Fourier-time transform.
  - For the stationary part of signals the thesis reports good agreement with TVL, Glasberg & Moore's program for time-varying sounds, without figures.

## Before you compare numbers

Implementations of the same metric can give different numbers without either being wrong. Check these choices first.

- Input must be sampled at 32 kHz; the reference level is entered as the sound pressure level of a full-scale sine.


## Notes

- Code by Christian Sabrautzky (2007, revision 0.7), with changes by Robert Mores (2013) and a playback toolbar by Nico Schäfer. The Zenodo record (2022-12-16) includes an English overview of the models and the German thesis.
- Offers free-field and diffuse-field outer-ear filters and three spectral analyses: FFT with a Blackman–Harris or Hann window, and a Fourier-time transform.

## Before you rely on it

- Not an implementation of ANSI S3.4-2007 or ISO 532-2/-3. It follows Glasberg & Moore (2002) with the constants A, α and E_THRQ read from published graphs and interpolated, and its Chalupper–Fastl and Baumgarte options apply those models' temporal processing to Moore–Glasberg specific loudness.

## Sources

- https://zenodo.org/records/7361480
- https://reposit.haw-hamburg.de/handle/20.500.12738/14892


---

# IoSR Matlab Toolbox

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/iosr-matlab-toolbox.html

**Legacy project.** Not maintained. Its last commit was in August 2017, more than three years ago. Kept here for reference. Its code may follow an older edition and may not run with current software.

General-purpose MATLAB toolbox from the Institute of Sound Recording (University of Surrey) for auditory modelling, signal processing, source separation, statistics and plotting. For this list it provides ISO 226:2003 equal-loudness contours; it has no loudness, sharpness or roughness models.

- **Repository:** https://github.com/IoSR-Surrey/MatlabToolbox
- **Language:** MATLAB
- **Kind:** Library/Toolbox (Functions to call from your own code: a Python package, a MATLAB toolbox, or a C, C++, C#, Rust or Julia library.)
- **Group:** legacy (Archived, or no commit for three years or more. Kept for reference. The code may follow an older edition and may not run with current software.)
- **Licence:** MIT
- **Latest release:** v2.8 (2017-06)
- **Last commit:** 2017-08-18 (inactive since 2017-08)
- **GitHub stars:** 133
- **Maintainers:** Christopher Hummersone
- **AI assistance:** not stated
- **How to cite:** The project does not say how to cite it. Cite the repository with the version or commit you used.
- **Entry checked:** 2026-10-06

## What it implements

| Metric | Edition | Functions | Status | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Equal-loudness contours](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/equal-loudness-contours.html) | [ISO 226:2003](https://www.iso.org/standard/34222.html) | `iosr.auditory.iso226` | available | not stated | — |

## How it was validated

As reported by the project; LISQM has not run the code. Two implementations that agree can still share the same error.

The project does not say how any of these were validated.

## Notes

- `iosr.auditory.loudWeight` returns loudness-weighting coefficients derived from the 65-phon ISO 226:2003 contour.
- The two functions are also published on MATLAB File Exchange, as submissions 50348 ("ISO 226:2003 Normal equal-loudness-level contours") and 50349 ("Loudness weighting coefficients").

## Before you rely on it

- ISO 226:2003 was withdrawn in 2023 and replaced by ISO 226:2023; the function follows the 2003 edition.
- No commits since August 2017.

## Sources

- https://github.com/IoSR-Surrey/MatlabToolbox
- https://github.com/IoSR-Surrey/MatlabToolbox/blob/master/README.md
- https://github.com/IoSR-Surrey/MatlabToolbox/blob/master/+iosr/+auditory/iso226.m
- https://github.com/IoSR-Surrey/MatlabToolbox/blob/master/+iosr/+auditory/loudWeight.m

# MoSQITo-FDP

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito-fdp.html

**Legacy project.** Archived by its authors; its last commit was in July 2021. Kept here for reference. Its code may follow an older edition and may not run with current software.

Archived Python snapshot of a MoSQITo fork made for a final-degree project. It adds the Sottek Hearing Model with specific and total loudness (ECMA-418-2, 1st edition) as a step towards hearing-model tonality, and contains tone-to-noise ratio and prominence ratio after ECMA-74 Annex D.

- **Repository:** https://github.com/djcaminero/MoSQITo-FDP
- **Language:** Python
- **Kind:** Research code (Code published with a study, a thesis or a student project, to run or adapt; not packaged as a library.)
- **Group:** legacy (Archived, or no commit for three years or more. Kept for reference. The code may follow an older edition and may not run with current software.)
- **Licence:** Apache-2.0
- **Latest release:** no release
- **Last commit:** 2021-07-05 (archived)
- **GitHub stars:** 2
- **Maintainers:** Daniel Jiménez-Caminero Costa
- **AI assistance:** not stated
- **How to cite:** The project does not say how to cite it. Cite the repository with the version or commit you used.
- **Entry checked:** 2026-10-08

## What it implements

| Metric | Edition | Functions | Status | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Sottek Hearing Model loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-ecma-418-2.html) | [ECMA-418-2:2020 (1st ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_1st_edition_december_2020.pdf) (hearing model with specific and total loudness) | `comp_loudness` | available | standard or paper data | Module `mosqito.functions.hearing_model`. Its author committed the same hearing model to MoSQITo on 2021-05-30, two weeks before this snapshot. |
| [Tone-to-noise ratio and prominence ratio](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tone-to-noise-prominence-ratio.html) | [ECMA-74:2019 (17th ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-74/) (Annex D) | `comp_tnr`, `comp_pr` | available | own tests only | — |

## How it was validated

As reported by the project; LISQM has not run the code. Two implementations that agree can still share the same error.

- [Sottek Hearing Model loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-ecma-418-2.html), ECMA-418-2:2020 (1st ed.): standard or paper data
  - Ported or adapted from **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)** (the author's own code).
  - Validation scripts compare the ear filter and model output with figures and values from ECMA-418-2 and ECMA-74 Annex F.
- [Tone-to-noise ratio and prominence ratio](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tone-to-noise-prominence-ratio.html), ECMA-74:2019 (17th ed.): own tests only
  - Ported or adapted from **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)**.
  - The README lists TNR/PR as available but not validated; the tests use synthetic tones in white noise.

## Notes

- Commits run from 2021-06-13 to 2021-07-05. The package inside is still named `mosqito`, and later work went into MoSQITo itself.
- The hearing-model code cites both ECMA-418-2 (1st edition, 2020) and ECMA-74 Annex F (17th edition, 2019).
- Also contains the Zwicker loudness, DIN 45692 sharpness and Daniel & Weber roughness of the MoSQITo version it was forked from.

## Before you rely on it

- Archived snapshot without releases or maintenance.
- The README marks hearing-model tonality (ECMA-74:2019 Annex G) as under development; the repository contains the hearing-model stages, but no separate tonality function was found.

## Sources

- https://github.com/djcaminero/MoSQITo-FDP
- https://github.com/djcaminero/MoSQITo-FDP/blob/master/readme.md
- https://github.com/djcaminero/MoSQITo-FDP/tree/master/mosqito/functions/hearing_model
- https://github.com/djcaminero/MoSQITo-FDP/tree/master/mosqito/validations/hearing_model

# PsychoacousticParametersMeasurer

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psychoacoustic-parameters-measurer.html

**Legacy project.** Not maintained. Its last commit was in June 2021, more than three years ago. Kept here for reference. Its code may follow an older edition and may not run with current software.

Python scripts, commented in Spanish, that translate psychoacoustic parameters described in Zwicker and Fastl's book: Zwicker loudness (stationary and time-varying, from third-octave levels), sharpness, roughness, fluctuation strength and psychoacoustic annoyance.

- **Repository:** https://github.com/AndreaCastiella/PsychoacousticParametersMeasurer
- **Language:** Python
- **Kind:** Research code (Code published with a study, a thesis or a student project, to run or adapt; not packaged as a library.)
- **Group:** legacy (Archived, or no commit for three years or more. Kept for reference. The code may follow an older edition and may not run with current software.)
- **Licence:** none
- **Latest release:** no release
- **Last commit:** 2021-06-06 (inactive since 2021-06)
- **GitHub stars:** 13
- **Maintainers:** Andrea Castiella Aguirrezabala
- **AI assistance:** not stated
- **How to cite:** The project does not say how to cite it. Cite the repository with the version or commit you used.
- **Entry checked:** 2026-10-06

## What it implements

| Metric | Edition | Functions | Status | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Zwicker loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html) | [ISO 532-1:2017](https://www.iso.org/standard/63077.html) (stationary and time-varying, from third-octave levels) | `loudness_ISO532`, `loudness_ISO532_time` | available | not stated | The file header says "Loudness ISO 532-1:2014" and the filter coefficients are labelled "ISO 532-1:2014"; the published edition is ISO 532-1:2017. |
| [Sharpness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/sharpness.html) | [DIN 45692:2009](https://www.dinmedia.de/en/standard/din-45692/117635111) | `calc_sharpness` | available | not stated | The file header says "Sharpness DIN 45692"; the function also returns the von Bismarck and Aures variants. |
| [Fluctuation strength (Osses et al.)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/fluctuation-strength-osses.html) | [Fastl & Zwicker (2007)](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-540-68888-4) (Zwicker & Fastl formula) | `acousticFluctuation`, `fmoddetection` | available | not stated | The header cites Zwicker & Fastl, "Psychoacoustics: Facts and Models", without naming an edition. |
| [Psychoacoustic annoyance](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/psychoacoustic-annoyance.html) | [Zwicker & Fastl (1999)](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-662-09562-1) | `psychoacousticAnnoyance` | available | not stated | The header cites Zwicker & Fastl, "Psychoacoustics: Facts and Models", without naming an edition. |

## How it was validated

As reported by the project; LISQM has not run the code. Two implementations that agree can still share the same error.

The project does not say how any of these were validated.

## Notes

- There is no README. The GitHub description calls the project "the translation to python of the most important parameters in the field of Psychoacoustics based on the book of Zwicker and Fastl".
- Roughness (`acousticRoughness`) follows the formula in Zwicker & Fastl's book, which is not one of the roughness metrics in this list.
- Also contains A-weighting, voice-activity detection and the scripts Main.py and Main_WAV.py for microphone or WAV input.

## Before you rely on it

- No licence file, so reuse is not permitted by default.
- No documentation and no stated validation.

## Sources

- https://github.com/AndreaCastiella/PsychoacousticParametersMeasurer/blob/main/Sharpness.py
- https://github.com/AndreaCastiella/PsychoacousticParametersMeasurer/blob/main/FluctuationStrength.py
- https://github.com/AndreaCastiella/PsychoacousticParametersMeasurer/blob/main/PsychoacousticAnnoyance.py

# PsySound3

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psysound3.html

**Legacy project.** Not maintained. Its last commit was in March 2015, more than three years ago. Kept here for reference. Its code may follow an older edition and may not run with current software.

MATLAB program with a graphical interface for analysing sound recordings. Its analysers include the Chalupper–Fastl dynamic loudness model, Moore–Glasberg–Baer loudness and Daniel & Weber roughness.

- **Repository:** https://github.com/densilcabrera/psysound3
- **Language:** MATLAB
- **Kind:** Application (A program to run, with a graphical or command-line interface; no programming needed.)
- **Group:** legacy (Archived, or no commit for three years or more. Kept for reference. The code may follow an older edition and may not run with current software.)
- **Licence:** none — The repository has no licence file, only a no-warranty disclaimer (README-NO_WARRANTY). The licence of the original Google Code project was not checked.
- **Latest release:** no release
- **Last commit:** 2015-03-28 (inactive since 2015-03)
- **GitHub stars:** 17
- **Maintainers:** Densil Cabrera, Samuel Ferguson
- **AI assistance:** not stated
- **Paper:** PsySound3: a program for the analysis of sound recordings (2008). Acoustics'08 abstract, *The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America*, 123(5_Supplement), 3247. https://pubs.aip.org/asa/jasa/article/123/5_Supplement/3247/712568/
- **How to cite:** Cite the paper above. Name the version or commit you used.
- **Entry checked:** 2026-10-06

## What it implements

| Metric | Edition | Functions | Status | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Zwicker loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html) | [Chalupper & Fastl (2002)](https://www.ingentaconnect.com/contentone/dav/aaua/2002/00000088/00000003/art00009) (time-varying) | `@LoudnessCF` | available | not stated | The analyser names J. Chalupper and H. Fastl as authors. |
| [Moore–Glasberg loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg.html) | [Moore, Glasberg & Baer (1997)](https://aes2.org/publications/elibrary-page/?id=10272) | `@LoudnessMGB` | available | not stated | Also cites Glasberg & Moore (1990) for the auditory filters. The analyser description says it covers time-varying and binaural loudness, and it also cites Glasberg & Moore (2002) and Moore & Glasberg (2007). |
| [Time-varying loudness (Moore–Glasberg–Schlittenlacher)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg-time-varying.html) | [Glasberg & Moore (2002)](https://aes2.org/publications/elibrary-page/?id=11081) (time-varying and binaural) | `@LoudnessMGB` | available | not stated | The same analyser as the stationary entry; its description cites Glasberg & Moore (2002). |
| [Roughness (Daniel & Weber)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/roughness-daniel-weber.html) | [Daniel & Weber (1997)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/standards.html#ref-daniel-weber-1997) | `@RoughnessDW` | available | not stated | Adapted for PsySound3 by Matt Flax (2006), with changes by Farhan Rizwi (2007). AARAE's `RoughnessDW.m` is a port of this analyser. |

## How it was validated

As reported by the project; LISQM has not run the code. Two implementations that agree can still share the same error.

The project does not say how any of these were validated.

## Notes

- The GitHub repository is an automatic export of the Google Code project `psysound3`; its commits run from January 2009 to March 2015. It also bundles MIRtoolbox functions.
- `@LoudnessMG` computes loudness with a "Moore et al. static model" adapted from PsySound2; the model version is not stated.
- Search results describe PsySound3 as also covering sharpness and fluctuation strength. In this mirror, the descriptions of `@LoudnessCF` and `@LoudnessMG` list sharpness among their outputs; a fluctuation-strength analyser was not confirmed.

## Before you rely on it

- `README-BUGSISSUES` lists open problems, including "Various Accuracy Bugs", "Calibration Problems" and "Revisit calibration modes".
- The project states no validation, and there have been no commits since March 2015.
- With no licence file, the terms for reuse and redistribution are unclear.

## Sources

- https://github.com/densilcabrera/psysound3
- https://github.com/densilcabrera/psysound3/blob/master/README-BUGSISSUES
- https://github.com/densilcabrera/psysound3/blob/master/README-NO_WARRANTY
- https://github.com/densilcabrera/psysound3/blob/master/AudioAnalysers/@LoudnessCF/getAuthors.m

# python-acoustics

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/python-acoustics.html

**Legacy project.** Archived by its authors; its last commit was in August 2023. Kept here for reference. Its code may follow an older edition and may not run with current software.

General Python library for acousticians, published on PyPI as `acoustics`. For this list it is relevant for its tonal audibility and tonal adjustment after ISO 1996-2:2007. Archived in February 2024 and continued as acoustic-toolbox.

- **Repository:** https://github.com/python-acoustics/python-acoustics
- **Documentation:** https://python-acoustics.github.io/python-acoustics/
- **Language:** Python
- **Kind:** Library/Toolbox (Functions to call from your own code: a Python package, a MATLAB toolbox, or a C, C++, C#, Rust or Julia library.)
- **Group:** legacy (Archived, or no commit for three years or more. Kept for reference. The code may follow an older edition and may not run with current software.)
- **Licence:** BSD-3-Clause
- **Package:** PyPI `acoustics` (https://pypi.org/project/acoustics/)
- **Install:** `pip install acoustics`
- **Latest release:** 0.2.6 (2022-07)
- **Last commit:** 2023-08-20 (archived)
- **GitHub stars:** 563
- **Maintainers:** Frederik Rietdijk
- **AI assistance:** not stated
- **How to cite:** The project does not say how to cite it. Cite the repository with the version or commit you used.
- **Entry checked:** 2026-10-08

## What it implements

| Metric | Edition | Functions | Status | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Tonal audibility (ISO 1996-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tonal-audibility-iso-1996-2.html) | [ISO 1996-2:2007](https://www.iso.org/standard/41860.html) (tonal audibility and tonal adjustment) | `Tonality`, `tonal_audibility`, `tonal_adjustment` | available | own tests only | Module `acoustics.standards.iso_1996_2_2007`. The `Tonality` docstring uses the title of Annex C ("Objective method for assessing the audibility of tones in noise"), though the code does not name the annex. |

## How it was validated

As reported by the project; LISQM has not run the code. Two implementations that agree can still share the same error.

- [Tonal audibility (ISO 1996-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tonal-audibility-iso-1996-2.html), ISO 1996-2:2007: own tests only
  - A test of the examples in the standard, using DELTA tone files, is commented out.

## Notes

- The successor is [acoustic-toolbox](https://github.com/Universite-Gustave-Eiffel/acoustic-toolbox), which continues the same code.
- It has no loudness, sharpness or roughness modules.

## Before you rely on it

- The repository was archived on 2024-02-07 and is read-only.
- A fix to the default window of the tonality code (2023-08-20) is on the default branch but not in the last PyPI release (0.2.6, July 2022).
- It follows ISO 1996-2:2007, which has been withdrawn; ISO 1996-2:2017 replaced its tonal audibility method with those of Annexes J and K.

# SUAVE

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/suave.html

**Legacy project.** Not maintained. Its last commit was in December 2022, more than three years ago. Kept here for reference. Its code may follow an older edition and may not run with current software.

Python environment for the multi-fidelity conceptual design of aircraft ("An Aerospace Vehicle Environment"). Its noise tools compute perceived noise level (PNL), tone-corrected PNL (PNLT) and effective perceived noise level (EPNL) from one-third-octave spectra.

- **Repository:** https://github.com/suavecode/SUAVE
- **Language:** Python
- **Kind:** Library/Toolbox (Functions to call from your own code: a Python package, a MATLAB toolbox, or a C, C++, C#, Rust or Julia library.)
- **Group:** legacy (Archived, or no commit for three years or more. Kept for reference. The code may follow an older edition and may not run with current software.)
- **Licence:** LGPL-2.1
- **Latest release:** 2.5.2 (2022-03)
- **Last commit:** 2022-12-23 (inactive since 2022-12)
- **GitHub stars:** 530
- **Maintainers:** SUAVE team (Stanford Aerospace Design Lab)
- **AI assistance:** not stated
- **How to cite:** The project does not say how to cite it. Cite the repository with the version or commit you used.
- **Entry checked:** 2026-10-06

## What it implements

| Metric | Edition | Functions | Status | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Perceived noise level and EPNL](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/epnl.html) | [ICAO Annex 16, Vol. I](https://store.icao.int/en/annex-16-environmental-protection-volume-i-aircraft-noise) (PNL, PNLT and EPNL; the code cites no edition) | `pnl_noise`, `noise_tone_correction`, `epnl_noise` | available | not stated | EPNL is computed from a PNLT time history. The noise tools cite neither ICAO Annex 16 nor 14 CFR Part 36, nor an edition; their docstrings give "Source: None". |

## How it was validated

As reported by the project; LISQM has not run the code. Two implementations that agree can still share the same error.

The project does not say how any of these were validated.

## Notes

- The noise tools are in `SUAVE/Methods/Noise/Fidelity_One/Noise_Tools`, written by C. Ilario (2015) and modified by E. Botero (2016). The same folder has SENEL, dBA and noise-certification-limit helpers.

## Before you rely on it

- Development appears to have stopped in 2022: the last release (2.5.2) is from March 2022 and the last commit from December 2022.
- No validation of the noise metrics is stated.

# Swift & Gee codes

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/rapid-loudness-sharpness.html

**Legacy project.** Not maintained. Its last commit was in January 2020, more than three years ago. Kept here for reference. Its code may follow an older edition and may not run with current software.

MATLAB code by S. Hales Swift (Brigham Young University) on MATLAB File Exchange for fast Moore–Glasberg loudness: ANSI S3.4-2007 stationary loudness and Glasberg & Moore (2002) time-varying loudness, each with the sharpness of Swift & Gee (2017), which is computed from Moore–Glasberg specific loudness.

- **Full name:** Codes for the rapid calculation of loudness and sharpness
- **Repository:** https://www.mathworks.com/matlabcentral/fileexchange/73808-codes-for-the-rapid-calculation-of-loudness-and-sharpness
- **Language:** MATLAB
- **Kind:** Research code (Code published with a study, a thesis or a student project, to run or adapt; not packaged as a library.)
- **Group:** legacy (Archived, or no commit for three years or more. Kept for reference. The code may follow an older edition and may not run with current software.)
- **Licence:** BSD-3-Clause — license.txt: Copyright (c) 2019, Stephen Hales Swift.
- **Package:** MATLAB File Exchange `73808` (https://www.mathworks.com/matlabcentral/fileexchange/73808-codes-for-the-rapid-calculation-of-loudness-and-sharpness)
- **Latest release:** 1.0.0 (2020-01)
- **Last commit:** 2020-01-24 (inactive since 2020-01)
- **Maintainers:** Stephen Hales Swift
- **AI assistance:** not stated
- **Paper:** Swift, S. H., & Gee, K. L. (2019). Techniques for the rapid calculation of the excitation pattern in the time varying extensions to ANSI S3.4-2007. *Proceedings of Meetings on Acoustics*, 36, 040002.
- **How to cite:** The File Exchange page asks for the paper above for the loudness code and for Swift & Gee (2017) for the sharpness code. Name the version or commit you used.
- **Entry checked:** 2026-10-07

## What it implements

| Metric | Edition | Functions | Status | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Moore–Glasberg loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg.html) | [ANSI/ASA S3.4-2007](https://webstore.ansi.org/standards/asa/ANSIASAS32007R2020) | `stationaryLoudness` | available | not stated | — |
| [Time-varying loudness (Moore–Glasberg–Schlittenlacher)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg-time-varying.html) | [Glasberg & Moore (2002)](https://aes2.org/publications/elibrary-page/?id=11081) | `Glasberg_loudness` | available | not stated | — |
| [Sharpness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/sharpness.html) | [Swift & Gee (2017)](https://doi.org/10.1121/1.5016193) (from Moore–Glasberg specific loudness, stationary and time-varying) | `stationaryLoudness`, `Glasberg_loudness` | available | not stated | — |

## How it was validated

As reported by the project; LISQM has not run the code. Two implementations that agree can still share the same error.

The project does not say how any of these were validated.

## Before you compare numbers

Implementations of the same metric can give different numbers without either being wrong. Check these choices first.

- The code works at 32 kHz; other rates are resampled with the Signal Processing Toolbox's `resample`.


## Notes

- Version 1.0.0 (2020-01-24) is the only update after the first upload (2019-12-31). There is no public commit history; the files can be read online on File Exchange without logging in.
- The sharpness code is by the authors of the sharpness model.

## Before you rely on it

- No validation is described.
- Without the Signal Processing Toolbox, the File Exchange page says a file from the Cambridge Hearing Group's website is needed; that page now needs a University of Cambridge login.

## Sources

- https://www.mathworks.com/matlabcentral/fileexchange/73808-codes-for-the-rapid-calculation-of-loudness-and-sharpness
- https://viewer.mathworks.com/addons/73808/latest
- https://doi.org/10.1121/1.5016193

# Zhen-Ni/epnl

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/zhen-ni-epnl.html

**Legacy project.** Not maintained. Its last commit was in July 2023, more than three years ago. Kept here for reference. Its code may follow an older edition and may not run with current software.

Small Rust crate that computes perceived noisiness (noy), perceived noise level (PNL) and tone-corrected perceived noise level (PNLT) from 24 one-third-octave band levels, citing ICAO Annex 16, Volume I, Appendix 2 in its code comments.

- **Repository:** https://github.com/Zhen-Ni/epnl
- **Language:** Rust
- **Kind:** Library/Toolbox (Functions to call from your own code: a Python package, a MATLAB toolbox, or a C, C++, C#, Rust or Julia library.)
- **Group:** legacy (Archived, or no commit for three years or more. Kept for reference. The code may follow an older edition and may not run with current software.)
- **Licence:** none
- **Latest release:** no release
- **Last commit:** 2023-07-10 (inactive since 2023-07)
- **GitHub stars:** 0
- **Maintainers:** Zhen-Ni
- **AI assistance:** not stated
- **How to cite:** The project does not say how to cite it. Cite the repository with the version or commit you used.
- **Entry checked:** 2026-10-06

## What it implements

| Metric | Edition | Functions | Status | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Perceived noise level and EPNL](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/epnl.html) | [ICAO Annex 16, Vol. I](https://store.icao.int/en/annex-16-environmental-protection-volume-i-aircraft-noise) (PNL and PNLT only; no duration correction to EPNL) | `SPL`, `Noy`, `PNL`, `PNLT` | available | not stated | Code comments cite "Annex 16 - Volume I, APP 2-16 / 2-17" and number the 24 bands "consistent with ICAO ANNEX 16". The quantities are Rust types converted into each other with `From`. |

## How it was validated

As reported by the project; LISQM has not run the code. Two implementations that agree can still share the same error.

The project does not say how any of these were validated.

## Notes

- The crate (version 0.1.0) has no README and is not published on crates.io; input.txt holds two example 24-band spectra.

## Before you rely on it

- The GitHub description reads "Calculate Effective Perceived Noise Level (EPNL) for aircrafts", but EPNL itself is not implemented: there is no time integration or duration correction.
- No licence file, so reuse is not permitted by default.

## Sources

- https://github.com/Zhen-Ni/epnl
- https://github.com/Zhen-Ni/epnl/blob/master/Cargo.toml
- https://github.com/Zhen-Ni/epnl/tree/master/src

# zwickerloudness

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/zwickerloudness-sourceforge.html

**Legacy project.** Not maintained. Its last commit was in June 2018, more than three years ago. Kept here for reference. Its code may follow an older edition and may not run with current software.

Console program in C, for BSD, Linux and Windows, that calculates the loudness of stationary sounds with Zwicker's method (ISO 532B / DIN 45631) from one-third-octave band levels. A companion tool analyses WAV files to produce those input files.

- **Full name:** Zwicker's Loudness Calculation SW + Tool (ISO 532B)
- **Repository:** https://sourceforge.net/projects/zwickerloudness/
- **Language:** C
- **Kind:** Application (A program to run, with a graphical or command-line interface; no programming needed.)
- **Group:** legacy (Archived, or no commit for three years or more. Kept for reference. The code may follow an older edition and may not run with current software.)
- **Licence:** GPL-2.0 — SourceForge lists "GNU General Public License version 2.0", but the license file in the release archive (loudness-020) has the author's own BSD-style terms, with a fourth clause: a significantly different project that reuses parts of the code must be open source as well and must reference the original code.
- **Latest release:** zwickerloudness-020 (2011-07)
- **Last commit:** 2018-06-05 (inactive since 2018-06)
- **Maintainers:** V. Portet
- **AI assistance:** not stated
- **How to cite:** The project does not say how to cite it. Cite the repository with the version or commit you used.
- **Entry checked:** 2026-10-08

## What it implements

| Metric | Edition | Functions | Status | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Zwicker loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html) | [DIN 45631:1991](https://www.dinmedia.de/en/standard/din-45631/1666531) (stationary, from one-third-octave band levels) | — | available | own tests only | Port of the 1991 BASIC program "according to DIN 45631 (ISO 532B)", the program that accompanies DIN 45631:1991; the same program is the basis of deeuu/loudness. |

## How it was validated

As reported by the project; LISQM has not run the code. Two implementations that agree can still share the same error.

- [Zwicker loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html), DIN 45631:1991: own tests only
  - Ported or adapted from BASIC program of DIN 45631 (Zwicker et al., 1991).
  - The documentation in the release archive says that tests with "classical cases", such as the included test WAV files, "seems to give correct results", and invites users to compare the output with that of the original BASIC program.

## Notes

- Partly ported from the BASIC "Program for calculating loudness according to DIN 45631 (ISO 532B)", published in the Journal of the Acoustical Society of Japan in 1991, as obtained from Osaka University's website.
- Distributed as release archives on SourceForge, from release 010 (2010-04-15) to zwickerloudness-020 (2011-07-01). The last-commit date given here (2018-06-05) is the project's "Last Update" date on SourceForge, not a commit date.

## Before you rely on it

- Stationary sounds only; there is no procedure for time-varying sounds.

## Sources

- https://sourceforge.net/projects/zwickerloudness/
- https://sourceforge.net/projects/zwickerloudness/files/
- https://sourceforge.net/projects/zwickerloudness/files/README.TXT/download
- https://sourceforge.net/projects/zwickerloudness/files/zwickerloudness-020/loudness-020.tar.gz/download

# PsychoBox

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psychobox.html

Desktop application (PySide6 GUI) for playing, editing, filtering and analysing audio. Its psychoacoustic metrics are computed by MoSQITo 1.2.1: Zwicker loudness, ECMA-418-2 loudness, DIN 45692 sharpness, Daniel & Weber roughness and ECMA-418-2 roughness.

- **Repository:** https://github.com/henriquealende/PsychoBox
- **Documentation:** https://github.com/henriquealende/PsychoBox/tree/main/Documentation
- **Language:** Python
- **Kind:** Application (A program to run, with a graphical or command-line interface; no programming needed.)
- **Group:** other (Tools that do not compute the metrics themselves: interfaces, front ends and wrappers that call one of the listed projects.)
- **Licence:** MIT
- **Latest release:** no release
- **Last commit:** 2026-03-16 (active)
- **GitHub stars:** 10
- **AI assistance:** not stated
- **How to cite:** The project does not say how to cite it. Cite the repository with the version or commit you used.
- **Entry checked:** 2026-10-06

## What it implements

| Metric | Edition | Functions | Status | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Zwicker loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html) | [ISO 532-1:2017](https://www.iso.org/standard/63077.html) (stationary) | `Loudness.loudnessZWK` | available | not stated | Calls `loudness_zwst` of MoSQITo 1.2.1. |
| [Sottek Hearing Model loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-ecma-418-2.html) | [ECMA-418-2:2022 (2nd ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_2nd_edition_december_2022.pdf) (Clause 5 hearing-model loudness only) | `Loudness.loudnessECMA` | available | not stated | Calls `loudness_ecma` of MoSQITo 1.2.1 (ECMA-418-2:2022, Clause 5 only). |
| [Sharpness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/sharpness.html) | [DIN 45692:2009](https://www.dinmedia.de/en/standard/din-45692/117635111) | `Sharpnes_DIN.sharpnessCalculation` | available | not stated | Calls `sharpness_din_st` of MoSQITo 1.2.1 with the DIN weighting. |
| [Roughness (Daniel & Weber)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/roughness-daniel-weber.html) | [Daniel & Weber (1997)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/standards.html#ref-daniel-weber-1997) | `Roughness.roughnessDW` | available | not stated | Calls `roughness_dw` of MoSQITo 1.2.1. |
| [Sottek Hearing Model roughness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/roughness-ecma-418-2.html) | [ECMA-418-2:2022 (2nd ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_2nd_edition_december_2022.pdf) | `Roughness.roughnessECMA` | available | not stated | Calls `roughness_ecma` of MoSQITo 1.2.1, whose bibliography cites ECMA-418-2:2022. |

## How it was validated

As reported by the project; LISQM has not run the code. Two implementations that agree can still share the same error.

The project does not say how any of these were validated.

## Notes

- `requirements.txt` pins `mosqito==1.2.1`; PsychoBox itself states no standard editions.
- Also does recording and binaural playback correction. An install guide and a tutorial (PDF) are in the Documentation folder.
- Listed as an end-user application, although its metric values come from MoSQITo. Wrappers that are neither an application nor an established library are recorded in `data/ignored.yaml` instead.

## Before you rely on it

- All metric values come from MoSQITo 1.2.1, whose ECMA-418-2 functions follow the 2nd edition (2022), two editions behind the current one.

## Sources

- https://github.com/henriquealende/PsychoBox
- https://github.com/henriquealende/PsychoBox/blob/main/README.md
- https://github.com/henriquealende/PsychoBox/blob/main/requirements.txt
- https://github.com/henriquealende/PsychoBox/tree/main/Psychoacoustics
- https://github.com/Eomys/MoSQITo/blob/master/docs/ref.bib

# Soundscapy

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/soundscapy.html

Python library for soundscape assessment. Its optional audio module computes psychoacoustic metrics of binaural recordings, per channel, by calling MoSQITo: time-varying Zwicker loudness, DIN 45692 sharpness and Daniel & Weber roughness.

- **Repository:** https://github.com/MitchellAcoustics/Soundscapy
- **Documentation:** https://soundscapy.readthedocs.io/en/latest/
- **Language:** Python
- **Kind:** Library/Toolbox (Functions to call from your own code: a Python package, a MATLAB toolbox, or a C, C++, C#, Rust or Julia library.)
- **Group:** other (Tools that do not compute the metrics themselves: interfaces, front ends and wrappers that call one of the listed projects.)
- **Licence:** BSD-3-Clause
- **Package:** PyPI `soundscapy` (https://pypi.org/project/soundscapy/)
- **Install:** `pip install "soundscapy[audio]"`
- **Latest release:** v0.8.5 (2026-05)
- **Last commit:** 2026-05-14 (active)
- **GitHub stars:** 59
- **Maintainers:** Andrew Mitchell
- **AI assistance:** disclosed — Commit metadata only; the README does not mention AI. At least 31 commits from March to May 2026 carry co-author lines for Claude or Copilot, and eight commits are authored by copilot-swe-agent[bot].
- **Paper:** Mitchell, A., Aletta, F., & Kang, J. (2022). How to analyse and represent quantitative soundscape data. *JASA Express Letters*, 2, 037201. https://doi.org/10.1121/10.0009794
- **How to cite:** Cite the paper above. The repository has a [CITATION.cff](https://github.com/MitchellAcoustics/Soundscapy/blob/main/CITATION.cff) file. Name the version or commit you used.
- **Entry checked:** 2026-10-06

## What it implements

| Metric | Edition | Functions | Status | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Zwicker loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html) | [ISO 532-1:2017](https://www.iso.org/standard/63077.html) (time-varying, per channel) | `Binaural.mosqito_metric`, `process_all_metrics` | available | not stated | Calls `loudness_zwtv`. |
| [Sharpness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/sharpness.html) | [DIN 45692:2009](https://www.dinmedia.de/en/standard/din-45692/117635111) | `Binaural.mosqito_metric`, `process_all_metrics` | available | not stated | Calls `sharpness_din_from_loudness`, `sharpness_din_perseg` or `sharpness_din_tv`; the weighting can be chosen. |
| [Roughness (Daniel & Weber)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/roughness-daniel-weber.html) | [Daniel & Weber (1997)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/standards.html#ref-daniel-weber-1997) | `Binaural.mosqito_metric`, `process_all_metrics` | available | not stated | Calls `roughness_dw`. |

## How it was validated

As reported by the project; LISQM has not run the code. Two implementations that agree can still share the same error.

The project does not say how any of these were validated.

## Notes

- The psychoacoustic functions need the optional `audio` extra (MoSQITo 1.2.1 or newer). Environmental acoustic metrics come from acoustic-toolbox and ecoacoustic indices from scikit-maad.
- Issue [#123](https://github.com/MitchellAcoustics/Soundscapy/issues/123), open since 2025-10-29, plans to integrate sottek-hearing-model for ECMA-418-2 metrics; its branch has no such code yet.
- The paper the README asks users to cite covers soundscape data analysis, not the psychoacoustic functions.

## Before you rely on it

- The psychoacoustic values are computed by MoSQITo, so their editions and accuracy are those of the installed MoSQITo version.

## Sources

- https://github.com/MitchellAcoustics/Soundscapy
- https://github.com/MitchellAcoustics/Soundscapy/blob/main/README.md
- https://github.com/MitchellAcoustics/Soundscapy/blob/main/src/soundscapy/audio/metrics.py
- https://github.com/MitchellAcoustics/Soundscapy/issues/123
- https://pypi.org/project/soundscapy/

# ZwickerLoudnessAudio.jl

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/zwickerloudnessaudio-jl.html

**Newly released project.** First registered in June 2026. Not yet seen to be widely used in the community. Check its validation before relying on it.

Julia front end to ZwickerLoudness.jl that computes ISO 532-1:2017 Zwicker loudness from waveforms or WAV files: stationary loudness, and since v0.3.0 time-varying loudness with N5 and N10.

- **Repository:** https://github.com/slink/ZwickerLoudnessAudio.jl
- **Language:** Julia
- **Kind:** Library/Toolbox (Functions to call from your own code: a Python package, a MATLAB toolbox, or a C, C++, C#, Rust or Julia library.)
- **Group:** other (Tools that do not compute the metrics themselves: interfaces, front ends and wrappers that call one of the listed projects.)
- **Licence:** MIT — The README credits MoSQITo (Apache-2.0) for the transcribed time-varying filter tables.
- **Package:** Julia General `ZwickerLoudnessAudio` (https://juliahub.com/ui/Packages/General/ZwickerLoudnessAudio)
- **Install:** `using Pkg; Pkg.add("ZwickerLoudnessAudio")`
- **Latest release:** v0.3.0 (2026-09)
- **Last commit:** 2026-09-02 (active)
- **GitHub stars:** 2
- **Maintainers:** slink
- **AI assistance:** not stated
- **How to cite:** The README links a [Zenodo DOI](https://zenodo.org/badge/latestdoi/1253784080) for the latest version. Name the version or commit you used.
- **Entry checked:** 2026-10-06

## What it implements

| Metric | Edition | Functions | Status | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Zwicker loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html) | [ISO 532-1:2017](https://www.iso.org/standard/63077.html) (stationary, from a waveform or WAV file; since 0.2.0) | `loudness_zwst`, `band_levels` | available | standard or paper data | Computes the third-octave levels itself (per-band Butterworth filters of order 3 by default, as in MoSQITo) and passes them to ZwickerLoudness.jl for the loudness. |
| [Zwicker loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html) | [ISO 532-1:2017](https://www.iso.org/standard/63077.html) (time-varying, from a waveform or WAV file at 48 kHz; since 0.3.0) | `loudness_zwtv` | available | standard or paper data; also compared with MoSQITo (its source) | The Annex A filter cascade is transcribed from MoSQITo (`_third_octave_levels`, `_square_and_smooth`). |

## How it was validated

As reported by the project; LISQM has not run the code. Two implementations that agree can still share the same error.

- [Zwicker loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html), ISO 532-1:2017 (stationary, from a waveform or WAV file): standard or paper data
  - ISO 532-1 Annex B signals 2–5, synthesised in-process, are within the standard's ±5 % (+2.9 %, +3.6 %, +0.5 % and +2.6 % per the README).
- [Zwicker loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html), ISO 532-1:2017 (time-varying, from a waveform or WAV file at 48 kHz): standard or paper data; also compared with **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)** (its source)
  - Ported or adapted from **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)**. It was compared with the code it was ported from, which checks the port only.
  - Cross-checked end to end with MoSQITo `loudness_zwtv` (N(t) about 3e-16 relative, N5/N10 about 2e-15 absolute).
  - An Annex B.4 test is skipped when the ISO recording is not available locally.

## Before you compare numbers

Implementations of the same metric can give different numbers without either being wrong. Check these choices first.

- [Zwicker loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html) (ISO 532-1:2017): Stationary loudness resamples input below 48 kHz to 48 kHz (polyphase), with a warning.
- [Zwicker loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html) (ISO 532-1:2017): Time-varying loudness accepts 48 kHz input only (an error otherwise).

## Notes

- Depends on ZwickerLoudness.jl (compat 0.3), which does the loudness calculation from band levels; this package computes the band levels.
- First registered in the Julia General registry as version 0.2.0 (2026-06-01).

## Sources

- https://github.com/slink/ZwickerLoudnessAudio.jl
- https://github.com/slink/ZwickerLoudnessAudio.jl/blob/main/README.md
- https://github.com/slink/ZwickerLoudnessAudio.jl/releases
- https://github.com/JuliaRegistries/General/tree/master/Z/ZwickerLoudnessAudio

# PsyTools

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psytools.html

**Status unknown.** The repository cannot be opened without a login. It redirects to the TU Graz GitLab login page, while the author's profile page on the same server is public (checked 2026-10-07). What it implements has not been verified, so it is not listed under the metrics.

Python toolbox for psychoacoustic analysis from TU Graz, described in a 2026 student conference paper.

- **Repository:** https://gitlab.tugraz.at/11F34386B3DC1474/psytools
- **Language:** Python
- **Kind:** Library/Toolbox (Functions to call from your own code: a Python package, a MATLAB toolbox, or a C, C++, C#, Rust or Julia library.)
- **Group:** status unknown (Projects whose code could not be opened, for example because the repository needs a login. What they implement is unverified, so they are listed with what they claim and not under the metrics.)
- **Licence:** unknown
- **Latest release:** unknown
- **Last commit:** unknown (unknown)
- **Maintainers:** Eugen-Maximilian Stangl, Julia Donnerer
- **AI assistance:** not stated
- **Paper:** Stangl, E.-M., & Donnerer, J. (2026). PsyTools: An open-source Python toolbox for standardized psychoacoustic analysis. *POSTERS 2026: Proceedings of the International Student Scientific Conference Poster*, Czech Technical University in Prague, 172–173. https://tugraz.elsevierpure.com/en/publications/psytools-an-open-source-python-toolbox-for-standardized-psychoaco/
- **How to cite:** Cite the paper above. Name the version or commit you used.
- **Entry checked:** 2026-10-07

## What it is said to implement

A conference paper describes an open-source Python toolbox for standardised psychoacoustic analysis: loudness, sharpness, fluctuation strength, roughness, tonality, psychoacoustic annoyance, LAeq and LAmax, following ISO 532-1, DIN 45692 and ECMA-418, with the Zwicker model and the Sottek Hearing Model.

As described in the sources below; the code itself could not be checked.

## Sources

- https://tugraz.elsevierpure.com/en/publications/psytools-an-open-source-python-toolbox-for-standardized-psychoaco/
- https://gitlab.tugraz.at/11F34386B3DC1474/psytools

# Project map

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/map.html

Each line of the map joins two projects: code ported or adapted from another project, the author's own code moved between projects, a project that uses another one at run time, results checked against another project, or a shared contributor. The lines come from the implementation rows on the project pages. On the web page, arrows point from the source to the project that uses it, and a check points from the project to the one it checked its results against.

## Kinds of line

- **Ported or adapted from another project.** The project's code for a metric was ported from the source (translated into another language) or adapted from it (reused with changes), or the whole project continues the source. A grey box is a program published with a standard or a paper.
- **The author's own code.** The code was written by someone who also maintains the project that ported or adapted it: a contribution, a move or a translation within the same team, not a port by someone else.
- **Used at run time.** The project calls the source to compute the metric, or needs its results as input.
- **Results checked against.** The arrow points from the project to the one it checked its results against. Comparisons with the code a project was ported or adapted from, with a port of its own code or with another port of the same code are not drawn, because they only show that two versions of the same code agree.
- **Same contributor.** Someone has worked on both projects, as a maintainer or with code of their own. Not drawn beside a line of the author's own code, which says the same.

## Ported or adapted from another project

- From [AARAE](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/aarae.html): **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** (Zwicker loudness and Roughness (Daniel & Weber))
- From BASIC program of DIN 45631 (Zwicker et al., 1991): **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)** (Zwicker loudness); [ITA-Toolbox](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/ita-toolbox.html) (Zwicker loudness); [deeuu/loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/deeuu-loudness.html) (Zwicker loudness); [zwickerloudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/zwickerloudness-sourceforge.html) (Zwicker loudness)
- From [python-acoustics](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/python-acoustics.html): [acoustic-toolbox](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/acoustic-toolbox.html) (Tonal audibility (ISO 1996-2))
- From ISO 532-1 Annex A reference program: [AARAE](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/aarae.html) (Zwicker loudness); [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html) (Zwicker loudness)
- From **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)**: [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/metasona.html) (Zwicker loudness and Roughness (Daniel & Weber)); [Kirin Hypha](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/kirin-hypha.html) (Zwicker loudness and Sharpness); [Mosqito.NET](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito-net.html) (Zwicker loudness, Sottek Hearing Model loudness, Sharpness, Roughness (Daniel & Weber), Sottek Hearing Model roughness, Tone-to-noise ratio and prominence ratio, and Equal-loudness contours); [PsychoacousticMetrics.jl](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psychoacousticmetrics-jl.html) (Roughness (Daniel & Weber)); [ZwickerLoudness.jl](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/zwickerloudness-jl.html) (Zwicker loudness); [MoSQITo-FDP](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito-fdp.html) (Sottek Hearing Model loudness and Tone-to-noise ratio and prominence ratio); [ZwickerLoudnessAudio.jl](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/zwickerloudnessaudio-jl.html) (Zwicker loudness)
- From **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)**: [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/metasona.html) (Zwicker loudness, Sottek Hearing Model loudness, Roughness (Daniel & Weber), Sottek Hearing Model roughness, Tonality (Aures), and Sottek Hearing Model tonality); [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/pysqat.html) (Zwicker loudness, Sharpness, Roughness (Daniel & Weber), Fluctuation strength (Osses et al.), Tonality (Aures), Psychoacoustic annoyance, and Perceived noise level and EPNL)
- From [AMT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/amt.html): [NumpyLibforPsychoAcoustic](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/numpylib-psychoacoustic.html) (Moore–Glasberg loudness and Time-varying loudness (Moore–Glasberg–Schlittenlacher)); [torch_amt](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/torch-amt.html) (Time-varying loudness (Moore–Glasberg–Schlittenlacher))
- From [iso532-3 (tv2018.m)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/js2251-iso532-3.html): [LoudnessModel](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/loudnessmodel.html) (Time-varying loudness (Moore–Glasberg–Schlittenlacher))

## The author's own code

- From [refmap-psychoacoustics](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/refmap-psychoacoustics.html) (Mike Lotinga): **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** (Sottek Hearing Model loudness, Sottek Hearing Model roughness, and Sottek Hearing Model tonality); **[sottek-hearing-model](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sottek-hearing-model.html)** (Sottek Hearing Model loudness, Sottek Hearing Model roughness, Sottek Hearing Model fluctuation strength, and Sottek Hearing Model tonality)
- From [fluctuation-strength-TUe](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/fluctuation-strength-tue.html) (Alejandro Osses): **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** (Fluctuation strength (Osses et al.))
- From [PsySound3](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psysound3.html) (Densil Cabrera): [AARAE](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/aarae.html) (Zwicker loudness, Moore–Glasberg loudness, Time-varying loudness (Moore–Glasberg–Schlittenlacher), and Roughness (Daniel & Weber))

## Used at run time

- [PsychoacousticMetrics.jl](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psychoacousticmetrics-jl.html) needs [ZwickerLoudness.jl](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/zwickerloudness-jl.html) (Sharpness and Psychoacoustic annoyance)
- [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/pysqat.html) calls **[sottek-hearing-model](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sottek-hearing-model.html)** (Sottek Hearing Model loudness, Sottek Hearing Model roughness, and Sottek Hearing Model tonality)
- [PsychoBox](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psychobox.html) calls **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)** (Zwicker loudness, Sottek Hearing Model loudness, Sharpness, Roughness (Daniel & Weber), and Sottek Hearing Model roughness)
- [Soundscapy](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/soundscapy.html) calls **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)** (Zwicker loudness, Sharpness, and Roughness (Daniel & Weber))
- [ZwickerLoudnessAudio.jl](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/zwickerloudnessaudio-jl.html) calls [ZwickerLoudness.jl](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/zwickerloudness-jl.html) (Zwicker loudness)

## Results checked against another project

- [iso532-1-rs](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/iso532-1-rs.html) against **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)** (Zwicker loudness)
- [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/phonometry.html) against **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** (Fluctuation strength (Osses et al.))
- [PsychoacousticMetrics.jl](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psychoacousticmetrics-jl.html) against **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** (Fluctuation strength (Osses et al.) and Psychoacoustic annoyance)
- [SoundPalette](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/soundpalette.html) against **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)** (Zwicker loudness, Sharpness, and Roughness (Daniel & Weber))

## Same contributor

- **[SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sqat.html)** and **[sottek-hearing-model](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/sottek-hearing-model.html)** (Mike Lotinga)
- **[MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito.html)** and [MoSQITo-FDP](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/mosqito-fdp.html) (Daniel Jiménez-Caminero Costa)
- [acoustic-toolbox](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/acoustic-toolbox.html) and [Soundscapy](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/soundscapy.html) (Andrew Mitchell)
- [PsychoacousticMetrics.jl](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psychoacousticmetrics-jl.html) and [ZwickerLoudness.jl](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/zwickerloudness-jl.html) (slink)
- [PsychoacousticMetrics.jl](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psychoacousticmetrics-jl.html) and [ZwickerLoudnessAudio.jl](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/zwickerloudnessaudio-jl.html) (slink)
- [ZwickerLoudness.jl](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/zwickerloudness-jl.html) and [ZwickerLoudnessAudio.jl](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/zwickerloudnessaudio-jl.html) (slink)

On the map without a line, as no relation is recorded for them: [PSYCHO](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/pd-psycho.html), [PyDSM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/pydsm.html), [HAW loudness tool](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/haw-specific-loudness.html), [IoSR Matlab Toolbox](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/iosr-matlab-toolbox.html), [PsychoacousticParametersMeasurer](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psychoacoustic-parameters-measurer.html), [SUAVE](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/suave.html), [Swift & Gee codes](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/rapid-loudness-sharpness.html), and [Zhen-Ni/epnl](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/zhen-ni-epnl.html).

Left out, as their code could not be opened: [PsyTools](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/projects/psytools.html).

# Standards and models

> Part of [LISQM](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/) (List of Implementations of Sound Quality Metrics), a list of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-09. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/standards.html

All documents the list refers to, newest first. Each implementation in the list is tied to one of these editions. They are also available as BibTeX, together with the papers that describe the listed software: https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/references.bib

## Standards and regulations

| Date | Document | Title | Status | Used by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-04 | [ISO/AWI 26573](https://www.iso.org/standard/93922.html) | Acoustics — Procedures for assessment and prediction of noise-induced perceptual annoyance through laboratory-based listening tests | in development | [Psychoacoustic annoyance](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/psychoacoustic-annoyance.html) |
| 2025-06 | [ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_4th_edition_june_2025.pdf) | Psychoacoustic metrics for ITT equipment — Part 2 (methods for describing human perception based on the Sottek Hearing Model) | current | [Sottek Hearing Model loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-ecma-418-2.html), [Sottek Hearing Model roughness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/roughness-ecma-418-2.html), [Sottek Hearing Model fluctuation strength](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/fluctuation-strength-ecma-418-2.html), [Sottek Hearing Model tonality](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tonality-ecma-418-2.html) |
| 2024-12 | [ECMA-418-2:2024 (3rd ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_3rd_edition_december_2024.pdf) | Psychoacoustic metrics for ITT equipment — Part 2 (methods for describing human perception based on the Sottek Hearing Model) | superseded | [Sottek Hearing Model loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-ecma-418-2.html), [Sottek Hearing Model roughness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/roughness-ecma-418-2.html), [Sottek Hearing Model tonality](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tonality-ecma-418-2.html) |
| 2024-12 | [ECMA-418-1:2024 (3rd ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-1_3rd_edition_december_2024.pdf) | Psychoacoustic metrics for ITT equipment — Part 1 (prominent discrete tones) | current | [Tone-to-noise ratio and prominence ratio](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tone-to-noise-prominence-ratio.html) |
| 2024-11 | [ISO/CD 532-3](https://www.iso.org/standard/90816.html) | Acoustics — Methods for calculating loudness — Part 3: Moore-Glasberg-Schlittenlacher method (2nd edition) | in development | [Time-varying loudness (Moore–Glasberg–Schlittenlacher)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg-time-varying.html) |

| 2024-11 | [DIN 38455:2024](https://www.dinmedia.de/en/standard/din-38455/376186532) | Berechnung der Hörempfindung Rauigkeit (Calculation of the auditory sensation of roughness) | current | [Roughness (DIN 38455)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/roughness-din-38455.html) |
| 2023-07 | [ISO 532-3:2023](https://www.iso.org/standard/69856.html) | Acoustics — Methods for calculating loudness — Part 3: Moore-Glasberg-Schlittenlacher method | current | [Time-varying loudness (Moore–Glasberg–Schlittenlacher)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg-time-varying.html) |
| 2023-03 | [ISO 226:2023](https://www.iso.org/standard/83117.html) | Acoustics — Normal equal-loudness-level contours | current | [Equal-loudness contours](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/equal-loudness-contours.html) |
| 2022-12 | [ISO/TS 20065:2022](https://www.iso.org/standard/81518.html) | Acoustics — Objective method for assessing the audibility of tones in noise — Engineering method | current | [Audibility of tones in noise (ISO/TS 20065)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tonal-audibility-iso-20065.html) |
| 2022-12 | [ECMA-418-2:2022 (2nd ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_2nd_edition_december_2022.pdf) | Psychoacoustic metrics for ITT equipment — Part 2 (models based on human perception) | superseded | [Sottek Hearing Model loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-ecma-418-2.html), [Sottek Hearing Model roughness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/roughness-ecma-418-2.html), [Sottek Hearing Model tonality](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tonality-ecma-418-2.html) |

|---|---|---|---|---|

| 2018 | [Moore et al. (2018)](https://doi.org/10.1121/1.5027246) | Testing and refining a loudness model for time-varying sounds incorporating binaural inhibition | published | [Time-varying loudness (Moore–Glasberg–Schlittenlacher)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg-time-varying.html) |

| 2016 | [Osses et al. (2016)](https://doi.org/10.1121/2.0000410) | Modelling the sensation of fluctuation strength | published | [Fluctuation strength (Osses et al.)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/fluctuation-strength-osses.html) |
| 2016 | [Moore et al. (2016)](https://doi.org/10.1177/2331216516682698) | A loudness model for time-varying sounds incorporating binaural inhibition | published | [Time-varying loudness (Moore–Glasberg–Schlittenlacher)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg-time-varying.html) |
| 2016 | [Di et al. (2016)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.apacoust.2015.12.006) | Improvement of Zwicker's psychoacoustic annoyance model aiming at tonal noises | published | [Psychoacoustic annoyance](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/psychoacoustic-annoyance.html) |
| 2011 | [Chen et al. (2011)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.heares.2011.08.001) | A new method of calculating auditory excitation patterns and loudness for steady sounds | published | [Moore–Glasberg loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg.html) |
| 2010 | [More (2010)](https://docs.lib.purdue.edu/dissertations/AAI3453255) | Aircraft noise characteristics and metrics | published | [Psychoacoustic annoyance](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/psychoacoustic-annoyance.html) |
| 2007 | [Fastl & Zwicker (2007)](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-540-68888-4) | Psychoacoustics: Facts and Models (3rd edition) | published | [Sharpness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/sharpness.html), [Fluctuation strength (Osses et al.)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/fluctuation-strength-osses.html) |
| 2002 | [Glasberg & Moore (2002)](https://aes2.org/publications/elibrary-page/?id=11081) | A model of loudness applicable to time-varying sounds | published | [Time-varying loudness (Moore–Glasberg–Schlittenlacher)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg-time-varying.html) |
| 2002 | [Chalupper & Fastl (2002)](https://www.ingentaconnect.com/contentone/dav/aaua/2002/00000088/00000003/art00009) | Dynamic loudness model (DLM) for normal and hearing-impaired listeners | published | [Zwicker loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html) |
| 1999 | [Zwicker & Fastl (1999)](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-662-09562-1) | Psychoacoustics: Facts and Models (2nd edition) | published | [Psychoacoustic annoyance](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/psychoacoustic-annoyance.html) |
| 1997 | [Moore, Glasberg & Baer (1997)](https://aes2.org/publications/elibrary-page/?id=10272) | A model for the prediction of thresholds, loudness, and partial loudness | published | [Moore–Glasberg loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg.html) |
| 1997 | Daniel & Weber (1997) | Psychoacoustical roughness: implementation of an optimized model | published | [Roughness (Daniel & Weber)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/roughness-daniel-weber.html) |
| 1992 | Widmann (1992) | Ein Modell der psychoakustischen Lästigkeit von Schallen und seine Anwendung in der Praxis der Lärmbeurteilung | published | [Psychoacoustic annoyance](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/psychoacoustic-annoyance.html) |
| 1985 | Aures (1985b) | Berechnungsverfahren für den sensorischen Wohlklang beliebiger Schallsignale | published | [Sharpness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/sharpness.html), [Tonality (Aures)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/LISQM/metrics/tonality-aures.html) |
